Mia saw many pretty colors and shapes on the tree. She saw a funny face too. "Hi, funny face!" Mia said. The funny face said, "Hi, Mia! I am Mr. Unusual. Do you like my wide tree?" Mia said, "Yes, I do! I like your tree and your display. Can I play with you?" Mr. Unusual said, "Of course, Mia! Let's play together and have fun!" So Mia and Mr. Unusual played under the wide tree all day.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Kitty and a little dog named Buddy. They lived in a small house with a girl named Sue. Sue loved to play with Kitty and Buddy, but sometimes they would quarrel. One day, Kitty and Buddy were playing with a ball. Kitty wanted to play with the ball, but Buddy wanted to play too. They began to quarrel. "Meow, it's my turn!" said Kitty. "Woof, no, it's my turn!" said Buddy. Sue heard the quarrel and came to help. She saw that Kitty had hurt her toe while playing. Sue picked up Kitty and gave her a hug. She told them, "No more quarrelling. Let's all play together." Kitty and Buddy agreed, and they all played happily ever after.

Once there was a little bear cub named Buzz who was very curious. One day Buzz saw a big oak tree in the forest. He wanted to explore the tree but his mom wouldn't allow it. Buzz said, "But Mom, I want to see what's in the tree!" His mom replied, "It's too dangerous. I won't allow it." But Buzz wasn't deterred. He was very curious and he knew there was something special inside the tree. So later that night, when he thought his mother wasn't paying attention, he sneaked back to the tree. And sure enough, there was something special inside - a big family of squirrels living in the top of the tree. Buzz was so excited by all the activities and noises the squirrels were making. He knew he had found something truly special. His mother was a bit angry when she found out, but she was also proud of Buzz for being so curious. She allowed him to go back to the tree again, but only if he promised to be careful.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Spot. He liked to play with his pen. Spot would protect his pen because it was his favorite toy. He would run, jump, and wag his tail when he played with it. Spot loved his pen very much. One day, Spot could not find his pen. He looked everywhere. He looked under the bed, behind the door, and in his toy box. Spot was sad. He missed his pen and wanted to protect it. As he was looking, he saw something behind the big tree in the yard. Spot ran to the tree and found a big, red ball. He was surprised! Spot played with the ball and had lots of fun. He forgot about his pen. He ran, jumped, and wagged his tail with the big, red ball. Spot was happy again. Later, Spot's friend, Max, came to play. Max had found Spot's pen! It was under the couch. Spot was so happy to see his pen again. He thanked Max and shared his new ball with him. Now, Spot had two toys to play and protect. Spot and Max played together all day long. They were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a thin cat. The cat liked to travel. One day, the cat went on a walk. The cat saw a fence. The fence was very tall. The cat wanted to see what was on the other side. The cat jumped over the fence. There were many friends to play with there. The cat was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had very long hair. One day, he decided he wanted a haircut. So, he went to his mom and said, "Mom, can I request a haircut, please?" His mom was glad to hear this. She took Tim to the hair-cutting place. The man at the hair-cutting place asked Tim, "How short do you want your hair?" Tim said, "I want it very short!" The man cut Tim's hair very short. Tim was very happy with his new haircut. His mom was happy too. They went home and showed Tim's dad. Tim's dad said, "Wow! You look great, Tim!" And they all lived happily ever after.

Tim and Mia went to the park with Mom. They saw many ducks in the pond. Tim and Mia liked the ducks. They wanted to feed them some bread. "Can we feed the ducks, Mom?" Tim asked. "Yes, but be polite and gentle. Don't throw the bread or scare the ducks," Mom said. Tim and Mia nodded. They broke the bread into small pieces and walked to the edge of the pond. They saw a big duck with a green head and a yellow beak. He looked hungry. "Hello, duck. Do you want some bread?" Mia said. The duck quacked and swam closer. Mia tossed a piece of bread to the duck. The duck caught it and ate it. He quacked again and wagged his tail. "Thank you, duck. You are very polite," Mia said. The duck nodded and smiled. He liked Mia. He wanted more bread. "Can I feed him too, Mia?" Tim said. "Sure, Tim. Here, take some bread," Mia said. Tim took some bread and threw it to the duck. The duck ate it and quacked. He liked Tim too. He wanted to be friends. "Thank you, Tim. You are very polite too," the duck said. Tim and Mia smiled. They clapped their hands and laughed. They were happy. They made a new friend. Mom watched them and smiled too. She was proud of Tim and Mia. They were polite and kind to the duck. She took a picture of them and the duck. She wanted to remember this day.

One day, a little boy named Tim saw gray clouds in the sky. He was playing outside with his toy car. Tim heard a loud noise and saw a bright lightning. He was scared and ran inside the house. Tim's mom saw him and asked, "Why did you come in, Tim?" Tim said, "Mom, I saw lightning and it was very loud!" His mom hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tim. Lightning can be scary, but we are safe inside the house." Later, the gray clouds went away and the sun came out. Tim's mom said, "You can go play outside now, the lightning is gone." Tim was happy and went outside to play with his toy car again. The sky was blue and he had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a smart nurse. She worked in a big hospital. She helped many people feel better. The nurse had a big heart. One day, the nurse wanted to sell her old toys. She put them in a box and went to the park. Many kids came to see the toys. They were very happy. But then, a big rain came. The toys got wet and the kids ran away. The nurse was sad. She went home with her wet toys. The nurse had a bad day.

Once upon a time, there was a little pumpkin. The pumpkin lived in a big garden. The garden had many flowers, trees, and other pumpkins. The little pumpkin had many friends. They played together every day. One day, the sun became very hot. The garden did not have much water. The plants and the pumpkins started to feel dry. They needed water to grow and be happy. The little pumpkin and its friends were sad. A kind girl saw the dry garden. She knew the plants and pumpkins needed water. She brought a big watering can and gave water to the garden. The plants and pumpkins drank the water. They felt better and started to grow again. The little pumpkin and its friends were happy. They thanked the kind girl for her help.

Emma was feeling happy. She went to the roof of her house. She saw some birds wearing colourful feathers. She wanted to wear feathers too! So her mum and dad found some colourful feathers for Emma. She was very excited and put them on quickly. She wore them around the roof like the birds. Emma felt very happy wearing the feathers. She laughed and twirled around the roof. The birds were singing and clapping their wings. When it was time to go home, Emma took off the feathers and kept them safe in a box. She was sad to leave but happy that she had had a wonderful time.

One day, a big red bus was driving down the street. Inside the bus, there was a little boy named Tim and his mom. Tim was very hungry. He saw a girl eating a tasty apple and wanted one too. "Mom, I want a tasty apple like her," said Tim. His mom told him to wait until they got home. But Tim didn't want to wait. He started to tease the girl with the apple. "Give me your apple!" he said. The girl felt sad and started to cry. Just then, the bus hit a big bump and the apple flew out of the girl's hand. The apple rolled to Tim's feet. Tim picked it up and felt bad for teasing the girl. He gave the apple back to her and said, "I'm sorry for teasing you. I should have waited like my mom said." The girl smiled and they both learned to be patient and kind to others.

Once upon a time, a boy named Tim loved to ride his bike. One day, he went on a bike ride to find a special rock called a mineral. He heard that this mineral was very pretty and he wanted to see it for himself. As Tim rode his bike, he was a little careless. He didn't watch where he was going and hit a big rock. He fell off his bike and started to cry. But then, he saw the rock he hit was the pretty mineral he was looking for all along! Tim was so happy that he found the mineral, even though it was because of his fall. He took the pretty rock home and showed it to his mom. She was so proud of him for finding it. From that day on, Tim was more careful when he rode his bike and always remembered the special day he found the pretty mineral.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. Lily loved to eat jelly. One day, she saw a big, cold jelly on the table. Lily was very happy and wanted to eat it all. But, her brother Tom saw the jelly too. Tom wanted to eat the jelly as well. They both waved their hands at each other and said, "No, it's mine!" This made them very sad because they both wanted the jelly. Then, their mom came and saw them fighting. She said, "Don't fight, kids. Let's share the cold jelly." So, Lily and Tom both ate the jelly together. They were happy and waved at each other with a big smile. From that day on, they always shared their jelly and never fought again.

Monica and her brother Tony were playing together in the park. Monica had a radio and they were both singing and dancing to the music. Then Tony had an idea. "Let's be famous," said Tony. "We'll pretend to be a singing act and perform to the people in the park." Monica was very excited, so they practised their dance moves and songs. But then their mum called them back home. "No!" said Tony. He tried to make his mum understand, but she said it was time for dinner. Monica and Tony were very sad and disappointed. But then Tony had another idea. "Let's be famous at home too," said Tony. So Monica and Tony pretended to be a singing act at home in their living room. They found something special to be their stage and danced around it. Even their mum joined in and sang with them. Monica and Tony were thrilled and felt famous. They laughed and danced until it was time for bed.

One day, John and his mom went to the park. John skipped happily around the grass. He liked skipping. It was fun! John then saw a hose. "Mom, what's that?" he asked. "It's a hose," his mom said. "It's used for watering the flowers. See, it's making the flowers nice." John was so excited! He wanted to try it too. His mom said, "Ok, you can have a turn." She showed him how to move the hose around the flowers. John skipped around with the hose, watering the flowers. He thought it was so fun and the flowers looked really nice. After he was done, John said, "Mom, let's come back to the park tomorrow and I'll water the flowers again!" His mom smiled and replied, "Ok, that sounds like a nice idea!"

Once upon a time there was a boy. He was 3 years old and really wanted to get a colorful clock. Every day he would ask his mummy and daddy for one, but they said no. One day he saw one in the store window. He was so excited! He asked his Mummy to get it for him and she said: "No, sorry sweetheart. It's too expensive". He was sad and dejected. He went outside to play and saw a colorful clock in the neighbor's garden. He went to take a closer look. It was his dream clock! He ran home to ask his parents for it. His mummy and daddy looked at each other and laughed. "Of course you can have the clock, sweetheart" his mummy said. The little boy was very excited and thanked his mummy and daddy. He ran outside to get his new colorful clock. He couldn't believe his luck. He was so happy to finally have the colorful clock he always wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a soft bunny named Bob. Bob liked hopping on the trail near his home. He liked to play with his friends, a squirrel and a bird. One day, while they were playing, they saw a big rock on the trail. They did not want to disturb the rock, but they wanted to keep playing. So, they thought of a plan. The squirrel and the bird pushed the rock, while Bob hopped over it. They were happy they did not disturb the rock. They kept playing on the trail and had a fun day.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and building towers. They did not see that their dad was sleeping on the big armchair near the window. He was very tired from working all day and he needed a nap. Suddenly, Lily saw something hairy on the armchair. She thought it was a toy and she wanted to touch it. She ran to the armchair and grabbed the hairy thing. It was not a toy, it was dad's beard! "Ouch!" dad shouted, waking up. He was not happy that Lily disturbed his sleep. He looked at her with a frown. "Daddy, what is this?" Lily asked, holding his beard. "That is my beard, Lily. It is part of my face. You should not pull it, it hurts," dad said. "Sorry, daddy. I did not know. I thought it was a toy. It is very hairy," Lily said. "I know, Lily. But it is not a toy. It is for keeping me warm and making me look handsome," dad said, smiling. "Can I touch it gently?" Lily asked. "OK, Lily. But only gently. And then let me sleep a little more, please," dad said. Lily touched his beard gently and felt how soft and prickly it was. She liked it. She gave dad a kiss and said, "You are handsome, daddy. And hairy." "Thank you, Lily. You are sweet, and pretty. And not hairy," dad said. He hugged her and closed his eyes. Lily went back to her toys and played quietly with Ben. She did not disturb dad again. She was a good girl.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy old cat named Tom. Tom lived in a small house with a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to play with Tom, but Tom did not like to play. He just wanted to sleep all day. One sunny day, Sue wanted to play a game with Tom. "Tom, let's play a game! We can run and count numbers," said Sue. Tom did not want to play, but Sue was very excited. So, Tom decided to try the game. They ran around the house and counted numbers. "One, two, three!" Sue laughed as they played. After playing the game, Tom did not feel grumpy anymore. He was happy and had fun with Sue. They played the game every day. Tom learned that playing with friends can make you happy. The moral of the story is that sharing fun times with others can help you feel better and less grumpy.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a nosy cat named Tom. Tom liked to watch a film with his best friend, a little girl named Sue. They watched films on the big TV in Sue's house. One day, Tom and Sue were watching a film about a big, happy dog. But the film stopped working. Tom and Sue were sad. Tom started to complain. He meowed and meowed. He wanted to see the happy dog again. Sue's mom heard Tom complain. She came into the room and fixed the film. Tom and Sue were happy again. They watched the film about the big, happy dog and laughed. Tom stopped being nosy and complaining, and they all had a great day.

Once upon a time, there was a big lake. A duck named Tim lived there. Tim was a proud duck who liked to test how fast he could swim. One day, Tim met a new friend, a fish named Sam. Sam also liked to swim fast. "I can swim faster than you, Tim!" said Sam. Tim laughed and said, "No, you can't! Let's test it!" So they decided to race from one side of the lake to the other. They asked a frog named Fred to watch and see who won. The race started and Tim and Sam swam as fast as they could. Tim was ahead, but then something unexpected happened. A big wave came and took Tim away. Sam stopped and looked for Tim, but he was gone. Sam and Fred were very sad. They did not know what to do. The proud duck Tim was lost, and the race had a bad ending. Sam and Fred learned that it's not always good to test how fast you can swim in the big lake.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to eat yogurt. He went to the kitchen and saw a big yogurt cup. Tim was very happy. He tried to open the yogurt, but it was too tight. He tried and tried, but he could not open it. Tim was sad. Tim had an idea. He saw a small hole in the yogurt cup. He thought his hand could fit in the hole. So, he put his hand inside the hole to get the yogurt. But, his hand got stuck. Tim was very sad and scared. Tim's mom came into the kitchen and saw him. She tried to help him, but his hand would not come out. They went to the doctor, but the doctor could not help either. In the end, Tim had to live with the yogurt cup on his hand forever. Tim was very sad and never ate yogurt again.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim and his friend, a talking cat named Kitty, wanted to create a swing in their yard. They found a strong tree with a big branch. They needed a rope to make the swing. Tim said, "Kitty, can you help me find a rope?" Kitty nodded and they both looked around. They found a long rope in the shed. They were very happy. Together, they tied the rope to the tree branch. Tim said, "We need to make it tight so it won't fall." Kitty helped Tim pull the rope tight. Then they made a seat with a small piece of wood. They took turns on the swing, laughing and having fun.

Lily and Ben are playing with blocks in the living room. They are building a big tower with many colors. Lily likes to move the blocks with her hands and stack them high. Ben likes to move the blocks with his mouth and chew them softly. "Ben, stop!" Lily says. "You are making the blocks messy with your mouth. They are not food. They are toys." Ben looks at Lily and smiles. He has a block in his mouth and some drool on his chin. He thinks the blocks are tasty and fun. He does not want to stop. "No, Lily," he says. "I like the blocks. They are yummy and chewy. They are food and toys." Lily shakes her head. She does not like the blocks in Ben's mouth. She thinks they are dirty and gross. She wants to keep them clean and neat. "Ben, please," she says. "Give me the block. You can have this one." She holds out a different block for Ben. It is yellow and round. Ben looks at the yellow block. He does not like it. It is not as good as the block in his mouth. It is boring and smooth. "No, Lily," he says. "I want this one." He points to the block in his mouth. It is blue and square. Lily and Ben start to argue. They both want the blue block. They pull and tug on it. They make loud noises with their mouths. They are not happy. Mom hears the noise from the kitchen. She comes to the living room. She sees Lily and Ben fighting over the block. She sees the messy blocks on the floor. She is not happy. "Lily, Ben, stop!" she says. "What are you doing? You are making a big mess with the blocks. You are not sharing. You are not being nice." Lily and Ben stop. They look at Mom. They feel sorry. They know they did something wrong. "Sorry, Mom," they say. "We were playing with the blocks. We wanted the same one. We did not share. We did not be nice." Mom nods. She understands. She knows they are still learning. She wants to help them. "It's okay," she says. "But you need to learn how to play with the blocks. You need to move them with your hands, not your mouth. You need to keep them clean, not messy. You need to share them, not fight over them. You need to be nice, not loud." Lily and Ben listen to Mom. They want to play with the blocks the right way. They want to make Mom happy. "Okay, Mom," they say. "We will move them with our hands. We will keep them clean. We will share them. We will be nice." Mom smiles. She is happy. She gives Lily and Ben a hug. She helps them pick up the blocks. She shows them how to build a bigger tower with many colors. They all play together. They have fun.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a hungry little bear named Ben. Ben loved to eat sweet honey from the bees. One day, he went out to find food because the new season had just started. The sun was shining, and the flowers were waking up. Ben walked and walked until he found a big tree. He started to climb the tree to get closer to the bees. The bees were busy making honey. Ben was very careful not to scare the bees away. He knew that if he was nice to them, they would share their honey with him. Finally, Ben reached the top of the tree. The bees saw how hungry he was and decided to give him some honey. Ben was so happy! He ate the honey and thanked the bees. Then, he climbed back down and went home. From that day on, Ben and the bees became good friends, and they shared honey every season.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny infant named Tim. Tim had many animal friends in the forest. They liked to play together every day. Tim's animal friends were a big bear, a fast rabbit, and a funny bird. One day, Tim and his friends felt frustrated. They could not find a good game to play. They tried to play hide and seek, but the big bear could not hide well. They tried to race, but Tim and the big bear were too slow. They tried to fly, but only the funny bird could do it. Then, Tim had a great idea. He said, "Let's unite and make a new game!" So, they all worked together. The big bear carried Tim, the fast rabbit ran around them, and the funny bird flew above them. They called their new game "Forest Friends Fun." They played their new game all day and were very happy.

One day, a weak bunny named Ben wanted to win a race. All his friends were fast, but Ben was not. He was sad because he could not run fast like them. Ben had a big sister named Sue. Sue was very funny and liked to tell jokes. She saw Ben was sad and wanted to help him. Sue said, "Ben, you may not be fast, but you can still win with a joke!" The next day, Ben and his friends lined up to race. When the race started, Ben told a very funny joke. His friends laughed so much they could not run fast. Ben ran as fast as he could and won the race! Ben's friends were happy for him and they all laughed together. Ben learned that even a weak bunny can win with a good joke. Now, Ben always tells jokes and makes his friends laugh.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely pan. The pan lived in a small house with a girl named Sue and her mom. The pan was sad because no one used it to cook. One day, Sue's mom said, "Sue, let's make some food." Sue was happy and went to the kitchen. Sue saw the lonely pan and decided to use it. She put the pan on the stove and started to cook. The pan became very hot. Sue's mom saw the pan and said, "Oh no, Sue! The pan is too hot. I regret not watching you." Sue was sad and worried about the pan. Sue's mom turned off the stove and let the pan cool down. She told Sue, "Next time, we will cook together so the pan won't be too hot." Sue smiled and said, "Okay, Mom. I want the pan to be happy." From that day on, Sue and her mom always cooked together, and the lonely pan was never lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a little car named Speedy. Speedy was a lucky car because he could go very fast. He loved to speed down the road and feel the wind blow through his windows. One day, Speedy saw a folder lying on the ground. He stopped and picked it up. Inside the folder, there were beautiful drawings of cars, trees, and houses. Speedy wanted to find the person who made the drawings and return the folder to them. As Speedy drove around, he met a little girl named Lily. Speedy asked, "Is this your folder?" Lily looked inside and smiled. "Yes, it is! Thank you, Speedy!" she said. Speedy felt happy that he could help Lily. They became good friends and had lots of fun together. And from that day on, Speedy felt even luckier than before.

Once upon a time, in a big house, there was a little mouse. The mouse was very excited. He loved to play and run around the house. The mouse had a secret room where he kept his toys. To keep his toys safe, he would lock the door. One day, the mouse found a new toy in the house. It was a big, red ball. He was so excited to play with it. He rolled the ball all around the house. But then, he remembered his secret room. He wanted to put the new toy with his other toys. The mouse pushed the big red ball to the secret room. He tried to open the door, but it was locked. He looked for the key, but he could not find it. The mouse was sad. He could not put his new toy in the secret room. But then, he remembered where he hid the key. It was under the blue rug. He found the key, unlocked the door, and put the big red ball with his other toys. The mouse was excited and happy again. He knew his toys were safe in the secret room, and he could play with them anytime he wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little ant named Amy. Amy was an independent ant who liked to work all by herself. She loved to find food and bring it back to her ant friends. One day, Amy saw a big cookie in the distance. She thought it would be a great sight to show her friends. Amy tried to carry the cookie all by herself, but it was too big and heavy. She pulled and pushed, but the cookie would not move. Amy felt sad and didn't know what to do. She wanted to bring the cookie back to her friends, but she needed help. Amy decided to ask her ant friends for help. Together, they all worked hard to carry the cookie back to their home. Amy learned that sometimes it's okay to ask for help and that working together can be fun. The ants all enjoyed the big cookie, and they were happy to share the great sight with each other.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing in the sun. They were very glad to be friends. The cat said, "I am glad to play with you." The dog said, "Me too! We have fun." Then, a big bird came down from the sky. The cat and the dog were scared. The bird said, "Do not be scared. I am a nice bird. I want to be your friend too." The cat, the dog, and the bird played all day. They were very glad to be friends. The big bird was not scary. They all had fun together. And from that day, they were always happy to play together.

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had a secret place under a big tree. There they had a box with their toys and books. They belonged to each other. One day, a new boy came to the park. His name was Ben. He saw Lily and Tom playing under the tree. He wanted to join them. He walked over and said, "Hi, can I play with you?" Lily and Tom looked at him. They did not know him. They did not want to share their secret place. They said, "No, this is our place. You can't play here. Go away." Ben felt sad. He did not have any friends. He did not have a place to belong. He walked away and sat on a bench. He wished he had someone to play with. A lady saw Ben sitting alone. She was his teacher. She knew he was new in town. She walked over and said, "Hello, Ben. Are you having fun in the park?" Ben shook his head. He said, "No, I'm not. I tried to play with Lily and Tom, but they didn't let me. They have a secret place under the tree. They said I can't play there. They said I don't belong." The lady felt sorry for Ben. She said, "That's not very nice of them. Everyone deserves a place to belong. Everyone deserves a friend. How about you come with me? I have a secret place too. It's in the library. There you can find many books and toys and games. You can play with me and other children. You can belong there." Ben smiled. He liked the sound of that. He said, "Really? Can I go with you? Can I see your secret place?" The lady nodded. She said, "Of course. Come on, let's go. I'm sure you'll be happy there." Ben got up and followed the lady. He felt hopeful and curious. He wondered what his new secret place would be like. He hoped he would find some friends there. He hoped he would belong there.

Once upon a time, there was a dancer named Lily. She loved to skip and dance all day long. One hot day, Lily went outside to play. The sun was shining, and the sky was blue. As Lily skipped around, she saw her friend, Tim the turtle. Tim was very slow and could not skip like Lily. "Hi Tim!" said Lily. "Do you want to skip with me?" Tim looked at Lily and said, "I can't skip, but I can watch you." So, Lily danced and skipped for Tim. She twirled and jumped, making Tim smile. They played together until the sun went down. When it was time to go home, Lily gave Tim a big hug. They were very happy to be friends.

One day, a little raven named Ray was playing in the park. Ray was a funny raven who liked to make his friends laugh. He saw a small plant and thought it would be fun to help it grow. Ray called his friend, a big elephant named Ella. "Ella, can you help me make this plant grow?" he asked. Ella nodded, "Yes, Ray! I will help you." Ella used her long nose to give the plant some water. Ray and Ella waited to see what would happen. After a few days, the plant started to grow. It grew bigger and bigger, and soon, it was a tall tree. Ray and Ella were very happy. They played under the tree and laughed together. The tree had grown so big because of their help, and now they had a new place to play.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a girl named Sue. Sue loved to mix colors. One day, she found a new color. It was a mix of blue and green. She was very happy. Sue ran to her friend Tom and said, "Look! I made a new color! Do you like it?" Tom looked at the color and said, "Yes, I like it. It is very nice. Can I have some?" Sue thought for a moment and said, "Yes, you can have some. But you must make a promise. You must be honest and not say it is your color." Tom agreed and said, "I promise. I will be honest." So, Sue gave Tom some of the new color. Tom was very happy. He used the color to paint a big tree. Sue and Tom played together, using the new color they both loved. They were happy because they were honest and kept their promise. And from that day on, they always shared their colors and played together.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion who loved to roar. He lived in a high cave on a high hill. The lion had a friend, a little bird with a pretty veil on her head. They played together every day. One day, the little bird lost her veil. She was very sad. The big lion wanted to help his friend. He roared very loud and asked all the animals to come and help find the veil. All the animals searched high and low for the pretty veil. At last, they found it in a bush. The little bird was so happy! She thanked the big lion and all the animals for their help. The big lion and the little bird learned that helping each other is very important. They stayed friends forever, always ready to help one another. And every time the lion roared, it was a reminder that friends should always help each other.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to mix things. He would mix water and mud, mix his toys, and even mix his food. One day, Tim found a paper with the word "license" on it. He didn't know what it meant, but he thought it looked fun to mix with other things. Tim went to his room and started to mix the license with his toys. He mixed and mixed until all his toys were in a big pile with the license. Suddenly, his toys started to move! They became dangerous and started to break things in his room. Tim was scared and didn't know what to do. He tried to stop the dangerous toys, but they were too strong. The toys broke everything in the house and then went outside. The whole town was scared of the dangerous toys. Tim felt very sad because he knew it was his fault. He wished he never mixed the license with his toys. In the end, Tim learned that mixing things can sometimes lead to bad things happening.

Once upon a time, in a charming little house, there lived a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. Her mom always told her to pack her bag before going out. Lily knew it was important to pack her bag with all the things she needed for a fun day. In her bag, Lily put her favorite toy, a ball, and some snacks. She also remembered to pack lotion. Her mom told her that lotion helps to keep her skin safe when she plays outside. Lily liked the smell of the lotion and how it felt on her skin. Lily went outside with her bag and played all day. She had so much fun with her ball and shared her snacks with her friends. When the sun was very bright, Lily put on her lotion. It was a great day, and Lily was happy that she had packed her bag with everything she needed.

One day, a girl named Sue found a big, red ball. It was not a normal ball. It was made of plastic. Sue wanted to taste the ball. She thought it would taste like candy. Sue went to her friend Tom and said, "Look at my big, red ball! I think it will taste like candy. Do you want to taste it too?" Tom said, "Yes, let's taste it!" They both took a small bite of the plastic ball. Suddenly, the ball started to grow bigger and bigger! Sue and Tom were very surprised. They did not know that the ball would grow when they tasted it. The big, red ball was now so big, they could play inside it! They had so much fun in the big, red ball that they forgot it was not a normal ball.

Once upon a time, there was a big march in a small town. People walked and danced together. They were very happy. At the end of the march, they had a big party. They wanted to decorate the party place with pretty things. A little boy named Tim wanted to help. He asked his mom, "Can I help decorate the party place?" His mom said, "Yes, Tim. You can help by making tasty treats for everyone to eat." So, Tim and his mom baked tasty cookies and cakes. They decorated them with colorful icing. When they took the treats to the party, everyone loved them. They said, "Thank you, Tim! Your treats are so tasty!" At the end of the party, Tim felt very proud. He learned that helping others can make you feel good. And that was the best feeling of all.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside in the deep grass. One day, he found a big, red ball. Tim had an idea. He wanted to throw the ball and see how far it would go. Tim took a big step back and threw the ball with all his might. The ball went up, up, up, and then down, down, down. It landed far away in the deep grass. Tim had a big smile on his face. He was so happy to see how far the ball went. Tim ran to get the ball and threw it again and again. Each time, he had a big smile on his face. His mom saw him playing and smiled too. They played together, throwing the ball and laughing in the deep grass. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little adorable dog named Toby. Toby loved to play with his red ball and run around the big green yard. One day, Toby saw a bright flame in the yard. He was curious and wanted to play with it. Toby's mom saw him near the flame and said, "No, Toby! Don't play with the flame. It is hot and can hurt you!" Toby didn't listen and tried to bathe the flame with water. He wanted to make it safe to play with. But when Toby splashed the water on the flame, it got bigger and bigger. The flame grew so big that it burned Toby's red ball. Toby was sad that he didn't listen to his mom. Now he had no red ball to play with, and he learned that he should always listen to his mom.

Once upon a time there was a queen who wanted to play a game. She asked her two children, a brother and a sister, if they wanted to play hide and seek with her. The children were very excited and the sister said, “Let’s play!” The queen said, “Ok, I’ll count to ten and you two hide somewhere.” She started counting, “One… two… three…” The brother said, “I’m gonna hide behind that tree!” He rushed over to the tree and hid. The sister was getting impatient so she said, “Hurry up, I need to find a place to hide too!” So the queen finished counting and she said, “Ready or not, here I come!” The brother and sister both stayed quiet and hoped the queen wouldn’t find them!

One day, a little girl named True went for a wander in the woods. She saw a huge tree and thought it would be fun to climb. As she climbed higher and higher, she saw a big bird sitting on a branch. "Hello, big bird!" True said. "Do you like this huge tree too?" "Yes, I do, True!" the big bird replied. "But be careful, it's very high up here!" True didn't listen to the big bird and kept climbing higher. She wanted to touch the sky. But the higher she went, the windier it got. True started to feel scared, but she didn't want to stop. Suddenly, a strong wind blew, and True lost her grip on the tree. She fell down, down, down, and landed on the ground with a thud. She was hurt and cried for her mom and dad. The big bird flew down to help, but it was too late. True had learned a hard lesson about listening to her friends and being careful when she wandered too high.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a big, interesting net. The net was on the ground. Tim wanted to play with the net. He thought it would be fun to catch things in the net. Tim saw a cat. He tried to catch the cat with the net. But the cat was too fast. "Come back, cat!" Tim said. But the cat did not come back. Tim felt sad. Then, Tim saw a dog. The dog was big and brown. Tim tried to catch the dog with the net. But the dog was too big. The net could not catch the dog. The dog said, "Woof!" The dog's big tail made Tim slip. Tim fell on the ground. He was not hurt, but he was surprised. Tim was sad he could not catch the cat or the dog. But then, he saw a butterfly. The butterfly was pretty and small. Tim tried to catch the butterfly with the net. This time, he did it! Tim caught the butterfly in the net. He was very happy. Tim let the butterfly go. The butterfly said, "Thank you!" Tim was surprised. He did not know butterflies could talk. The butterfly and Tim became friends. They played together in the park all day.

Tom and Mia liked to play with magnets. They had many magnets of different shapes and colors. They stuck them on the fridge, on the door, on the table. They made pictures and patterns with them. One day, they found a big magnet in the garage. It was silver and round and very strong. Tom and Mia wanted to try it. They took it to the kitchen and stuck it on the fridge. It made a loud clack sound. "Wow, this magnet is so interesting!" Mia said. "Look, it can hold many other magnets on it!" "Let me try!" Tom said. He took some magnets from the fridge and put them on the big magnet. They also made a loud clack sound and stayed on the big magnet. Tom and Mia had fun with the big magnet. They forgot about their mom, who was making lunch. She had a note on the fridge that said: "Don't forget to wash your hands before eating." The note had a small magnet on it. But when Tom and Mia stuck the big magnet on the fridge, the note fell off. The small magnet was not strong enough to stay on the fridge with the big magnet. The note landed on the floor, under the table. Tom and Mia did not see the note. They did not wash their hands. They played with the big magnet until mom called them for lunch. "Come on, kids, it's time to eat!" mom said. "Did you wash your hands?" Tom and Mia looked at each other. They did not remember to wash their hands. They remembered the big magnet. "Sorry, mom, we forgot," Tom said. "Why did you forget?" mom asked. "Because we found a big magnet in the garage," Mia said. "It was so interesting!" Mom looked at the fridge. She saw the big magnet and the other magnets on it. She did not see the note. "Where is the note I left you?" mom asked. Tom and Mia looked at the fridge. They did not see the note. They wondered where it was. Mom looked under the table. She saw the note on the floor. She picked it up and showed it to Tom and Mia. "Here is the note," mom said. "It says: Don't forget to wash your hands before eating. The big magnet made the note fall off. The big magnet did not remind you to wash your hands. It made you forget." Tom and Mia felt sorry. They said sorry to mom. They went to the bathroom and washed their hands. They learned that magnets are interesting, but they are not good at reminding.

Once upon a time, in a small house, lived a little boy named Tim and his mom. Tim loved to eat beef, but he didn't like spicy food. One day, his mom made a spicy beef stew for dinner. Tim looked at the stew and said, "Mom, is this spicy?" His mom smiled and said, "You'll see, Tim." She knew that Tim was a little scared of spicy food, but she wanted him to try it. Later, Tim's friend, Sam, came over to play. They played with their toys and had lots of fun. But Tim kept thinking about the spicy beef stew. He was scared to try it, but he didn't want to tell Sam. When it was time for dinner, Tim's mom put the spicy beef stew on the table. Tim looked at Sam and said, "I'm scared to try this. I don't like spicy food." Sam said, "Don't be scared, Tim. We can try it together." So, Tim and Sam tried the spicy beef stew. To their surprise, they both liked it! Tim was happy that he tried something new and wasn't scared anymore. From that day on, Tim wasn't scared of spicy food, and he and Sam enjoyed many spicy beef dinners together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a new toy. It was a big ball. He loved to play with it every day. One day, at noon, Tim went to the park with his mom. He played with his new ball. He threw it high in the air and caught it. He was very happy. But then, the ball went far away. Tim could not find it. He started to cry. His mom came to help him. They looked and looked. Finally, they found the ball under a tree. Tim stopped crying and smiled. He played with his new ball all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful cat named Kitty. Kitty liked to play with her friends. One day, Kitty found a toy with numbers on it. She was very happy and wanted to show her friends. Kitty and her friends played a game. They had to guess the number on the toy. They took turns and tried to measure how big the number was. They laughed and had a lot of fun. In the end, all of Kitty's friends guessed the right number. They were very proud of themselves. Kitty was happy that her friends liked her toy. They played with the toy and had a great day.

Tim and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. They had a new mailbox that their dad put up. It was red and shiny and had their name on it. One day, they saw a big truck stop by their mailbox. A man got out and put something in it. Tim and Lily ran to see what it was. "Maybe it is a present for us!" Tim said. "Or a letter from grandma!" Lily said. They opened the mailbox and saw a brown bag. It smelled bad. They took it out and looked inside. It was full of rotten fruit and worms. "Yuck!" Tim and Lily said. "Who did this?" They heard a laugh from behind a bush. It was Tom, the mean boy who lived next door. He liked to play tricks on them. "I did it!" Tom said. "I found this bag in the trash and thought you would like it. It matches your new mailbox. Ha ha ha!" Tim and Lily were angry and sad. They did not like Tom. He was not nice. He always made fun of them and their things. "Go away, Tom!" Tim said. "You are mean and rude. We don't want your rotten fruit. We want our mailbox to be clean and new." "Yeah, go away, Tom!" Lily said. "You are not our friend. You are a bully. We will tell our dad what you did." Tom did not care. He laughed some more and ran away. He thought he was funny and clever. Tim and Lily threw the bag in the trash. They cleaned their mailbox with a cloth and water. They hugged each other and went inside. They hoped Tom would not bother them again. They loved their new mailbox and each other.

Once upon a time, there was a kind vendor who sold yummy treats. He had a little cart with wheels that he pushed around the town. Every day, he would meet many people and share his treats with them. The vendor was a good friend to everyone. One day, a small, fearful dog came to the vendor's cart. The dog was shaking and looked very sad. The vendor knew he had to help the dog feel better. He thought of a plan to make the dog happy and not scared anymore. The next day, the vendor brought a soft, warm blanket and a tasty bone for the dog. When the fearful dog came back, the vendor gave the dog the blanket and bone. The dog felt comfort and safe with the vendor. The dog wagged its tail and smiled. From that day on, the dog and the vendor were best friends, and the dog was never scared again.

Once upon a time there was a mommy and a daddy, who both looked at something in the street. It was a pet, a cute little rabbit! They both thought he was so cute they had to have him. The mommy said, "Let's examine him closely." So the daddy picked up the pet and cuddled him softly. The pet felt so happy and jumped around in the daddy's arms. The mommy asked, "What's that the pet has in his mouth?" The daddy examined it closely, and suddenly he realised it was a tasty carrot! The pet munched on it very happily. The daddy looked at the mommy and said, "This pet sure is a tasty treat!" The mommy and daddy smiled, and from then on, the pet lived with them forever in their warm home.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to her room to pack her bag. She wanted to go to the park with her mom. She put her orange ball, her hat, and her water bottle in her bag. She was excited to play outside. "Mom, I am ready to go!" said Lily. Her mom came to her room and saw her bag. "Good job packing your bag, Lily! Let's go to the park," said her mom. They walked to the park, holding hands and smiling. At the park, Lily played with her orange ball. She kicked it and threw it in the air. After a while, Lily felt tired. She went to her mom and asked for a hug. Her mom gave her a big, warm hug. They sat on the grass and shared a snack. They had a fun day at the park together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big cabinet in her room. Lily loved to play with her toys near the cabinet. One day, she saw a grumpy cat sitting on top of the cabinet. The cat looked sad and lonely. Lily wanted to make the cat happy, so she gave it some food. The cat ate the food and started to nod its head. It was saying "thank you" to Lily. Lily felt happy that she could help the cat. They became good friends and played together every day. But one day, the cat was not on the cabinet. Lily looked everywhere for her friend, but she could not find it. She was very sad. Then, she heard a soft meow from inside the cabinet. Lily opened the cabinet, and there was the cat! The cat had been hiding in the cabinet all along. Lily was so surprised and happy to find her friend. They played together and had lots of fun.

Sam was a young boy who enjoyed playing in the sun. One hot day, he decided it was time to find some help from the heat. He ran to grab his fan and plugged it in. The cool air from the fan was so attractive that he just had to sit in front of it and relax. But then something very strange happened. As soon as he sat in front of the fan, it stopped working! Sam wondered why he was having such bad luck, but he didn't know what to do. He started to suffer from the heat. He felt so uncomfortable and hot. He couldn't take it anymore. Tears started to roll down his face. Suddenly, a thunder storm rolled in and brought a gentle breeze that cooled him down. Sam smiled with relief and thanked the heavens for helping him out. He learned that day to never take things like fans and cool air for granted.

One day, a deer was in the woods. The deer was very frustrated. It was dirty and wanted to be clean. The deer looked for a place to clean itself. It found a big pond with water. The deer was happy and started to clean itself in the water. While the deer was cleaning, a big wind came. The wind blew many leaves into the pond. The deer was surprised and a little scared. The leaves made the water dirty again. The deer was sad and frustrated. It did not want to be dirty anymore. Then, something unexpected happened. A big rain cloud came over the woods. The rain started to fall on the deer. The rain cleaned the deer and washed away the dirt. The deer was happy and clean again. The deer thanked the rain and went back to play in the woods.

One day, a little girl named Lucy dared to go into the deep, dark woods. She wanted to find her mother, who had gone there to pick berries. Lucy was scared, but she knew she had to be brave. As Lucy walked, she met a big, selfish bear. The bear said, "This is my forest! Go away!" But Lucy was brave and said, "I need to find my mother. I won't go until I find her!" The bear was surprised by Lucy's words and decided to help her. Together, they searched for Lucy's mother. Suddenly, they found her, but she was not picking berries. She was having a tea party with other animals! Lucy's mother said, "I wanted to surprise you with a fun tea party!" Lucy, her mother, and the bear all laughed and enjoyed the tea party together. The selfish bear learned to share, and they all became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle race. It was special because everyone raced with prunes. Every day the people in the race dashed and dashed until they crossed the finish line. All the while the prunes bounced along joyfully. One day, a little boy named Timmy joined the race. He had never raced with prunes before and was a bit scared. But as soon as he started moving with the prunes, he smiled. He was having so much fun! He kept running with the prunes and smiled even bigger when he saw the finish line. When Timmy finally crossed the finish line, he was so happy and so proud of himself. Everyone cheering for him made him feel even better. He was the champion. He had won the gentle race.

Once upon a time, there was a normal boy named Tim. Tim liked to joke a lot. He would make everyone laugh with his funny jokes. One day, Tim found a big book called a novel. The novel had many words and pictures in it. Tim thought it would be fun to read the novel. Tim started to read the novel every day. He read it at home, at school, and even at the park. But as he read the novel, he stopped joking as much. His friends missed his jokes and they did not laugh as much as before. One day, Tim finished the novel. He tried to joke with his friends again, but they did not laugh. They did not find his jokes funny anymore. Tim was sad because his friends did not like his jokes. He wished he never read the novel. From that day on, Tim never read a novel again and he could not make his friends laugh like before. Tim was very sad and he missed the times when everyone laughed at his jokes.

Sam likes to draw with crayons. He has many crayons of different colors. He likes to draw animals and trees and flowers. He draws on paper and on the wall and on the floor. One day, Sam wants to draw a wild lion. He takes a yellow crayon and a brown crayon. He draws a big head and a big body and a big tail. He draws eyes and ears and a nose and a mouth. He draws teeth and claws and a mane. He is very happy with his lion. He wants to show his lion to his mom. He runs to the door and calls for his mom. He does not see the crayon on the floor. He steps on the crayon and slips. He falls down and hurts his knee. He cries and drops his crayons. His mom hears him and comes to see what is wrong. She sees Sam on the floor and the crayon and the lion. She hugs Sam and kisses his knee. She tells him he is brave and his lion is beautiful. She helps him up and picks up his crayons. She tells him he can draw with crayons, but he has to be careful where he puts them. She tells him he can draw on paper, but not on the wall or on the floor. She tells him she loves him and his drawings. She gives him a new paper and a new crayon. Sam smiles and says thank you. He draws a wild lion and a wild mom.

Lily and her mom went to a big party at her aunt's house. There were many people, some she knew and some she did not. Lily saw her cousin Jake, who was four years old. He was playing with a toy car on the floor. "Hi, Jake!" Lily said. "Can I play with you?" "Sure, Lily. This is my new car. It goes very fast. Look!" Jake said. He pushed the car across the carpet and made a loud vroom sound. Lily smiled and picked up another car. She and Jake raced their cars and had fun. Lily's mom came to check on them. She was holding a glass of wine. Wine was a drink for grown-ups, Lily knew. It was red and smelled funny. "Are you having a good time, sweetie?" Lily's mom asked. "Yes, mom. Jake and I are playing with cars. They are very cool," Lily said. "That's nice. Do you want some juice?" Lily's mom asked. "Yes, please. Thank you, mom," Lily said. Lily's mom gave her a cup of juice and kissed her on the cheek. She looked around the room and saw a lady in a blue dress. She was graceful, Lily thought. She moved like a dancer. "Who is that lady, mom?" Lily asked. "That lady is your aunt's friend. She is a ballet teacher. She teaches people how to dance," Lily's mom said. "Wow. She is very pretty. Can she teach me how to dance?" Lily asked. "Maybe. Why don't you go and say hello to her? She might like to meet you," Lily's mom said. Lily nodded and put down her car. She walked over to the lady in the blue dress. She was smiling and talking to another lady. "Excuse me, miss. I'm Lily. I'm Jake's cousin. You are very graceful. Can you teach me how to dance?" Lily said. The lady in the blue dress looked down at Lily and smiled. She recognized her as her friend's niece. She was very cute and polite. "Hello, Lily. I'm Miss Anna. I'm your aunt's friend. You are very sweet. I can teach you some dance moves, if you like. Do you want to try?" Miss Anna said. "Yes, please. I love to dance," Lily said. Miss Anna took Lily's hand and led her to a corner of the room. She showed her how to stand on her toes, how to spin, and how to jump. Lily followed her and tried to copy her. She felt happy and proud. She was learning how to dance like a graceful lady.

Once upon a time, in a big garden, there was a dull flower. This flower was sad because it was not as pretty as the other flowers. It wanted to be like them, but it did not know how. One day, a little bug came to the garden. The bug wanted to fight the pretty flowers. The dull flower did not want the pretty flowers to get hurt, so it said, "I will fight you, bug." The bug laughed and said, "You are too dull to fight me." But the dull flower was brave and fought the bug anyway. As they fought, something unexpected happened. The dull flower started to change. It became bright and pretty, just like the other flowers. The bug was surprised and ran away. The other flowers were so happy and thanked the dull flower, which was now a pretty flower too. The moral of the story is that being brave and kind can make you shine.

One day, a rich man wanted to travel far away. He had a big vase that he loved. He wanted to take the vase with him. So, he put the vase in a box and got ready to go. On his way, he met a girl. The girl said, "Hi! What is in the box?" The rich man said, "It is my big vase. I love it very much." The girl said, "Be careful. It might break." The rich man kept traveling with his vase. He was very careful. He did not want to break it. He went up hills and down hills. He went through the woods and over the river. At last, the rich man got to his new home. He opened the box and looked at his vase. It was not broken. He was very happy. The rich man said, "Thank you, girl. I was careful because of you."

Sara and Tom like to play in the garden. They see many flowers of different colors. Sara likes the red ones and Tom likes the yellow ones. They pick some flowers and put them in a basket. But there is a problem. The sun is very hot and the flowers need water. Sara and Tom do not know this. They are lazy and do not want to go back to the house. They want to play more. "Look, Tom, this flower is pretty," Sara says, holding a purple one. "Yes, it is. But I like this one more," Tom says, showing a blue one. They do not see that the flowers in the basket are wilting. They are sad and thirsty. A bee comes by and sees the flowers. She is angry. She likes flowers and does not want them to die. She buzzes at Sara and Tom. "Hey, you, stop!" the bee says. "You are hurting the flowers. They need water. Give them back to the garden." Sara and Tom are scared. They do not like bees. They think the bee will sting them. "Go away, bee. We like the flowers. They are ours," Sara says. "No, they are not. They are the garden's. You are bad. You are lazy. You do not care about the flowers," the bee says. The bee flies around the basket and tries to take the flowers. Sara and Tom run away. They drop the basket and the flowers fall out. The bee is happy. She saves the flowers. She takes them back to the garden and gives them water. The flowers are happy too. They smile and thank the bee. The bee tells the flowers not to worry. She will protect them from Sara and Tom. She says they are good flowers and they deserve to live. Sara and Tom go back to the house. They are sad and sorry. They do not have any flowers. They learn a lesson. They should not be lazy and they should not hurt the flowers. They should respect the garden and the bee.

Once upon a time, there was a famous bunny named Bob. Bob liked to work a lot. He worked in a big garden, where he grew yummy carrots. He had many friends who came to visit him every day. One day, a little bird named Tim came to see Bob. Tim said, "Bob, I like your waist. It is so tiny!" Bob smiled and said, "Thank you, Tim. I work hard in the garden, and that helps me stay thin." Bob and Tim played in the garden all day. They had so much fun. They laughed and ate carrots together. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a lucky hippo. He was the luckiest hippo in the entire zoo. Every day he would display his skills that made him so lucky. He could make lots of noise, he could run fast, and could even burp the alphabet. The other animals in the zoo were so impressed by the lucky hippo. Every day they would gather around to watch him display his skills. One day the lucky hippo decided he wanted to do something new and special. He decided to build a giant sand castle. The other animals gathered around to watch the lucky hippo build his tower. The lucky hippo had so much fun building his castle that he even forgot to display his other skills. Everyone in the zoo was so proud of the lucky hippo. The moral of this story is that sometimes it is more important to learn new things than to show off the things we already know.

Lily and Ben are playing cops and robbers in the park. Lily has a toy gun and Ben has a hat and a badge. They run around the trees and the swings, pretending to chase bad guys. "Stop, robber! I will shoot you!" Lily shouts, pointing her gun at Ben. "No, you can't catch me! I am too smart!" Ben says, hiding behind a slide. Lily runs after him, but she trips on a rock and falls down. Her gun flies out of her hand and lands in a bush. She starts to cry. "Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asks, coming out of his hiding place. He sees her gun in the bush and picks it up. "I hurt my knee and I lost my gun," Lily says, rubbing her knee. "Here, take your gun back. I'm sorry I ran away from you," Ben says, giving her the gun. "Thank you, Ben. You are a nice robber," Lily says, smiling. They hug and decide to play something else. They see a big case near the bench. It is red and shiny and has a lock on it. "Wow, what is that?" Lily asks, curious. "Maybe it is a treasure case. Let's open it and see what is inside," Ben says, excited. They run to the case and try to open it, but it is too hard. They need a key. "Where can we find a key?" Lily wonders. "Maybe we can ask the man over there. He looks like a cop," Ben says, pointing to a man in a uniform. They go to the man and ask him if he has a key for the case. The man smiles and says yes. He is a real cop and the case is his. He shows them his badge and his gun. "This is my case. It has my things inside. Do you want to see?" he asks. "Yes, please!" Lily and Ben say, eager. The cop opens the case and shows them his things. He has a radio, a flashlight, a notebook, a pen, and a pair of handcuffs. "These are the things I use to do my job. I catch bad guys and keep people safe," he explains. "That is so cool! You are a very smart cop," Lily says, impressed. "Can we play with your things?" Ben asks, politely. "Sure, but be careful. Don't shoot the radio or the flashlight. They are not toys," the cop says, kindly. He lets them play with his things for a while, then he tells them it is time to go. He closes the case and puts it on his shoulder. "Thank you for letting us play with your things. You are a very nice cop," Ben says, grateful. "Thank you for being good kids. You are very smart and brave. Maybe you can be cops when you grow up," the cop says, friendly. He waves goodbye and walks away. Lily and Ben wave back and go to their parents. They tell them about their adventure in the park. They had a lot of fun playing cops and robbers.

Once there was a girl who was very curious. She wanted to explore the world around her. One day, feeling brave, she decided to borrow her mommy's fancy shoes. She slipped them on and felt so excited and grown-up. Now she could go on an adventure! On her way, she came across a grape patch. She was very hungry so she grabbed one of the big, juicy grapes. She took a big bite and oh, it tasted so good! She ate more and more until the whole grape was gone. Her stomach felt full, but she still wanted to explore. Suddenly, she heard a little voice say "is that fancy shoe yours?". She looked around, but no one was there. She looked down and saw a tiny mouse wearing her mommy's fancy shoe! The girl smiled and asked the mouse if he wanted to borrow her shoe. The mouse agreed and hopped away on his own special adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a whistle. He liked to play with it all day. One day, Tim saw a big, crazy bird. The bird was very loud. Tim thought that the bird wanted to play with his whistle. So, he gave his whistle to the bird. The bird took the whistle and flew away. Tim was sad. But then, something unexpected happened. The bird came back with many friends. They all had whistles too! They played a fun whistle song for Tim. Tim was very happy and had a great day with his new bird friends.

Lizzy and her Mom were at the park. The sky was filled with wild clouds and they were having lots of fun. Then, they spotted something special. "What's that Mom?" Lizzy asked. "It's called a card. It's made of paper and it has a special message inside," Mom replied. Mom picked up the card and opened it to show Lizzy. Inside the card was a magical phrase. "I'm going to show you something special Lizzy," Mom said. She waved her hand over the card. Lizzy gasped in amazement as the card started to flutter in the air, until it was destroyed. "Shall I show you how to do it again?," Mom asked. Lizzy was so excited and shouted, "Yes!" Without knowing it, she had just been given the ability to destroy things like the card. The following morning, Lizzy and Mom went to the park again. There were wild birds flying in the sky and Lizzy wanted to show off her newfound skill. "Look what I can do Mom!" Lizzy shouted, as she waved her hand over a card and it was destroyed. "That's amazing, sweetheart. You've learnt some pretty powerful magic," Mom said. Lizzy smiled, proud of herself and all the things she had discovered.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a blue bookshelf. The bookshelf was very big and full of books. A little girl named Amy lived in the house. She loved to read the books on the bookshelf. One day, Amy saw a big blue book on the bookshelf. She wanted to read it. She asked her mom, "Can I read the big blue book?" Her mom said, "Yes, you can read it, but be careful. It is a very special book." Amy took the big blue book from the bookshelf and started to read. As she read, the book began to part in the middle. Amy was surprised! Inside the book, she found a secret map. The map showed the way to a hidden treasure. Amy showed the map to her mom. They decided to follow the map together. They walked and walked until they found a big tree. Under the tree, they found a treasure box. They opened the box and found many colorful toys and treats. Amy and her mom were very happy. They took the treasure home and shared it with their family. The big blue book on the bookshelf was now even more special to Amy.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside with his dog, Spot. They would run and jump in the yard all day long. One day, Tim saw a ball on the roof of his house. He said to Spot, "Oh no! My ball is on the roof! We need to get it down!" Spot barked and wagged his tail, ready to help. They were both very alert, looking for a way to get the ball down. Tim found a long stick and tried to poke the ball off the roof. But as he poked, he accidentally made a hole in the roof. "Oh no! I spoiled the roof!" Tim cried. Spot barked loudly to let Tim's mom know something was wrong. Tim's mom came outside and saw the hole in the roof. She said, "Don't worry, Tim. We can fix the roof. But next time, be more careful and ask for help." Tim hugged his mom and promised to be more careful. And with Spot's help, they all fixed the roof together.

One day, a girl with long hair went to a store. She wanted to order a toy. At the store, she met a smelly dog. The dog was very nice, but it smelled bad. The girl said, "Hi, dog! Why are you smelly?" The dog said, "I don't know. I just smell bad." They both laughed and played together. The girl forgot about the toy she wanted to order. Then, something unexpected happened. The girl's hair got stuck in the dog's fur! They tried to get free, but they could not. They were scared and did not know what to do. A nice lady saw them and helped them. She used a brush to untangle the girl's hair from the dog's fur. They were free! The girl and the dog said, "Thank you!" The lady said, "You're welcome! Now, let's give this smelly dog a bath." After the bath, the dog was not smelly anymore. The girl and the dog became best friends. They played together every day and forgot all about the toy.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play in the kitchen. They find a fork and a lock. They want to see what they can do with them. "Look, Lily, I can put the fork in the lock," Tom says. He tries to turn the fork, but it does not move. "It is stuck. Help me, Lily." Lily tries to pull the fork out of the lock, but it does not come out. "It is too hard, Tom. We need to ask Mom." They run to find Mom. She is in the living room. She is reading a book. She sees the fork and the lock in Tom's hand. "What are you doing with that, Tom?" Mom asks. She is not happy. "That is not a toy. That is a lock for the door. And that is a fork for eating. You could hurt yourself or break something." "Sorry, Mom," Tom says. "We were just playing. We wanted to see if the fork can open the lock. But it did not work. It is stuck. Can you help us?" Mom sighs. She takes the fork and the lock from Tom. She uses a key to open the lock. She frees the fork. She gives them back to Tom. "Here you go, Tom. But please, do not play with these things again. They are not nice. They are dangerous. If you want to play, you can use your toys. They are nice. They are fun. They are safe. Do you understand?" "Yes, Mom," Tom says. He feels sorry. He hugs Mom. "Thank you, Mom. You are nice. You are the best." Lily hugs Mom too. "Yes, thank you, Mom. We love you." Mom smiles. She hugs them back. "I love you too, my sweet twins. Now, go and play nicely. And be careful."

Once upon a time, in a dark room, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was hungry and he wanted to eat a steak. He asked his mom, "Can I have a steak, please?" His mom said, "Yes, you can." Tim was so happy. He went to the kitchen and saw the steak on the table. He wanted to take it to his room, but he didn't want to use his hands. So, he decided to march. He put the steak on his head and started to march. Left, right, left, right, he marched all the way to his room. When he got to his room, he put the steak on a plate and sat down to eat. As he took a bite, he smiled. The steak was very yummy. Tim was very proud of himself for marching with the steak on his head. He finished his meal and went to bed, dreaming of more fun adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom had a coat that he loved very much. It was a big coat with many colors. He wore it every day. One day, Tom met a girl named Sue. Sue was very honest. She always told the truth. Sue saw Tom's coat and said, "I admire your coat. It is very pretty." Tom was happy that Sue liked his coat. Tom and Sue became good friends. They played together every day. They both liked to be honest and kind. And they both liked Tom's coat very much.

- Once upon a time there was an octopus. He was very wide, and loved exploring the ocean. He swam around, looking for something special. One day he saw something glimmering in the sunshine. He swam closer, and saw it was a big, wide shell. Octopus was very excited. He reached out and used his tentacles to try and pick it up. But just then another animal swam up to him. "What are you doing with my special shell?" said the animal. Octopus was surprised. He replied, "I'm just using my tentacles to try and take it." The animal was very pleased. "Thank you for being so careful. You can use it to sit on and rest while you explore the ocean." And so, ever since then, Octopus has been very happy, exploring the ocean on his wide shell.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy dog named Bob. Bob liked to play and run all day. One day, while playing, Bob saw something shiny on the ground. It was a diamond! Bob picked it up and started to follow a path. On the path, Bob saw a little girl named Sue. Sue was crying. Bob wanted to help, so he showed Sue the diamond. Sue smiled and took the diamond. She said, "Thank you, Bob!" Sue and Bob walked together, following the path. As they walked, something unexpected happened. The diamond began to glow! Then, the diamond turned into a big, beautiful butterfly. The butterfly flew away into the sky. Bob and Sue were surprised and laughed. They kept walking and playing, happy to have a new story to tell.

Once upon a time, there was a little gray bunny named Bobo. Bobo lived in a small house in the woods. He had many friends, like the birds and the squirrels. They would play together every day. One day, while playing with his friends, Bobo found a shiny rock. He picked it up and felt a strange power. He began to wonder what the power could do. He showed the rock to his friends, and they all wondered too. Bobo decided to use the power to help his friends. When the birds were hungry, he made food appear. When the squirrels were cold, he made them warm. Everyone was happy with Bobo's new power, and they played together every day, knowing that Bobo would always be there to help them.

Once upon a time, there was a big dragon. The dragon lived in a cave near a small town. The dragon was very rich. He had lots of gold and shiny things in his cave. One day, a little girl named Lily went to the dragon's cave. She was not scared of the dragon. Lily asked the dragon if he could give her some gold to help her family. The dragon said, "I will give you some gold, but you must promise to be my friend." Lily promised to be the dragon's friend. Lily and the dragon played together every day. They had lots of fun. The dragon gave Lily gold for her family, and they were happy. The dragon was happy too because he had a new friend.

Lila was a lonely girl. She had no friends to play with. She lived in a big house with her mom and dad, but they were always busy. Lila liked to make things with thread. She had many colors of thread and a big needle. She made dolls, animals, and flowers with thread. One day, Lila saw a boy outside her window. He was walking with his dog. He had a red hat and a blue shirt. Lila wanted to say hello to him. She ran to the window and waved her hand. But the boy did not see her. He walked away with his dog. Lila felt sad. She wished she had a friend like the boy. She decided to make a gift for him. She took some thread and a needle and made a small dog. She used brown thread for the body, black thread for the eyes and nose, and white thread for the tail. She made the dog look like the boy's dog. The next day, Lila saw the boy again. He was walking with his dog. Lila ran to the window and waved her hand. She also held the thread dog in her other hand. She hoped the boy would see her and her gift. This time, the boy saw her. He saw her waving and smiling. He also saw the thread dog. He was surprised and curious. He stopped and looked at Lila. He said, "Hi, I'm Ben. What's your name?" Lila was happy. She said, "Hi, I'm Lila. I made this for you. It's a dog like yours." Ben smiled. He said, "Wow, thank you. It's very nice. Can I come in and play with you?" Lila nodded. She said, "Yes, please. I have more thread and needles. We can make more things together." Ben agreed. He tied his dog to a tree and ran to the door. Lila opened the door and welcomed him. They went to her room and played with thread. They became friends. Lila was not lonely anymore.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. Yesterday, he had a boring day at home. He wanted to have fun today. He saw his friend, Sam, at the park. They played on the swings and went down the slide. Tim wanted to tell Sam about his boring day yesterday. He said, "Yesterday, I was at home and I was bored." Sam listened to Tim and said, "I had a fun day yesterday. I played with my toys." Tim and Sam played at the park all day. They had so much fun. Tim was happy that today was not like yesterday. He liked playing with Sam and telling him stories.

Once upon a time there lived a bear family. Every day the mama bear, papa bear and the baby bear would go to the forest together. One day they decided to take a walk near the river. The baby bear was so excited when she saw all the colorful rocks near the river. The baby bear wanted to stack them into a big tower and so she put as many rocks together as possible. But every time she tried, the rocks would keep falling. The mama bear saw this and said to the baby bear, "Baby bear, let me show you a trick. To stack the rocks so they don't fall, you have to repeat the same steps. Put one rock on top of the other, then get two rocks and put them on top and keep doing it again and again." The baby bear followed the mama bear's advice and with each step, he repeated the same thing over and over again, making sure all the rocks were stable. In the end, the baby bear was so proud when she saw the colorful stack of rocks. This story is a reminder that practice makes perfect. If you repeat the same steps over and over again, you'll end up with the perfect stack!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to pretend she was a big chef. Lily had a toy kitchen with a jug, a pan, and a spoon. She was very proud of her kitchen. One day, Lily's friend, Ben, came to play. They decided to pretend to make soup. Lily filled the jug with water and poured it into the pan. Ben stirred the soup with the spoon. They laughed and had fun. "Yummy soup!" said Lily. "Do you like it, Ben?" "Yes, I do!" said Ben, smiling. They felt proud of their pretend soup. They played together all day and had a great time in their little kitchen.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy loved to count. She counted everything she saw. One day, Lucy saw a big box of jackets. She wanted to count them all. Lucy started to count the jackets. She put them in a neat and organized line. She counted one, two, three, four, five jackets. Lucy was happy she could count them all. After counting the jackets, Lucy put them back in the box. She was proud of her counting. Lucy told her mom about the jackets she counted. Her mom was very happy too. They both smiled and went to play outside.

Once there was a wise pencil. He was old, but he was still very excited about life. He skipped around the room singing and jigging about. "I'm so excited!" he exclaimed. Suddenly, a three year old child appeared. She was curious about the pencil. "What are you doing?" asked the child. "I'm so excited about life!" the pencil replied. The child was surprised by the pencil's enthusiasm. She wanted to join him. "Can I be excited too?" the child asked. The pencil smiled. "Of course you can! Life is something to be excited about!" So they danced around the room, singing and excitedly celebrating life. They were happy together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a shiny medal that he loved very much. Tim would wear his medal every day and show it to all his friends. One day, when Tim was playing outside, he saw a harmless bug on the ground. He bent down to look at it, and his medal fell off. Tim did not see it drop, so he went back to playing. Later, Tim's friend Max came over to play with him. Max saw the shiny medal on the ground and picked it up. He thought it was a gift for him. Max put the medal around his neck and went to find Tim. When Tim saw Max wearing his medal, he was sad and asked Max to give it back. Max said, "I thought it was a gift for me. I am sorry, Tim." Max gave the medal back to Tim, and they both laughed about the mix-up. Tim and Max played together the rest of the day, and Tim was more careful not to drop his medal again. In the end, Tim and Max became best friends, and they learned to share their toys and medals with each other.

One day, a beautiful bird was flying in the sky. It saw a big brick house. The bird wanted to rest on the house. So, it flew down and sat on the roof. A little girl saw the bird and said, "Hi, bird! You are so beautiful! Will you be my friend?" The bird nodded and sang a song for the girl. They were happy to be friends. The girl went inside her house to get some food for her new friend. But when she came back, the bird was gone. The girl was sad and said, "I miss my beautiful bird friend." She looked around and saw the bird near a big tree. The girl tried to climb the tree to get her friend, but she fell down and got hurt. The bird flew away, and the girl cried. She missed her beautiful bird friend and wished she had been more careful.

Once upon a time, there was a kind king. He lived in a big castle. The king liked to look at the sky. He saw the sun and the clouds. The sky was very pretty. One day, the king went for a walk. He saw a small cat. The cat was lost. The king felt sad for the cat. He picked up the cat and took it to the castle. The cat was very happy. The king and the cat became good friends. They played together every day. The cat made the king feel calm and happy. They looked at the sky together. They lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a poor mommy with a poor baby. The mommy was very worried and sad because she did not have enough money to buy her baby a crib. One day, an angry man saw the baby and his face turned red. He raised his hand and slapped the baby. The poor mommy cried and shook with fear when she saw the man. The angry man stopped and felt ashamed. He knew he shouldn't have slapped the poor baby. He smiled and said he was sorry. He took out some money and handed it to the mommy.
