His heart felt better when he saw her use the money to buy a crib for the baby. The moral of this story is that we should always be kind and never hit anyone, no matter how angry we are.

Once upon a time, there was a little goat. The goat lived on a farm with many friends. The goat had a tight collar around its neck. One day, a kind girl came to the farm. She saw the goat and said, "Oh no! Your collar is too tight! Let me help you." The girl went to the goat and gently rubbed its neck to make it feel better. The goat was very happy and said, "Thank you, nice girl! I feel much better now." The girl and the goat became best friends, and they played together on the farm every day.

One day, a little girl named Daisy went to the park with her mom. Daisy loved the park because it was big and had many fun things to do. She liked to play on the swings, slide, and run around with her friends. But there was one thing Daisy did not like in the park. She hated the loud sounds from the big road near the park. Daisy was playing with her ball when it rolled near the big road. She was scared to go near the loud road, but she wanted her ball back. Daisy saw a boy near the road and asked him for help. "Can you help me get my ball?" Daisy asked the boy. The boy looked at the ball and said, "I don't like the loud road, too. But we can get the ball together." Daisy and the boy held hands and walked to the ball. They were scared, but they were brave together. They got the ball and ran back to the park. Daisy was happy to have her ball back and to make a new friend. They played together for the rest of the day, far away from the loud road.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Abby. She was so excited because it was finally spring. She had been so looking forward to running and playing in the warm sunshine. Every day, Abby would look outside and dream of all the fun she would have outside in the spring. But then one day, her parents said something very important. They said that she couldn't go and play outside until she finished all of her chores. That made Abby very sad and she wanted to go outside and play, but she knew her parents were right. So she began to finish her chores every day and she was so happy when she was finished. At last, spring arrived and Abby was finally done with all of her chores. She ran outside and enjoyed the sunshine and the warm weather. She had so much fun running and playing in the garden. She knew that it was very important to finish her chores, so she can have fun in the spring.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing in the park. The cat was very fast and the dog was very big. They were best friends. They saw a big box with a mystery inside. The cat and the dog wanted to open the box, but their mom warned them not to. The cat and the dog did not listen. They opened the box and found a deaf bird inside. The bird could not hear them. The cat and the dog felt bad for the bird. They wanted to help the bird, but they did not know how. Then, something unexpected happened. The cat and the dog found a magic hat. They put the hat on the bird's head. The bird could hear again! The cat, the dog, and the bird were very happy. They played together all day and became best friends.

"Mom, can I get a pup?" asked Jane. "What kind of pup?" her mom replied. "A golden pup with a fluffy tail," said Jane. Mom thought for a moment and said, "That sounds like a good idea, Jane." The next day Jane and her mom walked into the pet store. As soon as Jane saw the pup, she knew it was the one. She reached up, and carefully picked it up. It felt heavy in her arms. Jane looked at the pup's wide eyes, and said, "Can I keep this one?" The pet shop attendant nodded, and said, "Yes, you can. What are you going to name your new pup?" Jane smiled and said, "I'm going to call him Pupil." Pupil and Jane became fast friends. For the rest of the day they ran around in the park, playing games and having fun. Pupil became a pupil to Jane, learning new tricks, and they both enjoyed their time together.

One Sunday, a colorful car went zoom down the road. A little boy named Tim saw the car and wanted to play with it. The car was very fast, and Tim ran after it. He laughed and clapped his hands as he tried to catch the car. But then, the car stopped. Tim looked at the car and saw that it was not a toy, but a real car. It was just very small. A tiny man came out of the car and waved at Tim. Tim was very surprised. The tiny man asked Tim if he wanted to go for a ride. Tim said yes, and the car grew bigger. Tim and the tiny man went zoom in the colorful car all around the town. They had a lot of fun, and Tim knew that this was the best Sunday ever.

Sam likes to draw with his pen. He draws cars, trees, and stars on his paper. He is very happy when he draws. One day, he goes to the park with his mom. He brings his pen and paper with him. He wants to draw the birds and the flowers. He sits on a bench and starts to draw. "Look, mom, I draw a bird!" he says, showing his mom his paper. "Very good, Sam, you are a great artist!" his mom says, smiling. Sam draws more things on his paper. He is having fun. But then, he drops his pen. He does not see where it falls. He looks under the bench, but he does not find it. He looks around, but he does not see it. He feels sad. He loses his pen. "Mom, I lose my pen!" he says, with tears in his eyes. "Oh, no, Sam, I'm sorry. Maybe we can find it. Let's look together," his mom says, trying to help him. They look for the pen, but they do not find it. Someone else takes it, or it rolls away, or it hides in the grass. Sam does not know. He only knows that he loses his pen. He does not want to draw anymore. He does not want to play anymore. He wants his pen back. "Mom, can we go home?" he asks, with a sour face. "Okay, Sam, we can go home. But don't be too sad. We can buy you a new pen. And you can draw more things with it. Maybe you can draw a rainbow, or a cake, or a dinosaur. What do you think?" his mom says, trying to cheer him up. Sam thinks for a moment. He likes rainbows, and cakes, and dinosaurs. He likes to draw. He feels a little better. "Okay, mom, we can buy a new pen. And I can draw a rainbow, and a cake, and a dinosaur. And I can show you. And you can smile. And I can be happy," he says, with a small smile. "Good, Sam, I'm glad you feel better. You are a brave boy. And I love you very much. And I love your drawings. Come on, let's go home," his mom says, hugging him. They go home, holding hands. Sam still misses his pen, but he knows he can get a new one. And he knows he can draw more things with it. And he knows his mom loves him. And he loves his mom. And he is happy.

Once upon a time, there was a group of friends who wanted to have a fashion show. They wanted to weigh their fashion with a fair measuring stick. So, they all got together and looked around for a way to weigh their clothes. They found some different objects to use, but none of them seemed fair. Suddenly, one of them thought of a brilliant idea. They decided to use a toy scales so that everyone could weigh their own clothing. The friends took turns putting their clothes on one side of the scales, and then added little wooden weights until everything was balanced perfectly. When they were finished, all the outfits were perfectly weighed and it was time for their fashion show! They were so happy when they saw how fair their fashion show had become. All their work had paid off and they had a blast at their fashion show. They cheered and clapped and had so much fun. The end.

Once upon a time, a big fierce dog named Max lived in a small house. Max had a best friend who was a tiny bird named Sunny. They played together every day. One day, Max found a card on the ground. It was a special card that could provide one wish. Max and Sunny talked about what they should wish for. Max wanted a big bone, but Sunny wanted a beautiful nest. They could not agree. Then, a small hungry kitten came by. The kitten was very sad because she had no food. Max and Sunny decided to use the card to provide food for the kitten. The kitten was very happy and thanked them. Max and Sunny learned that it was better to help others than to wish for things for themselves.

One day, a big, bossy cat named Tom went to play. He saw a little bird in a cage on the floor. The bird was sad. Tom said, "Why are you sad, little bird?" The little bird said, "I want to fly, but I am in this cage. Can you help me?" Tom thought for a moment. He wanted to be nice, so he opened the cage and released the bird. The bird was very happy and flew high in the sky. But then, something unexpected happened. The bird came back down and said, "Thank you, Tom, for helping me. Now, I want to help you too." The bird found a big, shiny toy for Tom to play with. Tom was happy and not bossy anymore. The moral of the story is that when you are kind to others, they will be kind to you too.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby cat named Sam. He had soft, velvet fur. Sam lived in a small house with a little girl named Amy. They loved to play together every day. One day, Sam and Amy were playing in the garden. Sam was chasing a butterfly when he heard a whisper. "Help me," said a tiny voice. Sam looked around and saw a small bird stuck in a bush. "Don't worry, little bird, I will help you," Sam whispered back. He gently used his paw to free the bird from the bush. Amy saw Sam helping the bird and was very proud of her chubby, velvet cat. She never expected Sam to help a bird, as cats usually chase them. "Good job, Sam!" said Amy. From that day on, Sam and the little bird became best friends, and they all played together in the garden.

One day, a girl named Mia went to the beach with her mom. Mia loved the beach. She saw a big boat with a big anchor. Mia wanted to touch the anchor, but her mom said, "No, it's too heavy." Mia was sad, but she went to play in the sand. She found a small anchor. Mia was happy. She dug a hole and put the anchor in it. Then, she used her hands to cover it with sand. Mia's mom smiled and said, "Good job, Mia!" A small crab came out of the sand. It was anxious because it lost its home. Mia saw the crab and felt bad. She told the crab, "I'm sorry, I didn't know your home was there." Mia helped the crab find a new home. The crab was happy, and Mia felt good for helping her new friend.

Lily loved ponies. She wanted to see them and touch them and ride them. She asked her mom to take her to the farm where the ponies lived. Her mom said yes and they got in the car. At the farm, Lily saw many ponies. They were brown and black and white and spotted. They had long hair and tails and big eyes. Lily ran to the fence and called to them. "Hello, ponies! Can I pet you? Can I ride you?" But the ponies did not come to her. They ignored her. They ate grass and walked around and napped in the sun. Lily felt sad and angry. Why did the ponies not like her? She wanted to be their friend. She saw a small pony in the corner. It was white with a pink mane and a star on its forehead. It looked at her with curiosity. Lily smiled and walked to it. "Hi, pony. You are very pretty. Can I pet you?" The pony nodded and came closer. It sniffed Lily's hand and licked it. Lily giggled and stroked its soft hair. The pony nuzzled her and made a happy sound. Lily felt happy too. She had found a friend. "Mom, look! This pony likes me! Can I ride it?" Lily asked. Her mom came over and smiled. She saw that the pony was harmless and gentle. She asked the farmer if Lily could ride it. The farmer said yes and helped Lily get on the pony's back. The pony trotted around the farm with Lily holding its mane. Lily laughed and waved to the other ponies. They looked at her and wondered. Maybe she was not so bad after all.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived an elderly bunny named Mr. Fluffy. Mr. Fluffy loved to hop and play all day long. He was very happy. One day, Mr. Fluffy found a pen in the grass. He picked it up and thought, "I can use this to draw pretty pictures!" Mr. Fluffy hopped back to his house with the pen. In his house, Mr. Fluffy met his friend, Little Bunny. Little Bunny saw the pen and said, "Wow, a pen! Can I try too?" Mr. Fluffy nodded and they both started to draw. They drew many pictures together. They drew the sun, the moon, and the stars. They laughed and had a lot of fun. At the end of the day, Mr. Fluffy and Little Bunny were tired. They put the pen away and said, "That was a great day!" Then they hopped into their beds and slept, dreaming of more fun days to come.

One day, a little caterpillar named Bob was very frustrated. He wanted to go to a big tree far away. Bob tried to walk fast, but he was so slow. He was sad because he wanted to arrive at the tree soon. Then, a big bird named Tim saw Bob. Tim wanted to help Bob. So, Tim picked up Bob with his beak and flew to the big tree. Bob was so happy to be in the air. He thought he would arrive at the tree very fast. But, something unexpected happened. Tim took Bob to a different tree! It was not the tree Bob wanted to go to. The tree was full of tasty leaves, and Bob was not frustrated anymore. He made new friends and was happy in his new home.

Once upon a time, there was a fisherman named Tom. Tom liked to print pictures of fish. He had a delicate touch when he printed, so the pictures looked very nice. One day, Tom went to the sea to catch some fish. He saw a big fish and a little fish. He caught the big fish, but let the little fish go. The little fish swam away, happy to be free. Tom went home and printed a picture of the big fish he caught. He showed the picture to his friends, and they all liked it. Tom was happy, and he kept on being a good fisherman.

Ben was a young boy who liked to draw. He had many notes with his drawings on them. He kept them in a big box under his bed. He was proud of his notes and did not want to share them with anyone. One day, his friend Lily came to play with him. She saw his box and asked him what was inside. Ben said it was his notes and he did not want to show them. Lily felt sad and asked him why. Ben said they were his and he did not have to share them. Lily said that was not nice and that friends should share. Ben did not listen to Lily and told her to go away. Lily left and did not want to play with him anymore. Ben felt lonely and bored. He looked at his notes and realized they were not fun without someone to see them and say nice things. He wished he had been kind to Lily and shared his notes with her. He decided to call Lily and say sorry. He told her he was wrong and he wanted to share his notes with her. Lily was happy and came back to play with him. They looked at his notes and had fun. Ben learned that sharing is good and that it makes friends happy. He and Lily became good friends and kept drawing more notes together.

Danny saw an orange motorcycle at the park. He thought it looked really fun and wished he could have it. Danny's mom told him that he was too young and couldn't get it. Danny was very sad and started to cry. Danny and his mom kept walking around the park. His mom looked around and saw something in one of the gardens. It was a long yellow motorcylce with a big green bow. Danny was so excited. His mom said it was the perfect match for Danny. Danny was so happy and hugged his mom. They quickly put the motorcycle in the car and went home. Danny couldn't wait to show off his new ride. Danny has been riding his new motorcycle ever since and is never too far away.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little girl named Jane. She was always full of wonder and asked lots of questions. One day, her mummy took her to the post office to mail a special letter. Jane had never mail a letter before and it made her feel very troubled. Mummy smiled and said "It's ok Jane, it's very simple. You just need to give the letter to the nice lady at the counter and she'll do the rest." Jane was still feeling troubled, but she did as Mummy said and gave the letter to the lady. The lady smiled at Jane and said, "This is going to make someone very happy!" Then, Jane and Mummy walked home. On the way, Jane asked lots of questions about mailing a letter and Mummy was so proud that Jane was so full of wonder. Jane and Mummy both felt happy and content knowing that the letter was now on its way to make someone very happy.

One day, a beautiful cat named Lily went to a food place with her friend, a dog named Max. They were very hungry and needed to eat. They sat down and looked at the menu to see what they could eat. Lily said, "I need some fish. It is my favorite." Max said, "I need a big bone to eat. I love bones." They told the nice person who worked there what they wanted. But then, something unexpected happened! The nice person brought them the wrong food. Lily got the big bone and Max got the fish. They looked at each other and laughed. Then they decided to try each other's food. And guess what? They both liked it! They found out that trying new things can be fun.

Jill and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big white house with a fancy gate. Jill wanted to go inside and look around. Tom was scared. "Let's go see the house," Jill said. "It looks nice and pretty." "No, we can't," Tom said. "It's not our house. Maybe someone lives there. They might be angry if we go in." "Are you a baby?" Jill asked. "I dare you to go with me. It will be fun." Tom did not like being called a baby. He did not want to lose the dare. He followed Jill to the gate. They pushed it open and walked into the yard. There were many flowers and trees. They heard a dog barking. "See, it's not so bad," Jill said. "Let's go to the door." They ran to the door and knocked. No one answered. Jill tried to open the door. It was locked. "Let's go back," Tom said. "This is wrong. We should not be here." But Jill did not listen. She saw a window that was open. She climbed on a chair and looked inside. She saw a big room with many toys and books. She wanted to play with them. "Wow, look at all these things," Jill said. "Let's go inside and play." She jumped through the window and landed on the floor. Tom was very scared. He did not want to go inside. He heard the dog barking louder. He saw a car coming into the driveway. "Jill, come back," Tom shouted. "Someone is coming. We have to go." But Jill did not hear him. She was busy playing with a doll and a train. She did not see the door opening. She did not see the angry man who lived in the house. She did not see the big dog that ran towards her. Tom saw everything. He was very sorry he followed Jill. He wished he had said no to the dare. He wished they had stayed in the park. He wished they had never seen the white house with the fancy gate.

Once upon a time, there was a cat named Max. Max liked to stretch in the sun. One day, Max saw a stranger walking in his yard. The stranger was a big dog. Max was scared, but the dog just wanted to play. The dog was very persistent. He kept coming back to the yard to play with Max. Max did not want to play with the stranger. Max's friend, a bird, told Max that maybe the dog was not so bad. Max thought about it and decided to give it a try. The next day, Max stretched in the sun and waited for the dog. When the stranger came, Max played with the dog. They had so much fun! Max and the dog became best friends. Max learned that sometimes, new friends can be found in the most unexpected places.

The young girl was playing in the park when she saw a bird. She looked up at the sky and said to her mother, "Look at that bird, mom!" Her mother smiled and then mentioned something interesting. "You know, that bird is a very rare species. It only visits here once a year!" The young girl was amazed, so she looked up and said, "Wow! It's so beautiful looking at the sky." Mother nodded and said, "Yes, it's wonderful to watch the sky. You can learn a lot if you look up and observe nature." The little girl agreed and said, "What else is up there in the sky?" She placed her hand over her eyes to get a better view and then noticed a few white and fluffy clouds. Her mother smiled and said, "Those clouds are called cumulus clouds. They tell us the weather will be nice today." The little girl smiled and looked back up at the sky, feeling very small and yet learning something new each time she did.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue wanted to decorate her room. She had many colorful papers, glue, and a big smile on her face. Sue put glue on the papers and stuck them on the wall. She made a big sun, a happy tree, and pretty flowers. Sue's room looked so beautiful with her decorations. One day, Sue's mom made a spicy soup for lunch. Sue tasted it and said, "Wow, this soup is spicy!" They all laughed and enjoyed the soup together. Sue was happy with her decorated room and the spicy soup.

Once upon a time, in a regular little town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside with his friends. They would run, jump, and laugh all day long. Tim was happy. One day, while they were playing near the wake of a small river, Tim saw something strange. It was a small, shiny stone. He picked it up and showed it to his friends. They all looked at it, amazed. Tim decided to keep the stone. Later, when Tim was alone, he held the stone and made a wish. He wished for a big, tasty ice cream. Suddenly, the ice cream appeared! Tim was so surprised. He ate the ice cream and was very happy. But when he looked back at the stone, it began to vanish. Tim was sad to see it go, but he knew that he had a magical day.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. Tim saw a huge tree with lots of wood. He wanted to get some wood to build a fort. Tim said, "I need help to get wood from the tree." A big bird heard Tim and said, "I can help you get wood." The bird flew up and down, taking wood from the tree. Tim was happy and said, "Thank you, bird! Now I can build my fort." But, when Tim started to build his fort, the wood changed into toys! Tim was surprised and said, "Wow! This is not wood, these are toys!" The bird came back and said, "I made the wood into toys for you to play with!" Tim smiled and played with his new toys all day long.

Mommy was tired. She wanted to decorate the room to make it look more special. She knew what to do: add lots of jazz! Mommy went to the store to get some things. She bought some colorful balloons and big streamers. She also got some special glittery stars. When she got home, she was so excited to start decorating. She hung the streamers by the windows and taped the glittery stars on the walls. Then, she filled the balloons with air and tied them together. Finally, Mommy was done and the room looked so fun and bright. She was happy, and ready to take a break. All her hard work was worth it!

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Tim. Tim was a youth who liked to play outside in the mild sun. He had many friends, and they all liked to play together. One day, Tim and his friends were playing near a big door. They were having so much fun running and laughing. But then, Tim saw the door start to close. He knew he had to act fast to keep it open. Tim ran as fast as he could and put his hands on the door. With all his strength, he pushed to keep the door from closing. His friends saw what he was doing and came to help. Together, they pushed the door open and saved the day. They all cheered and continued playing, happy that they were able to keep the door open.

One day, a little boy named Tim and his dog, Spot, went on a walk. They saw a high mountain far away. Tim said, "Let's get to the top of the mountain, Spot!" On their way, they met a girl named Sue. Sue said, "I want to go too!" So, Tim, Spot, and Sue walked to the high mountain together. They went up and up. As they got near the top, it was very cold. Tim said, "I am cold." Sue said, "Me too." They did not have warm clothes. They had to go back down the mountain. They were sad they did not get to the top.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy lived near a large lake, and every night she would see a tour boat go past. All the people on the tour boat looked so happy, and Daisy felt envious of them. One evening, Daisy decided that she wanted to go on the tour boat. But the tour boat was broken. So Daisy set to work to try and restore it. She worked day and night, and eventually she managed to get it fixed. When Daisy was finished, she invited all her family and friends to take a tour of the lake with her on the boat. Everyone was so excited and happy to go. Daisy and her family and friends enjoyed the boat ride. Everyone laughed and smiled as the boat sailed around the lake, taking in the beautiful scenery. When the tour was over, everyone thanked Daisy for her hard work and for restoring the boat. Daisy knew that this was an experience she would remember forever.

Once upon a time, there was a yellow duck. She loved to spring around the pond and paddle around in the sunshine. One fine day, the yellow duck was out in the sun paddling around when she noticed something very strange. It was an orange juice that had sprung up on the edge of the pond. She squinted to make sure she wasn't dreaming. She hopped over to take a closer look. "Hi there! What are you doing here?" she asked the orange juice. The orange juice chuckled and said, "I'm just here for a holiday! I wanted to get some sun and meet new friends, like you!" The yellow duck was so excited and couldn't believe her luck. "Let's play together!" she said as she began to paddle around happily with the orange juice. They had so much fun playing together, and the hours passed in a flash. As the day ended, the yellow duck and the orange juice said goodbye and went their separate ways. The yellow duck couldn't wait to see her new friend again, so they could play together in the spring sunshine.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see an old man. He is jogging. He has a red hat and a blue shirt. "Look, Ben, he is fast!" Anna says. "Yes, he is. Do you want to jog with him?" Ben asks. Anna nods. They run after the old man. They say hello. The old man smiles. He stops jogging. "Hello, kids. Do you like jogging?" he asks. "Yes, we do. It is fun. You are good at jogging. How do you do it?" Anna says. The old man laughs. He points to his hat. "This is my secret. It is a magic hat. It makes me strong and happy. Do you want to try it?" he says. Anna and Ben are curious. They nod. The old man takes off his hat. He wraps it around Anna's head. Then he wraps it around Ben's head. They feel warm and cozy. "Wow, this is a nice hat. Thank you, mister," Anna says. "You're welcome, dear. Now you can jog faster and longer. But remember, the hat only works if you share it with others. That is the magic," the old man says. Anna and Ben smile. They hug the old man. They say thank you. They give him back his hat. They jog together. They share the hat with other kids. They make new friends. They have a lot of fun. The old man watches them. He is happy. He jogs away. He waves goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man who had a lot of shrimp. Every day he would go out into the sea and catch more shrimp. He was very good at catching them, and he was very kind too. One day, the elderly man went to buy some supplies at the market. He saw a nice little girl and asked her if she wanted some of his shrimp. The little girl was excited and said yes please! She went home and cooked the shrimp for her family. Her mum and dad said it was delicious! The little girl was very happy and thanked the elderly man for his kind and generous gift. From then on, the elderly man and the little girl were good friends. Whenever he went to the market, he would bring her some shrimp. They both enjoyed the time they spent together.

One day, a boy named Tim found a big board in his room. He thought it was fun to draw on the board. Tim was a little careless and made a big mess with the colors. He wanted to show his friends what he did, so he asked his mom for help. Mom came and saw the messy board. She had an idea to record Tim's drawing with her phone. Tim was very happy and excited. He stood next to the board and smiled while Mom recorded him. After Mom recorded Tim with the board, she showed him the video. Tim loved it and said thank you to his mom. He promised to be more careful next time when he draws. Now, Tim can show his friends his drawing and the video too.

Once upon a time, a cheerful player was asked to deliver something special. He was so excited! He went out on a journey to the store to buy the item. It was a long road, but he was looking forward to the task because it made him feel important. When he arrived at the store, the player found the item he needed. He was so happy that he delivered it with a big smile. On his way back to deliver the item, he met a lot of people. Everyone was so nice. They gave him cheerful smiles and said 'hello'. Finally, he arrived at the place where he needed to deliver the item. The person was so thankful and grateful. He gave the player a big hug and thanked him from the bottom of his heart. The journey was over and the player was glad he had done something good.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Pokie. Pokie had big ears that he loved to poke. One day, Pokie met a new friend, a tiny bird named Tweetie. Tweetie also liked to poke things with her beak. "Hi, I'm Tweetie," said the bird, "I like to poke things too! Can I poke your ear?" "Sure!" said Pokie, "But be gentle, my ears are important to me." Tweetie poked Pokie's ear very gently. They both laughed and played together. From that day on, Pokie and Tweetie became best friends. They poked many things together, but always remembered to be gentle with each other's important parts.

Once upon a time, in a lovely little house, there was a tiny mouse. The mouse had a friend, a big cat. They liked to play together. One day, the mouse said to the cat, "Can I borrow your ball to play with?" The cat said, "Yes, you can borrow my ball. Let's play together!" They played all day with the ball. The mouse and the cat were very happy. They had lots of fun together. And they shared many more toys in their lovely little house.

One day, a little boy named Tim did not like his toy. It was a model car. He said, "I hate this car." He was very sad. A girl named Sue saw Tim. She was very good at fixing things. Sue said, "I can help you." She was very persistent. She did not give up. Sue took the model car and fixed it. Now, the model car could talk! It said, "Thank you, Sue." Tim was so happy. He did not hate the car anymore. The car became Tim's best friend. They played together every day.

One day, a warm and big sun came out. A little boy named Tim saw a post in the ground. The post had a red ball on top. Tim wanted to play with the red ball. Tim said, "Ball, come down! I want to play with you!" The red ball heard Tim and jumped off the post. Tim and the red ball played and had fun. But then, something strange happened. The red ball started to get smaller and smaller. Tim was sad and said, "Ball, where are you going?" The red ball did not say anything. It just got smaller and smaller until it vanished. Tim looked around for the ball, but it was gone. He felt sad, but then he saw a new green ball on the post. Tim smiled and said, "Hello, green ball! Let's play!"

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they go to the lake with their moms. The lake is big and blue. There are ducks and fish in the lake. Anna and Ben have a ball. They throw the ball to each other. They have fun. But then, Ben sees a boat. He wants to go on the boat. He runs to the boat. He says to Anna, "Come with me!" Anna does not want to go on the boat. She is scared of the boat. She likes the ball. She says to Ben, "No, thank you. I want to play with the ball." Ben does not listen to Anna. He ignores her. He gets on the boat. He says to Anna, "Bye-bye!" Anna is sad. She is alone. She has the ball, but no one to play with. She looks at the lake. The lake is quiet. She hears the ducks and the fish. She wishes Ben was with her. Then, she sees another girl. The girl is near the lake. She has a bucket and a shovel. She is making a sand castle. She smiles at Anna. She says, "Hi! Do you want to play with me?" Anna smiles back. She says, "Yes, please. I want to play with you." She runs to the girl. She gives her the ball. She says, "I am Anna. What is your name?" The girl says, "I am Lily. Nice to meet you, Anna." They play with the ball, the bucket and the shovel. They make a big sand castle. They have fun. Anna and Lily are friends. They do not ignore each other. They share and take turns. They are happy. They like the lake.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot had an itch on his back. The itch made him feel uncomfortable. He tried to scratch it, but his paws were too short. He felt sad. One day, Spot saw a door. The door was locked. Spot wanted to see what was behind the door. He thought maybe he could find something to help with his itch. He tried to unlock the door, but he could not. He needed a key. Spot looked around and found a key under a rock. He was very happy. He used the key to unlock the door. Inside, he found a big, soft brush. Spot used the brush to scratch his itch. The uncomfortable itch went away. Spot was happy and wagged his tail.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Spring. Spring loved to jump and play in the pastel green grass. Every day, Spring would hop around, feeling happy and free. One day, Spring felt anxious. He saw a big, dark cloud in the sky. He decided to hide under a big tree. As he hid, he saw other animals running away. Spring thought they were playing a game, so he joined them. As Spring played, the dark cloud made a loud noise. It started to rain, and the rain turned into a big storm. Spring and his friends got wet and cold. They all wished they had stayed home. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a furry cat. The cat liked to play in the garden. One day, the cat heard a sound. It was a cricket. The cricket could whistle a pretty song. The cat and the cricket became friends. They played and had fun. The cricket taught the cat how to whistle too. They whistled songs together. The cat was happy. One day, another cat came. The new cat wanted to catch the cricket. The furry cat said, "No, the cricket is my friend." The new cat learned that being friends is better than being mean. They all played and whistled songs together. And they lived happily ever after. The moral of the story is to be kind and make friends.

Once upon a time there was a little bunny. The bunny lived in a oasis that was far away. He was very thoughtful and kind. One day, the bunny went out on a hike. He hopped and skipped through the oasis until he came to a clearing. In the clearing there was a big snake. The snake saw the bunny and said, “Hello there, little bunny.” The bunny was scared and he jumped back. The snake said, “Don’t be scared. I just want to be your friend.” The bunny thought about it for a moment and decided that the snake was right—maybe the snake could be his friend. So the bunny and the snake became friends. They talked for a long time and then the snake said, “Let’s go for a walk.” So the bunny and the snake walked through the oasis and talked some more. After a while, the bunny noticed that the snake was acting strange. The snake was getting closer to him and the bunny started to get scared. Suddenly, the snake opened his mouth and tried to bite the bunny! Luckily, the bunny was too quick for the snake and he hopped out of the way. The bunny was very lucky, but he knew he had to be more careful next time. He was thankful that he had been so thoughtful when he first met the snake.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a man in a suit. He looked serious. He had a big bag with him. "Who is he?" Lily asked Ben. "I don't know. Maybe he works in a big building," Ben said. The man put his bag on a bench. He took out a phone and started to talk. He did not see Lily and Ben. Lily and Ben were curious. They wanted to see what was in the bag. They ran to the bench. They grabbed the bag. They opened it. "Wow, look at this!" Lily said. She pulled out a red hat. She put it on her head. "And this!" Ben said. He pulled out a blue scarf. He wrapped it around his neck. They laughed. They looked funny. The man finished his talk. He turned around. He saw Lily and Ben with his bag. He was angry. "Hey, what are you doing? Give me back my bag!" he shouted. Lily and Ben were scared. They dropped the bag. They ran away. "Sorry, mister!" they said. They ran back to their mom. They told her what happened. She was not happy. "You should not grab things that are not yours. That is not nice. You could have made the man sad or mad," she said. Lily and Ben felt sorry. They learned a lesson. They said they would not do it again. They hugged their mom. She hugged them back. She loved them.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful bird. The bird had many colors, like red, blue, and yellow. The bird liked to fly and sing. One day, the bird saw a bike with a handle. The bird wanted to try and balance on the handle. So, the bird flew down and landed on the handle. It was hard at first, but the bird learned to balance. The bird was happy on the bike handle. It sang a pretty song for everyone to hear. People saw the beautiful bird and smiled. The bird made friends and had fun balancing on the handle. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was an attractive fisherman who lived by the lake. Every day he would take out his boat and put his fishing nets in the lake. He loved counting the fish he caught and could tell you the number of each kind of fish he caught. One day, he saw another fisherman near the lake. He asked the other fisherman what kind of fish he had caught. The other fisherman said he hadn't caught any. The fisherman was annoyed because the other fisherman was taking up his fishing spot. He said, "You're taking my spot, why don't you just leave?" The other fisherman said, "I'm not leaving until I get at least one fish!" The fisherman thought for a moment and then told the other fisherman, "Here's a deal. I'll give you one fish, if you leave now." The other fisherman agreed and took the fish. The attractive fisherman was happy to have the lake to himself again. Every day he could now go back to counting the fish he caught - it was far more enjoyable than arguing with the other fisherman!

Once upon a time, there was a big open park. In the park, there was a little girl named Susie. Susie liked to play and dance in the park. One day, a stranger came to the park. The stranger was tall and had a big smile. The stranger saw Susie dancing and started to clap his hands. The stranger wanted to applaud Susie because she was so good at dancing. Susie was happy that the stranger liked her dance. She smiled and danced even more. Then, Susie's mom came to the park. She saw the stranger applauding Susie. Susie's mom was not happy. She told Susie not to talk to strangers. Susie learned that it is good to be careful with strangers. The stranger was nice, but it is always better to be safe. And that was the day Susie learned a very important lesson.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a happy boy who loved to play with his toys. One day, Tim saw his mom prepare food for dinner. He wanted to help her, but he was too small. Tim felt a bit ashamed that he could not help his mom. Tim thought about how he could help his mom. He decided to use his body to do something nice for her. Tim picked up his toys and put them away. He also helped set the table for dinner. His mom was very happy to see him help. At dinner, Tim's mom told him that she was proud of him. She said, "Tim, you used your body to help, and you should not feel ashamed. You are a big help to me." Tim smiled and felt very happy. From that day on, Tim always tried to help his mom whenever he could.

One day, Tom and Sue were playing in their room. They heard a loud noise coming from the ceiling. Tom said, "What is that noise?" Sue said, "I don't know. Let's find out!" Tom and Sue went to their closet and found a small door. They opened the door and saw a ladder. They climbed the ladder and found a tiny room. It was dark, but they could see a little light coming from a hole. Tom decided to peek through the hole and saw a big bird making the loud noise. He told Sue, "It's a bird! It's singing a song!" Sue peeked too and they both smiled. They listened to the bird's song and then went back to their room to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat bananas. One day, he found a banana on the floor. It was brown and squishy. Tim thought it was disgusting. He showed the banana to his friend, Sam. Sam looked at the banana and said, "Ew! That's disgusting! Don't eat it!" Tim didn't listen to Sam. He thought the banana would still taste good. Tim took a big bite of the disgusting banana. He started to shout, "Yuck! This is so bad!" Sam told him, "I told you not to eat it!" Tim's tummy hurt a lot. He was sad that he didn't listen to his friend.

One day, a little girl named Mia went to the sea with her mom. They saw a small, harmless fish near the water. Mia wanted to look at the fish more closely. She asked her mom, "Can I examine the fish, please?" Her mom said, "Yes, but be careful not to scare it." Mia went closer to the fish and looked at it. She saw that it had pretty colors and a cute face. Mia was very happy. Suddenly, the harmless fish started to grow bigger and bigger. Mia and her mom were very surprised. They didn't know that the fish could do that. The big fish looked at them and said, "Thank you for being nice to me. I am a magic fish. I will give you one wish." Mia and her mom smiled and thought about what they would wish for.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was an independent dog who loved to run and play. One day, he saw a sign that said "Big Race Today." Spot thought, "I want to win that race!" Spot went to the race and saw many other dogs. They all had a strong look. Spot was a bit scared, but he knew he had to try. Before the race, Spot met a big dog named Max. Max said, "You are too small. You can't win." But Spot didn't listen. He knew he could do it. The race began, and all the dogs ran very fast. Spot ran as fast as he could. He remembered Max's words, but he kept going. In the end, Spot won the race! All the other dogs were amazed. Max said, "I was wrong. You are a great runner." Spot was very happy and proud that he didn't give up.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to nap on a soft patch of grass under a big tree. Every day, he would go to his favorite spot and lay down for a nap. One day, Spot saw a big, ignorant cat named Fluffy. Fluffy did not know about Spot's favorite patch. Fluffy walked over and laid down on the patch. Spot did not like this. He wanted to nap on his patch all by himself. Spot walked over to Fluffy and said, "This is my patch! Please go away!" But Fluffy did not listen. Spot felt sad, but then he had a good idea. He found a new, even better patch under another tree. Spot and Fluffy both napped happily in their own patches from that day on.

Once upon a time, there was a funny bunny named Bob. One day, Bob went out to wander in the woods. He hopped and hopped until he found a big tree. The tree had many pears on it. Bob liked pears a lot. Bob saw a squirrel named Sam in the tree. Sam said, "Hi Bob! Do you want a pear?" Bob said, "Yes, please!" So, Sam threw a pear down to Bob. Bob ate the pear and it was very yummy. Bob and Sam played and shared more pears. They had a great day together. The moral of the story is that sharing with friends is fun and kind.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable cow named Daisy. Daisy lived on a farm with her friend, a little boy named Tim. They loved to play together in the big green field. One day, Tim wanted to measure Daisy to see how big she was. He took a long piece of string and wrapped it around Daisy. "Wow, Daisy, you are so big!" Tim said. Daisy just smiled and mooed happily. Just then, a big gust of wind came and lifted Daisy up into the air! Tim was very surprised. He held onto the string and started to fly with Daisy. They went on a fun adventure in the sky and saw many new things. After their adventure, the wind gently put them back down in the field. Tim and Daisy laughed and knew they would always remember their special day.

Once upon a time, there was a big horse named Bob. Bob was a serious horse who liked to serve people. He had a job to help people go from one place to another. One day, Bob met a small cat named Tom. Tom was very sad because he lost his toy. Bob wanted to help Tom find his toy. They went to many places to look for the toy, but they could not find it. Tom was still sad. Then, Bob had an idea. He took Tom to a big tree. At the top of the tree, they saw the toy! Bob used his long legs to reach the toy and gave it back to Tom. Tom was very happy and thanked Bob for his help. They became best friends and went on many more adventures together.

Once upon a time, there were two friends out for a walk. They were called Missy and Joe. As they were walking, Missy saw a rod lying on the ground. "Look Joe, what's that?" she said, pointing at the rod. "That looks heavy. Let me touch it!" said Joe, moving closer to the rod. He bent down and touched it. The rod suddenly moved and flew out of Joe's hand. Joe yelled in surprise and stepped back. Missy laughed. "I think that rod was alive!" she said. Joe looked worried. He said he had never seen anything like this before. Missy smiled and said, "Maybe we can find out more if we keep looking, buddy." So, the two friends continued their walk, looking carefully and wondering what they might discover.

Once upon a time there was a small stay. It was very happy in its home. One day, it went for a walk in the park. On this walk, it met some new friends. When it was done playing, it was getting late and it was time for the stay to go home. On this walk back, it started to get dark and the stay began to feel scared. Then it saw a small light in the dark. It began to move closer and it knew it was a kind face that it had seen before. It was very happy to know this friendly face. The friendly face said that it can stay with him and the stay was so relieved. It was glad it knew someone who could keep it safe and it stayed with them ever since. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to play with her toys and keep them organized. One day, Lucy made a network of toy roads in her room. She was very happy. Lucy's friend, Tim, came over to play. They played with the network of roads and had lots of fun. But then, Tim broke one of the roads by accident. Lucy was sad and said, "Tim, you broke my road!" Tim felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Lucy. I didn't mean to break it. Can you forgive me?" Lucy thought for a moment and decided to forgive Tim. They fixed the road together and continued to play. They had a great day, and Lucy was happy that she forgave Tim.

One morning, a little boy was eager to dress for the day. He put on his shirt, his shorts and his shoes. Then he noticed something strange--a tiny green frog hopping around his room. He was so excited. He quickly put on his hat and grabbed the frog. He ran outside with the frog and giggled as he watched it hop around the yard. The boy and the frog explored the garden and the pond. They talked to the bugs and the birds. The little boy was so happy. When the sun began to set, the frog said goodbye and hopped away. The boy was sad to see the frog go, but he was also excited for the next time he could dress and explore with his friend.

Once upon a time, there was a tutor named Miss Bee. She was different because she had a big, round nose. Miss Bee loved to teach little kids how to read and write. One day, while Miss Bee was teaching, a little boy named Tim saw her big, round nose. He wanted to poke it. So, Tim walked up to Miss Bee and poked her nose. Miss Bee was surprised and said, "Oh, Tim! Why did you poke my nose?" Tim said, "I'm sorry, Miss Bee. Your nose is different, and I wanted to see if it was soft." Miss Bee laughed and said, "That's okay, Tim. But next time, just ask if you want to touch something." Tim learned his lesson and never poked anyone again. They all lived happily ever after.

Anna liked to play in the garden with her toys. She had a doll, a ball, a car and a book. She also liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. She saw a bee on a yellow flower. The bee was black and yellow and had wings. Anna wanted to touch the bee. She thought the bee was pretty and friendly. She asked her mom if she could touch the bee. Her mom said no. She said the bee could hurt Anna if she touched it. She said the bee had a sharp thing on its back that could make Anna cry. She said Anna should leave the bee alone and play with her toys. Anna was sad. She did not understand why the bee could hurt her. She still wanted to touch the bee. She waited until her mom was busy in the kitchen. She went back to the garden. She saw the bee on another flower. The flower was gray and had no smell. Anna thought the flower was ugly and boring. She wondered why the bee liked it. She reached out her hand to touch the bee. She did not see the sharp thing on the bee's back. She did not hear the bee's buzz. The bee felt Anna's hand on its body. The bee was scared and angry. It did not like to be touched by a big hand. It thought the hand was a danger. It used its sharp thing to sting Anna's hand. Anna felt a sharp pain in her hand. She screamed and let go of the bee. She ran to her mom and showed her the red spot on her hand. She cried and said the bee hurt her. Her mom hugged her and said she was sorry. She said she told Anna not to touch the bee. She said the bee stung Anna because it was afraid. She said the gray flower was not a real flower. It was a trap for the bee. It had a sweet thing inside that the bee liked. But it also had a poison that made the bee sick. She said the bee would die soon. She said Anna should not touch the trap either. She said Anna should listen to her mom and be careful in the garden. Anna nodded and said she was sorry. She said she learned her lesson. She said she would not touch the bee or the trap again. She said she loved her mom and her toys. She said she did not like the gray flower.

Once upon a time, there was a red candle. The red candle lived in a small house with a little girl named Lily. Lily loved the red candle very much. Every night, she would light the red candle and watch its light dance on the walls. One day, the red candle began to worry. It was getting smaller and smaller. The red candle did not want to go away. It wanted to stay with Lily forever. That night, when Lily came to light the red candle, she saw that it was very small. "Don't worry, red candle," said Lily. "I will find a way to keep you with me forever." Lily thought and thought. Then, she had a great idea. She took the red candle to her mom, who helped her make a beautiful drawing of the red candle. Now, even when the red candle was too small to light, Lily could look at the drawing and remember her friend. And the red candle never had to worry again.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful dog named Max. Max liked to watch TV every day. He liked to watch shows with other dogs running and playing. Max was very happy when he watched TV. One day, Max was watching TV when something unexpected happened. The TV stopped working! Max was sad and didn't know what to do. He tried to fix the TV, but he couldn't. Max didn't want to give up, but he knew he needed help. Max decided to surrender and ask his friend, a little bird named Lucy, for help. Lucy was very smart and knew how to fix things. Lucy looked at the TV and found a button Max didn't know about. She pushed the button and the TV started working again! Max was so happy and thanked Lucy for her help. They watched TV together and had a great time.

One day, a boy named Tim went with his mom to a big hotel. They were very happy to be there. The hotel was very tall and had many rooms. Tim and his mom went to their room and put their bags down. They were hungry, so they went to find food. They went to a room with food and saw a man cooking. The man said, "Hello! I have some spicy food for you!" Tim and his mom looked at the food. It was red and smelled very good. They took some and went back to their room. When they started to eat, Tim's mom said, "Oh no! This food is too spicy for you, Tim." Tim looked at the food and thought, "I can try it." He took a small bite and his face turned red. "It is spicy, but I like it!" Tim said. Just then, they heard a knock on the door. It was the man who cooked the food. He said, "I made a mistake. That food was not meant for you. I have some other food that is not spicy." Tim and his mom were surprised but happy to eat the new food. They thanked the man and enjoyed their meal together.

Once upon a time, there was a bright spot in the sky. It was a delicate spot that sparkled and glowed with beauty. It was so beautiful that everyone wanted to look at it all the time. Down on the ground, the animals stopped their chatter and peered up at the sky. What was that spot? Suddenly, there was a loud roar that filled the air. It sounded like thunder, much louder than usual, and the animals were scared. But then the animals heard a voice. "Welcome, everyone," the voice said. "Do not be afraid. I am the bright spot in the sky that you all can see." The animals cheered and welcomed this mysterious spot. They knew it was something special! The next day, the spot in the sky kept growing bigger and brighter. Until finally, the delicate spot roared and lit up the sky with a brilliant light. The animals called it a miracle. And from then on, every day the spot in the sky would roar and light up the sky with love and joy.

One day, a boy named Tim found a video. The video was boring, but he wanted to watch it. Tim asked his mom to explain the video to him. His mom said, "This video is about a man who talks a lot but does nothing fun." Tim wanted to make the video fun. So, he and his mom thought of a game. They would listen to the man and make funny faces when he said a boring word. Tim and his mom laughed a lot while playing the game. In the end, Tim learned that even boring things can be fun with a little imagination. He thanked his mom for explaining the video and making it fun. They hugged each other and laughed some more.

Sam was a restless kid. He liked to run and jump and play all day. He did not like to sit still or be quiet. One day, he was bored at home. He wanted to have some fun. He saw his mom's purse on the table. He thought it had many interesting things inside. He wanted to see what they were. He grabbed the purse and ran to his room. He opened the purse and dumped everything on the floor. He found a shiny key, a red lipstick, a soft scarf, and a small phone. He tried the key on his door, but it did not fit. He put the lipstick on his face, but it tasted bad. He wrapped the scarf around his neck, but it was too hot. He pressed the phone, but it did not make any sound. He was not happy. He wanted something else. He searched the purse again, but he did not find anything more. He heard his mom calling his name. He was scared. He knew he did something wrong. He hid under his bed with the purse. "Sam, where are you?" his mom asked. She came to his room and saw the mess on the floor. She was angry. She looked under the bed and saw Sam. "Sam, what did you do?" she asked. "Sorry, mom. I was bored. I wanted to play with your things," Sam said. "Sam, you can't play with my things. They are not toys. They are important. You could have lost them or broken them. You have to ask me first. Do you understand?" his mom said. "Yes, mom. I understand. I'm sorry. I won't do it again," Sam said. His mom hugged him and forgave him. She helped him clean up the mess. She gave him his own toy phone and key. She told him to play with them instead. Sam was happy. He learned his lesson. He played with his own things and did not touch his mom's purse again.

Once upon a time, there was a small frog named Tim. Tim lived by a pond with very good water. One day, Tim saw his friend, Ben the bunny, with a hurt leg. "Ben, what happened?" asked Tim. Ben said, "I fell and hurt my leg. It feels very bad." Tim thought about how to help Ben heal. He remembered the good water in the pond. Tim said, "Ben, let's go to the pond. The good water can help you heal." Ben hopped to the pond with Tim. They put Ben's hurt leg in the water. After some time, Ben's leg started to feel better. "Thank you, Tim," said Ben. "The good water helped me heal." Tim and Ben played by the pond all day, happy that the good water had helped Ben.

Once upon a time, in a small valley, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play and pretend all day. He liked to pretend he was a brave knight, fighting big monsters in the dark woods near his home. One day, Tim went into the dark woods to pretend to fight monsters. He took his toy sword and walked deep into the woods. He fought pretend monsters with his sword, but soon it started to get darker and darker. Tim tried to find his way back home, but he was lost in the dark woods. He called out for his mom and dad, but no one could hear him. Tim was scared and sad. He sat down on the ground and cried, wishing he had never gone into the dark woods to pretend.

Once upon a time, there was a big place. In this place, there were many animals. One day, a little rabbit wanted to cook some food for all his friends. He asked his friends to come to his home for a fun meal. The rabbit's home was a tight hole in the ground. His friends were happy to come. They all helped the rabbit cook the food. The rabbit cooked carrots, the squirrel cooked nuts, and the bird cooked seeds. When the food was ready, they all sat down to eat. They ate and ate until they were full. The rabbit, squirrel, and bird were happy that they cooked food for their friends. After they ate, they played games and had a great time in the big place. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to eat radish from the garden. One day, Remy saw a big, red radish. He wanted to eat it, but it was too big for him. Remy asked his friend, "Can you help me get the big radish?" His friend said, "I will try." They both tried to pull the radish out, but they could not manage. They tried and tried, but the radish did not move. Then, a big bird came and saw the two friends. The bird wanted the radish too. The bird said, "I will help you get the radish." The bird tried to pull the radish out, but it was too strong. The radish broke and fell on the ground. The big bird ate the dead radish and flew away. Remy and his friend were sad because they did not get to eat the big radish.

Once upon a time there were two friends: a frog and a bee. They had just finished playing a game together when it started to rain. The bee said to the frog, "Let's do something fun! How about we write stories together?" The frog answered, "That sounds like a great idea!" The bee flew off to get some lemon. On the way he saw a big green tree. He grabbed a lemony fruit from the tree and flew back to the frog. The frog took the lemon and smiled. He said, "This lemon will be great for our stories. Let's start writing!" The bee and the frog took turns writing stories about their day. They wrote about their friendship, the game they played, and the big green tree. At the end of the day, the bee and the frog were proud of their stories. They even drew pictures to go along with the stories. The bee and the frog were very happy they were able to write stories together and share their fun adventures.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Joe and Jody. Joe wanted to take a quiz to see how much he knew. Jody did not want to take the quiz because he was embarrassed. Joe was very determined and started to shake Jody to make him take the quiz. Jody started to cry and Joe became sad. Joe hugged Jody and told him it was ok if he didn't want to take the quiz. Jody was relieved and hugged Joe back. Joe said that he could try the quiz another day. They both hugged again and went to play outside.

Once upon a time, in a small town, lived a girl named Sue. Sue loved to eat red tomatoes. She ate them every day. One day, Sue wanted to share her tomatoes with her friend, Tim. Tim lived far away. Sue thought, "I will mail him a tomato, so he can taste it too!" She put the tomato in a box and went to the mail place. At the mail place, Sue gave the box to the mailman. The mailman said, "Is the tomato safe in the box?" Sue said, "Yes, it is safe." The mailman took the box and sent it to Tim. Tim got the box and opened it. He saw the tomato and smiled. He called Sue and said, "Thank you for the tomato!" Sue was happy that Tim liked the tomato. They both felt safe and loved.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, Anna has an idea. "Ben, do you want to come to my house for dinner?" she asks. "Yes, please. What are we having?" Ben says. "Turkey. My mom makes the best turkey. It is big and juicy and yummy," Anna says. "Wow, that sounds good. I love turkey," Ben says. They run to Anna's house. They see Anna's mom in the kitchen. She is busy with the turkey. "Hi, mom. This is Ben. He is my friend. Can he stay for dinner?" Anna says. "Hello, Ben. Of course he can. I'm glad you invited him. We have plenty of turkey," Anna's mom says. She smiles and cuts a thin slice of turkey for Ben. She puts it on a plate with some potatoes and carrots. "Here you go, Ben. Enjoy your dinner," she says. "Thank you, Anna's mom. This looks delicious," Ben says. He takes a bite of the turkey. It is soft and tender and tasty. "Mmm, this is the best turkey ever," he says. Anna and Ben eat their dinner. They are happy and full. They thank Anna's mom for the turkey. They hug and say goodbye. "Bye, Ben. See you tomorrow," Anna says. "Bye, Anna. Thanks for inviting me," Ben says. They wave and smile. They are good friends. They like turkey.

Once upon a time there was a stubborn worm. One day he was walking down the path when he heard a loud noise. It was a noise he had never heard before. He decided to explore and find out what it was. When he arrived, he saw a big machine that was shooting things up in the air. The worm was scared and he wanted to hide. He quickly ran and hid under a big leaf. The worm was intrigued and he wanted to know what was happening. He slowly began to crawl out from under the leaf. Then, he saw something big and black coming towards him. It was a big rubber ball that the machine was shooting. The worm quickly scurried away just in time and hid behind a tree. Once he was safe, the worm returned to the path. He was exhausted and very determined not to get close to the machine again. He was a very stubborn worm and he knew he needed to be careful!

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see some red berries on a bush. They want to pick them and eat them. "Look, Ben, berries!" Lila says. "They look yummy!" "Yes, let's get them!" Ben says. They run to the bush and start to pull the berries. But the sky is dark and gray. It starts to rain. The rain is heavy and cold. It makes them wet and sad. "Let's go home, Lila!" Ben says. "We can come back later!" But Lila does not want to go. She wants to get more berries. She says, "No, Ben, I want to stay! The berries are so good!" Ben is scared. He does not like the rain. He says, "Please, Lila, come with me! The rain is bad! It can hurt us!" But Lila does not listen. She says, "You go, Ben, I don't care! I will get all the berries for me!" Ben is sad. He does not want to leave Lila. But he is also cold and wet. He runs to his home. He hopes Lila will come soon. But Lila does not come. She stays by the bush. She eats more and more berries. She does not see the light in the sky. She does not hear the loud noise. She does not feel the pain. The light is a flash. The noise is a boom. The pain is a fire. The fire is a lightning. The lightning hits the bush. The bush burns. Lila burns. Lila is gone.

Once upon a time, there was a little train. The train had a big job. It had to take people to a fun party. The party was to celebrate a happy day. The train was very excited. The train went on the rail. It went up and down, left and right. The train loved the rail. The rail was perfect for the train. The train was very fast and strong. At last, the train got to the party. Everyone got off the train. They all said, "Thank you, train!" The train was very happy. The people had a great time at the party. The train went back on the perfect rail, ready for the next trip.

One day, a boy named Tim found a rod. It was a big and impressive rod. He was very happy. Tim wanted to show the rod to his friend, Sam. So, Tim went to Sam's house. When Tim got there, he said, "Look, Sam! I found this big rod." Sam looked at the rod and said, "Wow! That's impressive. Let's play with it." They played with the rod all day, having a lot of fun. Suddenly, a dog came and took the rod from them. Tim and Sam were sad. They tried to get the rod back, but the dog was too fast. Then, Tim said, "Let's quit. We can find another rod." But Sam said, "No, we can't quit. That's our rod." So, they kept trying to get the rod back. At last, they got the rod back and were very happy. The dog was not bad, he just wanted to play too. So, they all played together and had a great day.

Lily was a naughty girl. She liked to play with things that were not hers. One day, she saw a big pan on the stove. It was shiny and round. She wanted to touch it. She climbed on a chair and reached for the pan. But the pan was hot! It burned her hand. She cried out loud. "Ow! Ow! Ow!" she screamed. Mama heard her cry and ran to the kitchen. She saw Lily holding her hand and the pan on the floor. "What did you do, Lily?" Mama asked. She was angry and worried. "I wanted to lift the pan," Lily said. She was sorry and scared. "Lily, you are very naughty. You should not lift the pan. It is hot and heavy. You could hurt yourself or make a mess. You have to ask Mama before you touch anything in the kitchen. Do you understand?" Mama said. She took Lily to the sink and ran cold water over her hand. "Yes, Mama. I understand. I am sorry. I will not lift the pan again," Lily said. She hugged Mama and said, "I love you, Mama." "I love you too, Lily. But you have to be good and listen to Mama. Now let me put some cream on your hand and give you a band-aid. Then you can have a cookie and some milk," Mama said. She smiled and kissed Lily's cheek. Lily nodded and smiled too. She learned her lesson. She would not be naughty anymore. She would be a good girl.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl named Jane. One day, Jane was out playing in the garden and came across a small white rabbit that was stuck in a bush. Jane noticed that the rabbit was scared and so she decided to rescue him. Jane tried to think of a way to rescue the rabbit and decided to use some celery sticks to make a bridge for him to walk on. She placed the celery sticks next to the bush, forming a bridge. The rabbit sniffed the celery and started to nibble on it. He was so excited to have something to eat that he forgot to be scared, and walked across the celery bridge and hopped away. Suddenly, a stupid fox appeared and started to chase the rabbit! Jane was worried and said, "I must rescue it!" She grabbed the remaining celery sticks and threw them one by one at the fox. The fox got so distracted by the celery that he ran away and the rabbit was safe again. Jane had saved the rabbit! She hugged the rabbit and said goodbye before letting him go. Jane felt so happy that she was able to rescue the poor rabbit.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to sing. One day, Sue found a big mattress in her room. It was disgusting. It was dirty and smelled very bad. Sue did not like the mattress at all. Sue's mom came into the room and said, "Sue, why is this mattress in your room?" Sue said, "I don't know, Mom. It's disgusting. Can we throw it away?" Her mom said, "Yes, we can. But first, let's sing a song to make it go away faster." Sue and her mom started to sing. They sang louder and louder. But something unexpected happened. The mattress started to grow bigger and bigger! It filled the whole room. Sue and her mom were scared. They tried to run away, but the mattress was too big. They were stuck in the room with the disgusting mattress forever.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Tom. Tom lived in a small house with a girl named Lucy. They were best friends. One day, Tom and Lucy went out to play in the yard. While they were playing, Tom saw something shiny. It was an iron. "Look, Lucy!" said Tom, "I found an iron!" Lucy was very happy. They decided to pass the iron to each other and play a game. Tom passed the iron to Lucy. "Your turn!" he said. Lucy passed the iron back to Tom. They laughed and played with the iron all day long. They had so much fun together. And from that day on, Tom and Lucy always played with the iron in their yard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her pastel-colored toys. She had a big box filled with them. One day, she decided to match her toys by their colors. Lily took out her filthy, dirty toys from the box. She put all the pink toys in one pile, all the blue toys in another pile, and all the yellow toys in a third pile. She was very happy to see her toys matched by color. Lily's mom saw her playing and said, "Lily, your toys are filthy! Let's clean them up." So, Lily and her mom washed all the toys until they were shiny and clean. After they dried, Lily put her toys back in the box, still matched by color. She smiled and thought, "Now my toys are clean and matched. I love my pastel toys!"

Once upon a time there lived a little boy called Tim. One day Tim wanted to explore a big noisy place. So Tim's mom said "Follow me and be careful." They went outside and the noise was enormous. Tim had never heard such a loud noise before. He asked his mom "What is that noise?" His mom said "Oh, that's the market. It's full of people and it's very busy." Tim and his mom followed the noise and when they arrived, Tim was amazed. The market was huge and there were people everywhere. He asked "Can I explore?" His mom said "Yes, but stay close by me. Don't wander off." So Tim explored the market and he saw lots of interesting things. He saw enormous carts full of fruits and vegetables, he heard the noise of the people chattering and laughing, and he tasted some yummy treats. At the end of the day, Tim and his mom went back home. Tim was happy that he followed the noise and discovered such an incredible place!

One day, a boy named Tim went to the beach with his mom. They wanted to play in the sand and swim in the sea. Tim was very excited because he loved the beach. While they were playing, Tim found a pretty shell. He showed it to his mom and said, "Look, Mom! I found a nice shell!" His mom smiled and said, "That's great, Tim! Be careful not to lose it." After some time, Tim felt troubled. He could not find his shell. He looked everywhere in the sand, but it was gone. Tim was sad and told his mom, "Mom, I lost my shell." His mom hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tim. We can look for another shell together." They searched and found a new shell. Tim was happy again, and they had a fun day at the beach.

One day, a little girl named Lisa went to the park. She saw a tiny bug with big eyes. The bug would blink very fast. Lisa was scared of bugs, but she wanted to be brave. She put her hand close to the bug and said, "Hi, bug. I want to be your friend." The bug looked at Lisa and blinked its big eyes. It was a bit anxious, but it liked Lisa's big heart. The bug jumped onto Lisa's hand and said, "Hello, Lisa. I am a magic bug. I can make your wishes come true." Lisa was very surprised. She did not know that bugs could talk or do magic. She thought for a moment and said, "I wish for a big ice cream cone." The bug blinked its eyes, and a big ice cream cone appeared in Lisa's other hand. Lisa and the bug both smiled and shared the ice cream together.

One day, brave Toby was walking outside. He saw the sun shining brightly and he felt so hot. He thought to himself that he should find some shade to cool off in. But Toby wasn't a quitter - he was brave! So he kept walking until he saw a tree with a big branch overhanging the path. He looked up to the sun and back at the branch and thought to himself, "I can do this!". So he decided to climb the tree and he kept on going higher and higher until he reached the branch. As soon as he lay down on the branch, the sun shone even brighter! Toby was so happy - the shade kept him cool and he felt brave for conquering the tree. With a smile on his face, Toby stayed up in the tree until the sun went down.

One Tuesday, Tom got a new toy car. He was very happy. He played with the car all day. He made it go fast and slow. Tom's friend, Sue, came to play. She saw the car and said, "Wow, Tom! Your car is so new and fun!" Tom said, "Yes, it is my favorite now!" Tom and Sue played with the car. They made it go up and down the hills. They made it pause when they saw a pretend cat. They laughed and had a great time. They played until it was time to go home. Tom said, "I can't wait for next Tuesday to play with you again!"

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. The sun was out, and the day was mild. Tim saw a bench near the big tree. He sat on the bench and looked around. A bird came and sat next to Tim on the bench. The bird said, "Hi, Tim! Can you help me find my friend?" Tim was surprised that the bird could talk. But he wanted to help. So, he said, "Yes, I can help you." Tim and the bird walked in the park. They looked for the bird's friend. Then, they saw a big dog. The dog had a bird on its back. The bird on the bench said, "That's my friend!" The dog and the bird on its back came to Tim and the bird on the bench. They all became friends and played in the park together.

Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They saw a caterpillar on a leaf. It was green and fuzzy. Lily wanted to touch it. "Can I hold it, Max?" she asked. Max shook his head. "No, Lily. It is fragile. You might hurt it." Lily frowned. "But I want to see it better. It is so pretty." Max had an idea. He ran to the house and came back with a jar. He carefully put the leaf and the caterpillar in the jar. He poked some holes in the lid. "Look, Lily. Now we can display it. We can watch it and learn about it. But we have to be gentle and kind." Lily smiled. She took the jar and held it close to her eyes. She saw the caterpillar move and wiggle. She saw its tiny legs and antennae. "Wow, Max. It is amazing. Thank you for sharing it with me." Max nodded. He was happy to see Lily happy. He hoped the caterpillar would be happy too. He wondered if it would turn into a butterfly someday.

One day, a big dog with soft fur went for a walk. The dog liked to play and run in the park. The sun was bright and the sky was blue. In the park, the dog saw a small cat. The dog wanted to play, but the cat was scared. The dog barked and the cat ran away. The dog felt sorry for scaring the cat. The next day, the dog saw the cat again. This time, the dog did not bark. The dog walked slowly and said sorry. The cat was not scared anymore. They became friends and played together in the park.

Once upon a time, in a small house, lived a girl named Lily. Lily loved to cook. One day, she decided to make soup. She added carrots, peas, and corn to the pot. Her mom and dad were excited to eat the soup. But then, something unexpected happened. A tiny mouse ran into the kitchen and jumped into the soup pot! Lily was upset. She did not want a mouse in her soup. Her mom and dad were upset too. Lily's mom had an idea. She added more water to the soup and let the mouse swim out. The mouse was happy and ran away. Lily and her family laughed. They were happy the mouse was gone. They cooked the soup a little more and then they all ate it. It was the best soup they ever had.

Once upon a time, there was a gray bunny named Bob. Bob lived in a small house in the woods. He had many friends, like birds, squirrels, and mice. They all liked to play together. One sunny day, Bob and his friends were playing when they heard a loud noise. It was an emergency! Their friend, a little bird, had fallen from her nest. She needed help to get back home. Bob knew what to do. He asked his friends to help carry the little bird back to her nest. They all worked together, and soon the little bird was safe and sound. They were all very happy to have helped their friend in need. And from that day on, they knew they could always count on each other.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing in the park. The cat was very rude. It would not share its toys with the dog. The dog was sad and wanted to gain a new friend. The dog saw a ball and had an idea. "Let's play with the ball," said the dog. The cat agreed and they started to play. They had a lot of fun and the dog was happy. But then, something unexpected happened. The ball fell into a bush and when the cat went to get it, it felt a rub on its back. The cat was scared, but the dog was brave and went to see what it was. It was a little bird who wanted to play too. The cat, dog, and bird played together and the cat learned to share. The dog gained not one, but two friends that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Dizzy. Dizzy was a dizzy dog because he would run around and around in circles until he felt very dizzy. One day, Dizzy's mom told him they were going to a party. Dizzy was very excited! Dizzy's mom said they needed to prepare for the party. They put on their best clothes. Dizzy wore a nice vest. The vest was red and blue, and it made Dizzy look very fancy. Dizzy's mom wore a pretty dress. They both looked great for the party. At the party, Dizzy saw his friends. They played games, ate yummy food, and danced. Dizzy was careful not to run in circles, so he wouldn't feel dizzy. They all had a fun time at the party. When it was time to go home, Dizzy and his mom said goodbye to their friends and went back to their house. Dizzy was happy he got to wear his nice vest and have fun with his friends.

Once upon a time there was a sleepy fish who liked to swim in the sea. He went every day and had lots of fun. One day he saw something coming towards him in the sea. It looked like a missile but it was very friendly! It was a toy submarine. The fish liked to play with the submarine. He swam and chased it through the sea. Sometimes it would go away but the fish found it again. One night the fish was feeling very sleepy. He wanted to go to bed so he swam to the submarine and took a little nap in the submarine. He dreamed of swimming in the sea and playing with the submarine. The next morning he woke up feeling refreshed and went out to play again!
