They played together all day in the secret room, and it was the best day ever.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing. The cat was fast, and the dog was big. They liked to play together. The cat said, "I will never surrender to you!" The dog laughed and said, "We will see about that!" Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was an emergency! A little bird fell from the sky. The cat and the dog stopped playing. They knew they had to help the bird. The dog said, "This is bad. We must do something!" The cat and the dog worked together to help the bird. They found a safe place for the bird to rest. The bird was happy and said, "Thank you for helping me." The cat and the dog smiled. They knew that even though they liked to play, helping a friend in need was more important.

Once upon a time, there was a mom and her daughter. They lived in a house with many friends. The mom was very popular. She was nice and funny. The daughter liked to play with her mom's friends too. One day, the mom had to separate her clothes for washing. She told her daughter to help her. The daughter was happy to help. They put the clothes in two big piles. One pile was for the mom's clothes, and the other pile was for the daughter's clothes. The next day, the mom's friends came over. They saw the big piles of clothes. The friends laughed and said, "You are so popular, even your clothes have friends!" The mom and daughter laughed too. They were happy to have so many friends. And from that day on, the daughter became popular like her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a bald bird. The bird had no hair on its head. It lived in a big tree. One day, the bald bird found a worm. The worm was long and wiggly. The bird wanted to feed the worm to its baby birds. The bald bird took the worm to its nest. The baby birds were happy. They ate the worm and grew big and strong. And they all lived happily in their big tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat apples. One day, he found a big, smooth apple on the ground. He was very happy. Tim saw his friend, Sue, and wanted to share the apple with her. He walked up to her and said, "Sue, look at my big, smooth apple! Do you want to share it with me?" Sue looked at the apple and then she just shrugged. She said, "I don't like apples, but thank you, Tim." Tim was sad, but he knew that it was okay. Not everyone likes the same things. So, Tim took his big, smooth apple and sat under a tree. He ate the whole apple all by himself. It was yummy and sweet. Tim was happy that he found such a nice apple to eat. And even though Sue didn't want any, Tim still loved apples very much.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a scooter that he loved very much. He would ride it up and down the street, having lots of fun. One day, Tim saw something interesting on the ground. It was a big, shiny rock. Tim thought it was very pretty. Tim wanted to show the rock to his best friend, Lily. He put the rock in his pocket and rode his scooter to her house. When he got there, he showed her the interesting rock. Lily didn't know what it was, so she just shrugged. Tim and Lily decided to keep the rock and play with it. They took turns riding the scooter and holding the rock. They had a great day playing together, and they both loved the interesting rock. From that day on, the rock became their special treasure, and they always had fun with it and the scooter.

Once upon a time, in a big nation, there was a very unusual cat. This cat loved to stir things. One day, the cat found a big pot. The cat knew the pot was special, but did not know why. The cat wanted to stir the pot, so it did. The next day, the cat saw a big party in the town. The people were happy and dancing. The cat wanted to know why. A man told the cat that the pot was magic. When the cat stirred the pot, it made the people happy. The cat was happy too. It knew that stirring the pot was a good thing to do. Now, the cat stirs the pot every day to make the people in the nation happy. The unusual cat became a hero, and everyone loved it.

One day, a white cat and a little boy were playing in the park. They saw a man wave at them from far away. The man had a big pie in his hands. The white cat and the little boy ran to the man because they wanted some pie. The man said, "Hello, I will give you this pie, but you must share it with others too." The little boy and the white cat took the pie, but they did not want to share. They wanted to eat the whole pie by themselves. They found a place to hide and started eating the pie. But as they ate, the pie got smaller and smaller. Soon, there was no pie left. The little boy and the white cat felt sad and their tummies hurt because they ate too much. They wished they had shared the pie with their friends. The little boy and the white cat learned that being greedy is bad. Sharing with others makes everyone happy.

Once upon a time, there was a brave soldier. He had to go to a far away place for a war. The soldier was a little scared, because war was dangerous. But he thought to himself that he must be brave and do his job, so he moved forward. The soldier had a plan, a plan to make the war safe and peaceful. He worked hard to make sure it happened. He thought and thought, trying to find a way to end the war without hurting anyone. At last, the soldier found a way to make peace. He and the other soldiers worked together to make sure the war was over. Everyone was happy, as the war was over and they could go home in peace. The brave soldier was proud that he had made the war safe. He thought to himself that he must always remember that peace is far better than war.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to make noise. He would bark and jump around all day. One day, Buddy saw a big cat. The cat was very alert and fast. Buddy said to the cat, "I love to make noise! Do you want to play with me?" The cat looked at Buddy and said, "I like quiet, but I will play with you if you can catch me." So Buddy and the cat started to play. As they played, a big bird came down from the sky. The bird was very hungry and wanted to eat the cat. Buddy saw the bird and barked very loud. The noise scared the bird away. The cat was so happy and said, "Thank you, Buddy! Your noise saved me." From that day on, Buddy and the cat became best friends. They learned that sometimes making noise can be good. The moral of the story is that everyone has something special to offer, even if it seems annoying at first.

Max was a 3 year old boy who had a pet. Max's pet was a small, furry rabbit. Max loved his rabbit very much, they were the best of buddies! One day, Max's mum was walking with him to the park. She mentioned to him that she thought he should get a friend for his pet rabbit. Max got really upset. He didn't want another pet, he was happy with his lonely pet! Max and his mum arrived at the park and they got to playing. They were having a wonderful time until it was time to leave. When his mum asked him again about getting another pet, Max became very frustrated and said, "No! I only want one pet!" His mum tried to explain to him that the rabbit could get lonely and need a friend, but Max just wouldn't listen. He kept saying, "No, I want to keep my pet!" Eventually, his mum had to give in. She said, "Ok, but if you change your mind just let me know." But Max never changed his mind. Sadly, the rabbit became lonely and eventually died from lack of attention and care. Max was deeply saddened and knew that his stubbornness had caused his pet to die.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to make a print of his hand. He found some paint and a big piece of paper. Tim was very happy and excited to make his print. Tim put his hand in the paint and then on the paper. But he forgot to take his glove off! The print did not look like his hand. It looked like a big blob. Tim was sad and did not know what to do. Then, Tim had an idea. He took off his glove and tried again. This time, the print was perfect and fit just right on the paper. Tim was so happy and showed his mom the print. Now, Tim had a funny story to tell and a beautiful print to keep.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big piece of cardboard. He had a fun idea. He wanted to make a cardboard hat to wear on his head. So, he cut the cardboard into a hat shape and put it on his head. He was very happy with his new hat. Tim wore his cardboard hat all day. He showed it to his friend, Sue. Sue said, "Wow, Tim! I like your hat. Can I try it on?" Tim said, "Yes, you can wear it too." Sue put the hat on her head and they played together. After a while, the hat started to hurt Sue's head. She said, "Ouch, Tim! The hat hurts my head." Tim took the hat off Sue's head and looked at it. He saw that the edges were sharp. Tim said, "I'm sorry, Sue. I will make a new hat that won't hurt." So, Tim made a new cardboard hat with soft edges. They both wore the new hat and played happily together.

One day, there was a big king. The king was very nice, but he had a terrible secret. He was scared of the dark. Every night, when the sun went to sleep, the king would panic. He did not like the dark at all. One day, a little boy came to see the king. The boy said, "King, why are you scared of the dark? It is not bad. In the dark, we can see the stars and the moon. They are very pretty." The king thought about what the boy said. That night, the king looked at the stars and the moon. The king saw how pretty they were. The king was not scared of the dark anymore. The king said, "Thank you, little boy. You helped me see the dark is not bad." The king and the boy became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a helpful dog named Spot. Spot loved to play on the big, soft rug with his best friend, a little boy named Tim. They played every day and had lots of fun together. One day, Tim's mom gave him a ball to play with. The ball was red and had a sharp stick on it. Tim and Spot played with the ball on the rug, but they did not know that the sharp stick could be bad. They laughed and ran around, having a great time. The sun was shining, and they were very happy. But then, the ball with the sharp stick rolled under a chair. Spot went to get the ball from under the chair. As he tried to get it, the sharp stick poked him. Spot yelped and ran away, scared and hurt. Tim was sad because his helpful friend Spot was hurt. The ball with the sharp stick was not fun anymore. Tim and Spot learned that sharp things can be bad and should be used with care.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a dog named Bob and a cat named Tom. Bob and Tom did not like each other. They would fight all the time. One day, it started to rain. The rain made everything wet. Bob and Tom were outside in the rain. They were wet and cold. They saw a big tree and both ran to it to stay dry. Under the tree, they stopped fighting. They felt warm and safe together. The rain made them forget their fight. As the rain stopped, Bob and Tom became friends. They played and had fun together. They learned that it was better to be friends than to fight. The rain had taught them a lesson. From that day on, they never fought again, and they lived happily ever after.

Mia was so excited - it was her first day of pre-school! She ran happily into the classroom ready to meet all of the other children. She sat down in a comfortable chair and looked around. She could already tell it was going to be a great year. “Hi everyone!” said the teacher, Mrs. Smith. “My name is Mrs. Smith and I am going to be your teacher this year. I have a special staff I use in the classroom - can you tell me what it's for?” Mia thought for a moment before raising her hand. “You use the staff for drawing in the sky!” she said. Mrs. Smith smiled. “That's right!” she said. “Now let's get comfortable and begin our day.” Mia took out her crayons and ran to join the other children. She couldn't wait to see what they would learn today!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy rocket. She wanted to go to space one day. Lily's mom said, "Space is very far away, but you can dream about it." One day, Lily found an expensive toy rocket in the store. She asked her mom, "Can I please have this toy rocket?" Her mom said, "No, it is too expensive. We can make a rocket at home instead." At home, Lily and her mom made a rocket from a big box. They painted it and put stickers on it. Lily played inside her rocket and pretended to fly to space. Suddenly, she heard a voice, "Hello, Lily! I am an alien from space!" The alien was friendly and wanted to play with Lily. Lily and the alien played together and had so much fun. Then, the alien said, "I have to go back to space now. Please come visit me someday!" Lily promised she would try. From that day on, Lily knew that even if she couldn't go to space right away, she could still make friends from far away places. And she knew that sometimes, the best things in life don't have to be expensive.

Ben and Lily were playing with blocks. They liked to build towers and houses and cars. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes. "Look, I made a big tower!" Ben said, showing his blocks to Lily. "It is very tall and strong. I attached many blocks together." "That is nice, Ben," Lily said. "But I made a house. It has a door and a window and a roof. I attached blocks too, but in a different way." They were both happy with their blocks. But then, Tom came. Tom was older and bigger than Ben and Lily. He liked to make trouble. He saw their blocks and wanted to play with them. "Hey, give me your blocks!" Tom said, grabbing some of Ben's blocks. "I want to make something better." "Hey, stop it!" Ben said, trying to get his blocks back. "These are my blocks. You have your own blocks." Tom did not listen. He took more blocks from Ben and Lily. He threw some blocks on the floor. He laughed and said, "Your blocks are boring. Mine are better. I am smarter than you." Ben and Lily were sad and angry. They did not like Tom. They wanted their blocks back. They did not know what to do. Then, they had an idea. They whispered to each other. They made a plan. They smiled and said, "OK, Tom. You can have our blocks. But we want to see what you make. Show us how smart you are." Tom was happy. He thought he had won. He took all the blocks and started to build. He tried to make a big castle. He attached many blocks together. He made walls and towers and bridges. He used all the blocks he could find. But he did not attach the blocks well. He did not make the castle strong. He did not balance the blocks. He did not pay attention to the shapes and colors. He just wanted to make the biggest castle ever. Ben and Lily watched him. They waited for the right moment. They knew what would happen. They were ready. When Tom finished his castle, he was very proud. He said, "Look at my castle! It is the best castle ever. It is bigger and better than your tower and house. I am the smartest of all." He climbed on top of his castle. He wanted to show off. He wanted to see how high he was. But then, his castle collapsed. The blocks fell down. They made a loud noise. They hit Tom. He fell down too. He was hurt and scared. He cried and said, "Help! Help! My castle! My blocks!" Ben and Lily ran to him. They helped him get up. They gave him some of their blocks. They said, "Tom, are you OK? We are sorry for your castle. But you should not have taken our blocks. You should not have made trouble. You should have been nice and shared. That is what smart people do." Tom felt ashamed. He realized he was wrong. He said, "I am sorry, Ben and Lily. You are right. I was not smart. I was mean and greedy. Can you forgive me? Can we be friends?" Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "Yes, we can forgive you. We can be friends. But you have to be nice and share. And you have to attach the blocks well. Then we can all make nice things together." They hugged and smiled. They played with the blocks again. They made new towers and houses and castles. They attached the blocks well. They shared and helped each other. They had fun and learned. They were smart and happy.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a happy cat named Max. Max was proud of his soft, shiny fur. One day, Max got an invitation to a big party at his friend's house. Max was very excited to go to the party and play with his friends. Before the party, Max needed to move his toys to make his room clean. He asked his friend, a little bird named Sam, for help. "Sam, can you please help me move my toys?" Max said. Sam was happy to help Max. They worked together to move the toys and make the room clean. At the party, Max and Sam had lots of fun. They played games, ate yummy food, and laughed with their friends. Max was proud of his clean room and happy that he had a great time at the party. And Max was very thankful to have a good friend like Sam to help him.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Tara. Tara wanted to go have some cocoa. She had to travel far to find some. On her way, she encountered a large brown bear. The bear was very angry and blocked Tara's path. Tara was too scared to go around the bear. She put her hands together, closed her eyes and asked the bear to go away. The bear sighed and slowly large away, finally allowing Tara to go on her way. Tara continued on her journey to find cocoa. After a long day of walking, she finally arrived. She was so excited when she saw the cocoa shop. She ordered the largest cup of cocoa and enjoyed her delicious treat. She felt so happy and grateful - and lucky to have made it there safely.

Once upon a time, there was a fast player named Tim. Tim loved to run and play games with his friends. One day, Tim and his friends went to the park to play a game with a ball. They were all very excited. In the game, Tim's friend, Sam, had to hold the ball and release it for the others to catch. Sam was not very good at this, but he tried his best. Tim and his friends laughed and had fun as they played. As the game went on, Sam got better at releasing the ball. Tim knew that one day, Sam would release the ball just right. And then, it happened! Sam released the ball and Tim caught it. They all cheered and clapped for Sam. Tim was so happy that his friend had learned to play the game well. From that day on, they played together and had lots of fun.

One day, a bird sat on a long branch. The bird saw a cat. The cat saw the bird too. The cat wanted to talk to the bird. The cat said, "Bird, come down. I want to talk." The bird looked at the cat. The bird said, "No, I like this branch. You come up here." The cat tried to climb the tree, but the branch was too long. The bird saw the cat try to climb. The bird knew the cat could not reach. The bird said, "I will come down to talk." The bird flew down and talked to the cat. They talked and became friends. The cat knew the bird was safe on the long branch.

One day, a boy named Tim had an arrow. It was a fragile arrow that his dad gave him. Tim loved his arrow and played with it every day. He liked to pretend he was a great hero with it. One day, his friend Sam came over to play. Sam saw the arrow and asked Tim, "Can you lend me your arrow to play with?" Tim was scared that the arrow might break, but he didn't want to make Sam sad. So, he said, "Okay, but be careful. It's fragile." Sam played with the arrow, but he was not careful. He threw it too hard and the arrow broke. Tim was very sad and angry. Sam said, "I'm sorry, Tim. I didn't mean to break your arrow." Tim forgave Sam, but he still missed his arrow. Tim's dad saw that he was sad and made him a new arrow. This time, it was not fragile. Tim was happy again, and he shared his new arrow with Sam. They played together and were more careful this time. Tim learned that sometimes things break, but friends can still be friends.

One day, Tom wanted to sell his big fridge. It was an unusual fridge because it had many colors. Tom told his friend, "I want to sell my fridge." His friend, Tim, did not like the fridge. Tim said, "No, I don't want to buy it." They got mad at each other. Tom and Tim stopped being friends. In the end, Tom could not sell the fridge. The fridge stayed in his house. The moral is, don't let things come between friends.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby cat named Bob. Bob loved to play outside in the sun. One day, the sun went away, and it became very cold. Bob went outside to play, but he started to shiver because it was so cold. He looked up at the sky and saw no light, only big gray clouds. Bob missed the warm sun and the bright light it gave. Bob decided to go back inside his warm house. He curled up in his soft bed and waited for the sun to come back. Soon, the light returned, and the sun was shining again. Bob was happy and ran outside to play in the warm light.

One day, a big red truck was driving down the road. The truck was very sleepy, but it had to keep going. The truck was carrying many toys to the toy store. As the truck drove, a little boy named Tim saw it. Tim loved to throw balls. He picked up a ball and threw it at the truck. The ball hit the truck and made a loud noise. The truck was very sad and stopped. Tim felt bad for making the truck sad. He went to the truck and said sorry. The sleepy truck forgave Tim. They became friends and played together. The truck was happy again and continued to the toy store.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy sword that he loved to play with. He would swing it around and pretend to be a brave knight. One day, his mom told him not to play with the sword inside the house because he might break something. But Tim did not listen and ignored her. Later that day, Tim saw a big, disgusting bug on the floor. He thought that this was his chance to be a brave knight and save the day. He lifted his sword and swung it at the bug. But, when he did that, he also hit a tall lamp in the room. The lamp fell down and broke into many pieces. Tim felt sad because he knew he should have listened to his mom. His mom came into the room and saw the broken lamp. She was not happy, but she knew that Tim had learned his lesson. From that day on, Tim never ignored his mom's words and always played with his sword outside. And, he became the bravest knight in the whole backyard.

Once upon a time, there was a bright sun in the sky. Max and Milly were out playing on a hot day. “It’s too hot today,” said Max. Milly replied, “Let’s take a look at the thermometer.” So they found a thermometer and Max said, “It says 34 degrees. That’s hot!” Milly said, “Why don’t we take a break and wait for the sun to end soon?” So they waited and waited and eventually the sun set. The sky turned dark and cool. Max sighed with relief and said, “Finally the hot weather is over.” Milly smiled and said, “Let’s go home now.” So Max and Milly headed home and enjoyed the cool evening. The bright stars lit up the night sky.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lucy and she was very messy. Everywhere Lucy went she left a trail of mess, but she never noticed. Her family loved her very much, but it made them very sad when she made a mess. One day, Lucy woke up early. She was so excited to get an early start and have adventures. She raced around her room and soon the room was a mess. "Lucy, your room is so messy!" said her Mom. Lucy didn't know what to do. She was so excited to start her day she forgot to clean. But then she had an idea. "Mom, can I take a nap if I clean up my mess?" asked Lucy. Her Mom said yes and Lucy cheered. She started cleaning, stuffing her toys and clothes in her toy box. The room was neat in no time. Lucy got to take a nap and when she woke up she felt all fresh and ready for more adventures. Lucy learned a lesson that day - to always clean up her mess. She hoped that she would remember next time.

Once upon a time, there was a restless little boy named Tim. He loved to play outside in the mud. One day, Tim saw a big pile of mud and had a fun idea. He wanted to decorate the mud and make it look pretty. Tim ran to his friend, Sally, and said, "Let's decorate the mud!" Sally agreed, and they both started to collect colorful rocks, leaves, and flowers. They put the pretty things on the mud and made it look very nice. Tim and Sally were so happy with their muddy artwork. But then, something unexpected happened. A big dog came running and jumped right into their decorated mud. The dog wagged its tail and barked, "Woof! Woof!" Tim and Sally looked at each other and laughed. They didn't mind, because they had fun decorating the mud, and now they could do it all over again.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little pink bunny. The bunny had an impressive jump. One day, the bunny met a big blue bird. "Hello, bird!" said the bunny. "I like your blue color." "Thank you, bunny," said the bird. "I like your pink color too." The bunny wanted to play with the bird. "Let's play a game," said the bunny. "I will jump, and you will repeat my jump." The bird agreed, and they started to play. The bunny jumped high, and the bird repeated the jump. They had a lot of fun, and they became good friends. The little pink bunny and the big blue bird played together every day in the big forest.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. One day, they find a big box in the corner. They open it and see many things inside. They see books, clothes, and a soft bear. "Wow, look at this bear!" Lily says. "It is so soft and brown. Can I have it?" "No, I want it!" Ben says. "It is mine!" They both grab the bear and pull it. They hear a rip sound. The bear's arm comes off. "Oh no!" Lily and Ben say. "We broke the bear!" They hear their mom coming up the stairs. They are in trouble. They hide the bear under the bed. "Hi, kids. What are you doing?" Mom says. "Nothing, Mom. Just playing," Lily says. "Can I see what you are playing with?" Mom says. Lily and Ben look at each other. They are scared. They pray in their hearts. "Please, God, help us. We are sorry we broke the bear. We don't want Mom to be mad at us. Please, make her happy and kind," they pray. Mom comes into the room. She sees the box. "Oh, this is the box of things I wanted to donate to the orphanage. I forgot to take it out," she says. She looks inside the box. She sees the books, the clothes, and the soft bear. "Look, kids. There is a soft bear here. Do you want to give it to a child who has no toys?" she says. Lily and Ben feel a warm feeling in their hearts. They take out the bear and show it to Mom. "Mom, we are sorry. We broke the bear's arm. We wanted to keep it, but we fought over it," they say. Mom smiles and hugs them. "It's okay, kids. I'm not mad at you. I'm proud of you for telling me the truth and for being generous. We can fix the bear's arm and give it to someone who will love it. Do you want to do that?" she says. Lily and Ben nod and smile. "Yes, Mom. We want to do that. Thank you, God, for helping us," they say. They all go downstairs and sew the bear's arm. Then they put it back in the box. They take the box to the car and drive to the orphanage. They give the box to a lady who works there. She thanks them and takes them to a room where many children are playing. She gives the soft bear to a little girl who has no toys. She hugs the bear and smiles. "Thank you, thank you, thank you!" she says. Lily and Ben feel happy. They made a new friend. They learned to share and to pray. They hug their mom and thank her for taking them to the orphanage. They go back to the car and drive home. They are happy and grateful. They are not in trouble anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old owl who lived in a big tree. He had a staff of little birds who helped him. They all worked together to keep the forest clean and safe. One day, a small bird named Timmy was very tired. He said, "I want to quit. I don't want to help anymore." The wise owl asked, "Why do you want to quit, Timmy?" Timmy replied, "I am too small, and I can't do much." The wise owl said, "Remember, even small things can make a big difference." The next day, a big storm came to the forest. Many leaves and branches fell on the ground. The wise owl and the staff of little birds started cleaning up. Timmy saw a small hole in the tree where water was coming in. He thought, "I can fix this!" He used his small body to block the hole and stop the water. After the storm, the wise owl said, "Thank you, Timmy! You saved our home." Timmy was happy and didn't want to quit anymore. He learned that even small birds can do big things. The moral of the story is, "No matter how small you are, you can make a big difference."

Once upon a time, there was a little black dog named Spot. Spot loved to go on walks with his owner, Tim. One sunny day, Tim put Spot's leash on and they went for a walk. As they walked, the sun began to shine very bright. Spot saw another dog and wanted to say hi. "Woof, woof!" said Spot. The other dog said, "Woof, woof!" back. They were happy to meet each other. But, Spot forgot that he was on a leash. He pulled too hard and made Tim fall down. Tim was sad, and Spot felt bad. Spot learned that he should be careful when on a leash. From that day on, Spot never pulled on his leash again, and they had many happy walks together.

Once upon a time, there was a fearful cat. The cat lived in a house with a chimney. The cat liked to play near the chimney. One day, the cat saw that the chimney was dirty. It wanted to help clean the chimney. So, the cat got a cloth and started to clean. It was very happy to help. As the cat cleaned the chimney, it became less fearful. The cat was proud of its work. The house was now clean and the cat was happy. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a little girl named Mia was playing in her room. She felt restless and wanted to do something fun. She saw her mom sitting in a big armchair and asked, "Mom, can we play a game?" Mom smiled and said, "Sure, Mia. Let's complete a puzzle together." They started the puzzle on the floor near the armchair. Mia was excited and happy to play with her mom. As they were playing, something unexpected happened. A little mouse ran out from under the armchair! Mia and her mom jumped in surprise. The mouse looked at them and said, "I'm sorry I scared you. I just wanted to play too!" Mia, her mom, and the mouse all laughed and finished the puzzle together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her mom's makeup. One day, she found a big white box full of makeup under her mom's bed. She was so happy! Lily opened the box and saw lots of colors. She put some red on her lips, blue on her eyes, and pink on her cheeks. She looked in the mirror and laughed. "I look so funny!" she said to herself. Just then, her mom came into the room. "Lily, what are you doing?" her mom asked. Lily showed her mom the white box. "I found your makeup, Mommy!" she said. Her mom smiled and said, "That's okay, but next time, please ask me first. Now, let's close the box and put it away." Lily and her mom closed the white box and put it back under the bed. Then they went to the bathroom to wash Lily's face. After that, they had a fun day playing outside in the sun.

Once upon a time, in a big green field, there was a red ball. The red ball was very happy. It loved to roll around and play with the other balls. One day, the red ball heard about a big game. The game was at noon. The ball that could roll the fastest would win. The red ball wanted to win the game. So, it practiced every day. The other balls saw the red ball practice. They wanted to win too. They all practiced together. The red ball was fast, but it was not the fastest. The blue ball was the fastest. The red ball was sad. The day of the big game came. All the balls were ready to race. The race started and the balls rolled as fast as they could. Suddenly, the blue ball hit a rock and stopped. The red ball saw the blue ball and helped it. Together, they rolled to the finish line. They both won the race. The other balls were happy for the red ball and the blue ball. They learned that helping each other is more important than winning alone. From that day on, the balls always played together and helped each other. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily liked to play with her old jewelry. One day, she found a shiny ring in her jewelry box. She put the ring on her finger and showed it to her mom. "Look, Mommy! I found a pretty ring!" Lily said. Her mom smiled and said, "That's a very old ring. It was your grandma's ring. Do you want to know a secret about it?" Lily's eyes grew big. "Yes, please tell me!" she said. Her mom leaned in and whispered, "If you kiss the ring, something magical will happen." Lily was so excited. She held the ring up to her lips and gave it a big kiss. Suddenly, the room filled with beautiful butterflies. Lily and her mom laughed and played with the butterflies all day long. From that day on, Lily knew that her grandma's old ring was very special.

One sunny day, a little bird named Tim was sitting on a tree. He felt very comfortable in his nest. He liked to sing songs all day long. His songs made everyone happy. One day, Tim saw a funny cat. The cat was trying to climb the tree to say hello. But the cat was not good at climbing. The cat would slip and fall down, but it would try again and again. Tim wanted to help the cat. So, he sang a special song. The song made the cat feel strong and brave. The cat climbed the tree without slipping. Tim and the cat became good friends and they sang songs together every day.

Once upon a time, in a humble little town, there lived a girl named Lily. She had a lovely garden with many pretty flowers. Every day, she would play in her garden and take care of her plants. One day, she found a tiny seed in her garden. Lily planted the seed in the ground and watered it. She waited and waited for the seed to grow. After a few days, a little green shoot came out of the ground. Lily was so happy! As the days went by, the shoot grew bigger and stronger. One day, a beautiful flower bloomed on the plant. It had soft petals and smooth skin. Lily loved her new flower very much. She knew that with love and care, even the humblest seed could bloom into something beautiful.

Anna was very excited. Today was her birthday and she hoped to get a gift from her mom and dad. She woke up early and ran to the living room. She noticed a big box with a bow on the table. She smiled and clapped her hands. She wanted to open the box right away, but her mom and dad were still sleeping. She tried to be quiet, but she was too curious. She tiptoed to the box and touched the bow. She wondered what was inside. Maybe a doll, or a book, or a puzzle. She heard a noise from the box. It sounded like a squeak. She gasped and jumped back. What was that? She leaned closer and listened. She heard another squeak, and then a scratch. She felt scared and excited at the same time. She decided to open the box. She pulled the bow and lifted the lid. She saw a small, furry animal with big ears and a long tail. It was a bunny! It looked at her with bright eyes and twitched its nose. It was the best gift ever! She picked up the bunny and hugged it. It was soft and warm. It licked her cheek and made her giggle. She named it Fluffy and carried it to her mom and dad's room. She knocked on the door and said, "Look, look, I got a gift! It's a bunny! It's Fluffy!" Her mom and dad woke up and smiled. They were happy to see her happy. They hugged her and Fluffy and wished her a happy birthday. They said they were proud of her for being so persistent and brave. They said they loved her very much. Anna was very happy. She thanked them and kissed them. She said she loved them and Fluffy too. She said it was the best birthday ever.

Once upon a time, in a big palace, there lived a king, a queen, and their little boy. The palace was very big and had many rooms. The little boy loved to run and play in the big palace. One day, while the little boy was playing, he saw a funny-looking cat. The cat had a big, long nose. The little boy said, "Hello, cat! Do you want to play with me?" The cat nodded and started to play with the little boy. As they were playing, the cat suddenly let out a big sneeze. The sneeze was so big that it made the little boy and the cat fly up into the air! They landed in a secret room in the palace that no one knew about. In the secret room, they found a big box full of toys. The little boy and the cat played with the toys all day, and they became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She loved to play with her toys and eat dinner with her family. One day, her mommy asked her to help wash the dishes after dinner. Amy was excited to help, but she was a little scared too. She knew that some of the dishes were dangerous because they were very sharp. Amy started to wash the dishes very carefully. She didn't want to touch the dangerous ones. But then, she saw a big, sharp knife in the sink. Amy knew she had to be very careful with the knife. She didn't want to get hurt. Amy called her mommy to help her with the dangerous knife. Her mommy came and showed her how to wash it safely. Together, they finished washing all the dishes. Amy was very happy that she could help her mommy and learn how to be safe with the dangerous dishes.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Tom. Tom liked to play with his toy, a fork. One day, Tom saw a big box. He wanted to lift it and see what was inside. Tom tried to lift the box, but it was too heavy. He called his friend, a little dog named Max. "Max, can you help me lift this big box?" Tom asked. "Yes, I can help you," said Max. Together, Tom and Max lifted the box. Inside, they found a big cake. They were so happy! Tom took his fork and shared the cake with Max. They both ate the cake and had a great day.

One day, a boy named Tim got a letter. It was an invite to a big museum. He was very happy. Tim asked his friend, Sue, "Do you want to go with me?" Sue said, "Yes, I want to go too!" They went to the museum together. They saw big animals and pretty pictures. Sue was envious of Tim because he got the invite, but she was happy to be there too. At the museum, they met a nice lady. She showed them around. They had lots of fun. Tim and Sue liked the museum a lot. They went home and told their mom and dad all about it.

Once upon a time, there was a big piano. It was a magic piano. At night, the piano would glow. It was very pretty. One day, a little boy named Tim found the glowing piano. He was hungry. He said, "Hello, piano! Can you help me find some food?" The piano said, "Yes, Tim. I will help you." The piano played a happy song. The song made a big apple fall from a tree. Tim ate the apple. He was not hungry anymore. Tim and the piano became good friends. They played songs together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy sword that he loved to play with. He would run around his house, waving the sword in the air and pretending to be a brave knight. One day, Tim was playing with his sword in the park. He saw a big, fearful dog that scared him. The dog barked loudly at Tim, and Tim felt very afraid. He did not know what to do. Tim remembered that knights were brave, so he held up his sword and shouted, "Go away, dog!" The dog was surprised and ran away. Tim felt very happy and proud that he was brave like a knight. From that day on, Tim and his toy sword went on many more adventures together.

Once there was a girl named Elle. She was very brave and was always up for a challenge! One day she saw something in the bathroom that needed to be fixed. She thought to herself "I am so brave, I can do this!" Elle got some tools from the kitchen and carefully started to fix the bathroom. She worked hard and it was not easy, but she kept going. Finally, after lots of hard work and determination, Elle finished! The bathroom looked so pretty! Elle smiled and was very proud of her accomplishment. From that day on, Elle was even more brave and inspired to try new things. She was so happy that she could fix something all by herself. And her bathroom was looking so pretty!

Once upon a time, there was a dependable dog named Spot. Spot loved to hug his friends. He had a favorite bottle that he liked to play with. One day, Spot went to the park with his bottle. He saw his friend, Kitty. Spot hugged Kitty, and they played with the bottle together. They had a lot of fun. Then, it started to get dark. Spot and Kitty were very tired. They forgot the bottle at the park. When they went home, they were sad because they lost the bottle. They could not play with it anymore. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. One day, Tim went to the doctor with his mom. The doctor said, "Tim, you need an x-ray." Tim felt scared but his mom held his hand. In the x-ray room, the floor felt icy and cold. Tim saw a big machine. The doctor said, "Stand here and bow, Tim." Tim did as the doctor said. The machine made a funny noise, but it didn't hurt. After the x-ray, Tim was still scared. He said, "Mom, I don't want to do that again." His mom hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tim. The x-ray is done and now the doctor can help you feel better." Tim felt brave and happy because his mom was with him.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a big structure where kids played. One day, two friends, Tom and Sam, went to play there. They loved to wave at each other from the top of the structure. Tom and Sam were very competitive. They wanted to see who could climb the structure the fastest. Tom said, "Let's race to the top!" Sam agreed, "Yes, let's see who wins!" They started to climb, but they were not careful. They climbed too fast and did not hold on tight. Tom and Sam both fell down from the structure. They were sad and hurt. They learned that being too competitive can sometimes lead to a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there lived a small girl. Every day she would run and play in the garden with her friends. One day, as she was playing in the garden, a small bird came and landed on her shoulder. The bird whispered something in her ear. The little girl looked around and asked, "What did you say?" But the bird had already fluttered away! The little girl thought about the message the bird had whispered and she started to understand what he had been trying to tell her. He was sending her a message that it is better to be kind and considerate to each other, as it makes everyone so much happier. The little girl smiled and said, "Thank you!" as she watched the bird flutter away. From that day on, she would always whisper nice things to her friends and she wasn't afraid to give hugs and share her toys with them. Everyone was so happy and the little girl was proud that she had understood the bird's message.

Once there was a little dog named Alfie. Alfie was a very obedient dog who loved to play. One day, he was playing in the park with his owner. Alfie ran fast and chased a toy. He was going so fast, his legs were a blur! But then he tripped and his toe got hurt. Tears filled his eyes and his owner felt bad. His owner picked him up and hugged him tight. He said, "Alfie, you were being so obedient. That's why you had an accident." He put some ointment on his toe and Alfie felt better. He learned a lesson - running too fast can be dangerous!

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a flexible snake named Sam. Sam loved to cook food for his friends. One day, he decided to cook a big meal for all his friends in the forest. Sam invited all his friends to his tent, where he cooked a big meal. As he was cooking, his friend, a little bird named Lily, asked, "Sam, what are you cooking?" Sam replied, "I am cooking yummy food for all of us to eat!" When the food was ready, all the animals sat in the tent and enjoyed the meal. They laughed and talked as they ate. Sam was happy to see his friends enjoying the food he cooked. After the meal, they all thanked Sam and went back to their homes. The next day, Sam's friends came back to the tent with gifts for him. They wanted to thank him for the yummy food he cooked. They played games and had fun all day long. From that day on, Sam and his friends would cook and eat together in the tent. They all lived happily ever after.

Tom is a deaf boy. He can not hear sounds. He can see and feel and talk with his hands. He likes to learn new things. He goes to a school for deaf kids. His teacher is Miss Lee. She is deaf too. One day, Miss Lee teaches Tom and his friends how to wash dishes. She shows them how to use soap and water and a sponge. She says with her hands, "Washing dishes is good. It makes them clean and shiny. It helps your family." Tom and his friends nod and smile. Tom wants to try. He picks up a plate and puts it in the sink. He turns on the faucet. The water comes out fast and loud. Tom can not hear it, but he can feel it splash on his face and clothes. He is surprised and scared. He drops the plate. It breaks on the floor. Tom feels bad. Miss Lee hears the noise and comes to see. She sees the broken plate and the wet Tom. She is not angry. She hugs Tom and says with her hands, "It's okay. Accidents happen. You are not hurt. You can try again. I will help you." Tom feels better. Miss Lee teaches Tom how to turn on the faucet slowly and gently. She teaches him how to hold the plate and scrub it with the sponge. She teaches him how to rinse it and dry it and put it away. Tom learns how to wash dishes. He is proud and happy. He says with his hands, "Thank you, Miss Lee. You are a good teacher. I like washing dishes." Miss Lee smiles and says with her hands, "You are welcome, Tom. You are a good student. I like teaching you."

Once upon a time, there was a cat named Tom. Tom had soft fur. He liked to play with his friends. One day, Tom met a big dog named Max. Max was deaf, so he could not hear well. Tom and Max liked to play together. They played hide and seek. Tom would hide, and Max would try to find him. One day, Tom hid in a big box. Max could not find him. Max looked and looked, but he could not hear Tom. Tom felt regret for hiding in the box. He wanted to play with Max. So, Tom jumped out of the box. Max was very surprised! Max did not know Tom was in the box. They laughed and played together again. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a lively baby named Tim. Tim liked to play with his big, red ball. He would kick it all day long in his yard. One day, his mom said, "Tim, be careful with your ball. It might go too far away." Tim did not listen. He kept kicking the ball higher and higher. One day, the ball went very far away. Tim was sad. He looked and looked for his red ball, but he could not find it. Then, a friendly dog came to Tim. The dog had Tim's red ball in his mouth. Tim was happy. He said, "Thank you, dog!" Tim learned to be more careful when he played with his ball. And from that day on, Tim and the dog became best friends.

Sara and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig and water the plants. But they did not like the big red tomatoes that grew on the vines. They thought they were yucky and squishy. One day, they saw a tomato that was bigger than their heads. It had a mean face and sharp teeth. It was angry and hungry. It wanted to eat them. "Help! Help!" Sara and Ben shouted. They ran away from the tomato. But the tomato was fast and rolled after them. "Stop! Stop!" the tomato said. "I want to be your friend. I am lonely and bored. Please play with me." Sara and Ben did not believe the tomato. They thought it was lying and tricking them. They were scared and impatient. They wanted to escape. They saw a hole in the fence. They ran towards it. They squeezed through it. They left the garden and the tomato behind. They were safe and happy. They hugged each other. They decided to never play with tomatoes again. They liked carrots and peas better.

One day, a big plane wanted to fly high in the sky. The plane was very spoiled. It did not like to share the sky with other planes. The plane said, "I want the sky all to myself!" The plane started to fly up, up, up. It went so high that it could not see the other planes. But then, something unexpected happened. The plane saw a big bird. The bird was even bigger than the plane! The big bird said, "Hello, plane! You cannot have the sky all to yourself. We all have to share." The spoiled plane was sad, but it knew the bird was right. The plane flew back down and shared the sky with the other planes and the big bird. They all became friends and had fun flying together.

Once upon a time, there was a little model of a car. The car was red and shiny. It had four wheels and went very fast. The car always felt safe when it was with its friend, the teddy bear. One day, the car and the teddy bear went on a big adventure. They played and had fun. But then, the car had a little fall. The car was hurt and needed help to heal. The teddy bear hugged the car and gave it lots of love. Soon, the car started to feel better. The car was healed and safe again. The car and the teddy bear were very happy and played together forever.

One day, a big group of elderly animals wanted to unite. They wanted to make a big welcome party for all their friends. They were very happy and excited. They started to plan the party and make a big cake. But then, a mean and big animal came. He did not want the elderly animals to have a party. He took their cake away and made them very sad. The elderly animals did not know what to do. They were scared and upset. Then, something unexpected happened. A small and brave animal came to help. He was not scared of the mean and big animal. He talked to him and made him understand that the party was for everyone. The mean and big animal felt bad and said sorry. He gave the cake back, and they all had a great welcome party together. The elderly animals were very happy and grateful to the small and brave animal.

Once upon a time, there was a wise monkey named Momo. Momo loved to eat bananas. One day, Momo saw a big banana tree with many bananas on it. Momo was very happy. Momo wanted to get the bananas, but the tree was very tall. Momo thought hard and had a good idea. Momo asked his friend, the bird, to help him. The bird was happy to help Momo. The bird flew up and picked the bananas from the tree. Momo and the bird shared the bananas. They both were very happy. Momo was wise to ask for help, and they both win. They ate the bananas and played together all day.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and watch cartoons. But they do not like to eat the same food. Anna likes pizza, but Ben does not. Ben likes soup, but Anna does not. One day, their mom makes pizza for lunch. Anna is happy, but Ben is sad. He does not want to eat pizza. He thinks pizza is yucky. He says to his mom, "Mom, I do not want pizza. Can I have soup?" Mom says, "No, Ben. Today we have pizza. You have to try it. Maybe you will like it. Pizza is normal food. Many kids like pizza." Ben shakes his head. He does not want to try it. He thinks soup is normal food. He says, "No, mom. I want soup. Soup is normal food. Many kids like soup." Mom sighs. She does not know what to do. She says, "Ben, please listen to me. Pizza is not yucky. It is yummy. It has cheese and sauce and bread. You like cheese and sauce and bread, right?" Ben nods. He likes cheese and sauce and bread. But he does not like pizza. He thinks pizza is different. He says, "Yes, mom. But pizza is not cheese and sauce and bread. Pizza is pizza. It is not normal." Mom smiles. She has an idea. She says, "Ben, do you know what? Pizza is cheese and sauce and bread. But it is also something else. It is a shape. It is a circle. Do you like circles?" Ben nods. He likes circles. He likes to draw circles and play with balls. He thinks circles are fun. He says, "Yes, mom. I like circles. Circles are normal." Mom says, "Good. Then you can try pizza. Pizza is a circle. You can cut it into smaller circles. You can eat one circle at a time. You can pretend it is a ball. You can have fun with pizza." Ben thinks. He looks at the pizza. He sees the cheese and sauce and bread. He sees the circle. He thinks maybe pizza is not so yucky. He thinks maybe pizza is fun. He says, "Okay, mom. I will try pizza. Maybe I will like it." Mom is happy. She cuts the pizza into smaller circles. She gives one to Ben. Ben takes a bite. He tastes the cheese and sauce and bread. He thinks it is yummy. He smiles. He says, "Mom, you are right. Pizza is yummy. Pizza is fun. Pizza is normal." Mom hugs Ben. She says, "I am glad you like pizza, Ben. You see, sometimes you have to try new things. You might find out that they are not so bad. You might find out that they are normal. You might find out that you like them." Anna is happy too. She likes pizza. She likes to share pizza with Ben. She says, "Yes, Ben. Pizza is normal. Pizza is yummy. Pizza is fun. And pizza is better with you." The end. Moral value: The story teaches that sometimes it is good to try new things, even if they seem different or scary. You might discover that they are normal or fun or yummy. You might also discover that you can share them with others and enjoy them more.

One day, a boy named Tim went to school. It was a regular day. He played with his friends and learned new things. Today, Tim learned about math. He liked to count and add numbers. While Tim was in class, his teacher said, "I will send you a math problem to solve." Tim was excited and waited for the problem. But when the teacher gave him the problem, it was not a regular math problem. It was a big problem with lots of numbers! Tim was scared, but he talked to his friend, Sam. Sam said, "Let's try together." They worked on the big math problem, and something unexpected happened. They found out that the problem was not hard at all. They solved it and felt happy. From that day, Tim and Sam loved math even more.

Once upon a time, there was a big lake. Near the lake, there was a tall tree. A little bird lived in the tree. The bird liked to stand on a branch and look at the lake. One day, the bird saw a small boat on the lake. A boy and his dog were in the boat. The boy wore a tight hat on his head. The dog wagged its tail and barked. They were happy. The bird flew down to the boat. The boy and the dog were nice to the bird. They played together all day. When it was time to go home, the bird flew back to its tree. The bird, the boy, and the dog were now friends.

Once upon a time, there was a regular cat named Tom. Tom lived in a small house with his friend, a little girl named Sue. They played together every day and had lots of fun. One day, Tom saw a big pile of waste outside their house. Tom did not like the waste because it made their home look messy. He sighed and thought of a plan to clean it up. He knew Sue would be happy if their home was clean. Tom worked hard to clean up the waste. He picked up each piece and put it in a big bag. When Sue saw what Tom had done, she was so happy. They both smiled and played together in their clean yard.

One day, a little girl named Lily wanted to play with her new toy. She was very excited. But her mother said it was time for a nap. Lily thought naps were boring. She did not want to sleep. She wanted to play. Lily had an idea. She would introduce her toy to her mother. Maybe her mother would like the toy too. Then they could play together. So, Lily showed the toy to her mother. Her mother smiled and said it was a nice toy. But her mother still wanted Lily to take a nap. Lily was sad. She did not want to sleep. But she knew her mother was right. So, Lily took a nap. When she woke up, her mother was waiting. They played with the toy together. Lily was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She had a toy pony that she loved very much. The pony was brown and soft, but it was also a little dirty. Amy took her pony with her everywhere she went. One day, Amy and her pony went to the park to play. They saw a big ball on the ground. Amy picked up the ball and decided to throw it. She threw the ball very far, and her pony watched it fly through the air. Amy and her pony ran to get the ball. When they found it, the ball was dirty too, just like the pony. Amy laughed and hugged her dirty pony. They played with the ball all day long, and they had so much fun together.

Anna likes to play dress-up with her dolls. She has many dolls and many clothes for them. She likes to make them look pretty and have fun. One day, she finds a new blouse in her closet. It is pink and has a big bow on the front. Anna thinks it is very pretty and wants to try it on. She puts it on over her shirt and looks in the mirror. She smiles and twirls around. She decides to show her dolls her new blouse. She picks up her favorite doll, Lily, and says, "Look, Lily, I have a new blouse. Do you like it?" She holds Lily up to the mirror and makes her nod. "Yes, Anna, I like it. You look very pretty," she says in a high voice. She does the same with her other dolls, Molly, Rosie, and Ben. They all say they like her new blouse and tell her she looks very pretty. Anna is very happy and thanks them. She says, "You are all very kind. I love you very much." She hugs her dolls and puts them on her bed. She thinks of a game to play with them. She says, "Let's pretend we are going to a party. We have to dress up and be polite. We have to say hello and bow to everyone." She picks up Lily and makes her bow to Molly. She says, "Hello, Molly. You look very nice today." She picks up Molly and makes her bow to Lily. She says, "Hello, Lily. Thank you. You look very nice too." She does the same with Rosie and Ben. She makes them all bow and say hello to each other. Anna has fun playing dress-up and party with her dolls. She likes her new blouse and her kind dolls. She is a happy girl.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little girl named Lilly. She loved to play outside all day. One day, she saw a long log lying on the ground. Lilly wanted to walk on the log like an independent big girl. Lilly put one foot on the log and tried to balance. At first, she wobbled and almost fell off. But she tried again, and this time she could balance better. Lilly was so happy that she could stand on the log without help. Every day, Lilly practiced walking on the log. She got better and better at balancing. Soon, she could walk all the way across the log without falling. Lilly was proud to be an independent big girl who could balance on a log.

Once upon a time there was a kind boy called Peter. Peter loved to collect things. Every day he went out in the garden to collect leaves, stones and other bits and pieces. One day he saw a clock laying on the ground. “That’s a nice clock,” he thought. He was about to collect it when a voice shouted, “Hey! That’s my clock!” Peter turned around and saw an old man walking towards him. “Please don’t take my clock,” the old man said. Peter felt very sorry and said, “I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to collect it.” But the old man was still mad. He snatched the clock away from Peter and shouted, “Now get out of my garden!” Peter ran away as fast as he could and never came back again. The old man had a bad heart and was not always kind. That day, he not only lost his beloved clock, but he also lost a chance to make a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a warm, sunny day. A little ant named Tim was very busy. He had to march with his friends to find food. Tim saw a big tree with many leaves. He thought it would be a good place to look for food. Under the tree, Tim found a menu. The menu had pictures of food on it. Tim showed the menu to his friend, Sam. Sam said, "Wow! Let's find these foods and take them back to our home!" So, Tim, Sam, and their friends marched together to find the food on the menu. They found apples, nuts, and berries. They carried the food back to their home, feeling very happy. When they got home, they shared the food with their families. Everyone was very happy and thankful. They all enjoyed the warm sun as they ate their food together.

Once upon a time, a deaf little girl found a trunk in the attic. She wanted to hide something important in it, so she grabbed it and ran to her room. Once she was in her room, she opened the trunk and peeked inside. She found a little toy mouse, which was so special that she decided to hide it away. She placed it deep inside the trunk, and closed it tightly with a click. The little girl was very happy that the little mouse was safe and sound, so she decided to find some friends to show it to. She ran downstairs and saw her mom. Excitedly, she said, "Mom, look what I found!" Her mom smiled and said, "That looks like a very special toy! What are you going to do with it?" The little girl said, "I'm going to hide it in the trunk, so nobody can find it!" Her mom nodded and said, "That sounds like a great idea. But remember, whatever you hide must be safe in there forever." The little girl was content. She ran to her room and put the little mouse safely back into the trunk, where it would stay forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Molly. She was very excited because her mum told her about something special. She was going to go to the theater! Molly got ready for the theater. She put on her brown shoes and combed her brown hair. She was excited. When they got to the theater, Molly saw lots of lights and colors. She couldn't believe how big and beautiful it was! She was so excited that she couldn't wait to tell her friends! Molly loved the theater. She watched a movie with her mum and it was the best day ever. When they went home, she told her friends all about it. They were so excited to hear stories about the theater. Molly hadn't been to the theater since then, but when she did, it was still just as special.

Once upon a time, there was a big, wide palace. In this palace, there lived a kind king and queen. They had a little girl named Lily. Lily liked to play with her toys and run in the big, wide garden. One day, Lily saw a small cat outside the palace. The cat was lost and hungry. Lily wanted to help the cat. She took the cat to her mom and dad. "Can we keep the cat?" she asked. The king and queen said yes. They gave the cat food and a warm bed. Lily was happy. The cat was happy too. Now, Lily had a new friend to play with in the big, wide palace. They played and laughed together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful car named Beep. Beep was a happy car that loved to go on drives with his friend, a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and Beep decided to go on a long drive to the park. As they drove, Beep started to feel tired. "Lily, I need fuel," Beep said. Lily knew that Beep needed fuel to go, so they stopped at a fuel place. Lily helped put fuel in Beep, and Beep felt better. They were ready to go to the park again. While they were driving, they saw a big box in the road. Beep stopped, and Lily got out to look at the box. Inside, they found a lot of fun toys! Lily and Beep were so happy! They took the toys to the park and played all day. The day was full of fun and included a big, nice surprise.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very excited because his birthday was coming soon. He knew he would get a gift from his mom and dad. One day, Tim found a mysterious box under his bed. He thought it was his birthday gift! He wanted to open it, but he knew that would spoil the surprise. Tim decided to wait for his birthday. On his birthday, Tim opened the mysterious box. But it was not his gift from mom and dad! Inside the box was a funny hat. Tim laughed and put the hat on his head. Then, mom and dad gave Tim his real gift - a big, shiny ball. Tim was so happy, and he played with his ball and funny hat all day long.

One day, a jolly cat named Tom went for a walk. He saw a big tree with a bird on it. Tom wanted to play with the bird. He said, "Hi bird, can I play with you?" The bird said, "No, do not disturb me. I am busy." Tom felt sad and walked away. He saw a dog on his left. The dog was playing with a ball. Tom asked the dog, "Can I play with you?" The dog said, "Yes, let's play together!" But the bird was still mad. It flew down and took the ball away. The dog said, "Hey, give back my ball!" The bird said, "No, you are too loud. You disturb me." Tom had an idea. He said, "Bird, we will play far away from your tree. We will not disturb you." The bird agreed and gave the ball back. Tom and the dog played together and had lots of fun. They did not disturb the bird, and everyone was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a soft cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to sing. One day, she heard about an opera. Kitty wanted to sing at the opera. Kitty's friend, Doggy, tried to warn her. He said the opera was not safe for little cats. But Kitty did not listen. She wanted to sing and be famous. Kitty went to the opera and started to sing. But then, a big, mean dog came out. The dog chased Kitty away. She was very sad and scared. Kitty should have listened to Doggy's warning.

Once there was a little girl who loved mushrooms. She would spend all day searching for them in the forest. She was very patient and would look closely at all of the plants, hoping to find a delicious mushroom. One day, she was lucky and found a huge brown mushroom! She thanked the forest for giving her the perfect snack and quickly popped it into her mouth. It was delicious! She thanked the forest again for being so kind. Then, the little girl noticed something very strange. She was growing bigger and bigger with every mushroom she ate! She was getting so big that she could barely fit through the door. She thanked the mushrooms for their kindness and decided to give them a rest. The little girl was so pleased with her patience and never gave up looking for mushrooms. Every day, she looks for mushrooms and likes to thank them for all the fun she had in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty lion. The lion was big and strong. He lived in a forest with many trees and animals. One day, the lion saw an image on a tree. The image was a picture of a lion, just like him. He thought it was his friend. The lion went to find his friend in the picture. But he could not find him. The lion was sad. He wanted to play with his friend. So, the lion tried to play with the animals in the forest. But the animals were scared of the mighty lion. They ran away from him. One day, a fire started in the forest. The fire was hot and it burned the trees. The lion was scared. He tried to run away from the fire, but he could not. The fire burned the lion and the image on the tree. The forest was gone, and the mighty lion was gone too. It was a bad ending.

Tim and Mia are best friends. They like to play outside and pretend they are birds. They flap their arms and run around the yard. They say, "We are birds! We can soar in the sky!" One day, it is very hot. Tim and Mia are thirsty and tired. They go inside Tim's house to get some water. Tim's mom says, "Hello, kids. Do you want some ice pops? They are in the freezer." Tim and Mia say, "Yes, please!" They run to the freezer and open it. They see many ice pops of different colors. They each pick one and unwrap it. They lick the ice pops and feel cool and happy. Tim says, "This ice pop is so good. It is red and sweet. What is yours?" Mia says, "Mine is purple and sour. I like it. It makes my mouth tingle." They giggle and finish their ice pops. They thank Tim's mom and go back outside. They say, "We are birds again! We can soar in the sky!" They flap their arms and run around the yard. They are best friends. They are reliable. They always have fun together.

One day, a little girl and her daddy went to the store. They wanted to buy a toy. The girl saw a big, pretty doll. She asked her daddy, "Can I have the doll, please?" Daddy looked at the price. It was not cheap. He said, "Sorry, we can't buy this doll. It's not cheap. Let's find a cheaper toy." The girl was sad, but she understood. They looked around and found a small, cheap toy. It was a little horse that could stand. The girl was happy with the new toy. She said, "Thank you, daddy!" They went home and played together. The girl learned that it's okay to not have the most expensive toy. The cheap toy was just as fun to play with. The moral of the story is that you don't need expensive things to be happy.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lucy found a pretty glass. The glass was small and shiny. Lucy was very happy. One day, Lucy saw a tiny bug near the glass. The bug was patient and did not move. Lucy said, "Hello, little bug. Do you want to be my friend?" The bug nodded and smiled. Lucy wanted to encourage her new friend, the bug. She said, "You can do anything, little bug!" The bug felt happy and strong. Together, Lucy and the bug had lots of fun and played all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with water. One day, she found a spray bottle in her house. She was very happy and ran outside to play with it. Lily saw a sad, miserable cat sitting by the tree. She wanted to help the cat. Lily said, "Hi, cat! I will spray you with water to make you happy." The cat did not like this idea. The cat said, "No, please don't spray me!" But Lily did not listen. She sprayed the cat with water. The cat was very angry and chased Lily. Lily was scared and ran away. Then, something unexpected happened. The cat stopped chasing her and started to laugh. The water had made the cat happy after all. Lily and the cat became best friends. They played with the spray bottle every day. They learned that sometimes, things that seem bad can turn out to be good. And they lived happily ever after.

Once, there was a queen who had a big, pretty dress. The dress was very long and hard to fold. One day, she needed to fold it to put it away. But she was not good at folding. She felt poor at folding. So, she asked her friend, the cat, to help her. The cat tried to fold the queen's dress, but it was too big for her. The cat felt poor at folding too. They both did not know what to do. They were sad. Then, a little mouse came and saw them. The mouse wanted to help. The mouse had a big idea. The mouse told the queen and the cat to each hold one end of the dress. Then, the mouse ran back and forth, folding the dress for them. The queen and the cat were very happy. They did not feel poor at folding anymore. The queen, the cat, and the mouse became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a sweet bird named Lily. She loved to sing happy songs all day long. One day, she saw a big truck outside her tree. The truck had a big word on it, "Operation". Lily did not know what it meant, but she was curious. Lily flew down and saw a kind man named Tom. Tom was working on the truck. Lily asked, "What is 'Operation'?" Tom smiled and said, "It means I fix things that are broken." Lily thought this was very nice. Lily decided to sing a song for Tom while he worked. Her sweet voice made Tom happy. When the work was done, Tom said, "Thank you, Lily! Your singing helped me a lot." Lily was happy she could help and they became good friends.

Once upon a time, in a big garden, there was a little blue flower. The flower was waiting to bloom. It was very excited. The sun was shining bright and the sky was blue. One day, a little girl named Lily came to the garden. She saw the blue flower and said, "Hello, little flower! I can't wait to see you bloom!" The flower smiled and said, "I can't wait too, Lily!" Lily came to the garden every day to see the flower. One day, the flower finally bloomed. It was big and beautiful. Lily was so happy. She brought her yummy snack to share with her new friend, the flower. They had a fun day together in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly cat named Tom. Tom liked to sit near the window and watch the birds fly by. He would wave his tail and smile at the birds. One sunny day, Tom saw a little bird drop a shiny rock outside the window. Tom wanted to play with the shiny rock. So, he jumped out of the window and ran to the rock. Tom played with the shiny rock all day. He was very jolly and happy. When it was time to go home, Tom took the shiny rock with him. He put it near the window so he could look at it every day. And Tom and the shiny rock lived happily ever after.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a fat man with a long white beard and a red coat. He was sitting on a bench with a big sack. "Look, it's Santa!" Lily said. "Let's go and say hello." Ben was not sure. He thought the man looked funny. He did not have any reindeer or a sleigh. He did not look happy. "Maybe he is not Santa," Ben said. "Maybe he is just a man in a costume." Lily did not listen. She ran to the man and smiled. "Hello, Santa," she said. "Are you here to give us presents?" The man looked at Lily and frowned. He did not want to talk to her. He was not Santa. He was a magician. He was waiting for his show to start. He had a lot of tricks in his sack. "Go away, kid," he said. "I'm busy. I'm not Santa. I'm a magic man." Lily was sad. She did not like the man. She thought he was mean. She wanted him to be Santa. "No, you are Santa," she said. "You have a beard and a red coat and a sack. You are Santa and you have to give us presents." She pulled on his sack and tried to open it. The man was angry. He did not want her to touch his sack. He had a lot of secrets in it. "Stop it, kid," he said. "Let go of my sack. You are ruining my magic." Lily did not stop. She insisted. She wanted to see what was in the sack. She wanted to find a present for her and Ben. "Please, Santa, please," she said. "Give us a present. We have been good. We have been very good." The man had enough. He did not like Lily. He did not like kids. He did not like anyone. He wanted to be alone. He wanted to do his magic. He reached into his sack and pulled out a wand. He pointed it at Lily and said a word. "Zap!" Lily felt a tickle on her nose. She sneezed. She looked at her hands. They were covered in fur. She looked at Ben. He was laughing. He pointed at her. "Lily, you are a cat!" he said. "You are a funny cat. You have whiskers and a tail." Lily was shocked. She did not want to be a cat. She wanted to be a girl. She wanted to be herself. She looked at the man. He was smiling. He had a wicked smile. "That's what you get, kid," he said. "That's what you get for bothering me. That's my magic. That's my present for you." He put his wand back in his sack and walked away. He left Lily and Ben in the park. He left Lily as a cat. Lily was scared. She did not know what to do. She did not know how to change back. She did not like being a cat. She wanted to be a girl. She wanted to be Lily. She ran to Ben and meowed. She hoped he would help her. She hoped he would find a way to make her a girl again. Ben was sorry. He did not mean to laugh. He did not like the man. He did not like his magic. He did not like what he did to Lily. He hugged Lily and said, "Don't worry, Lily. Don't worry, cat. I will help you. I will find a way to make you a girl again. I will find a way to break the magic. I will find a way to make you Lily again."

Once upon a time, there were two friends. They loved to eat pizza and play together. One day, they saw that the pizza was all over the room. It was not very organized and there were pieces everywhere. The friends knew that they had to fix the mess. So, they got to work. The first friend found a big box. He put all the pieces of pizza into the box. Then, the second friend found a broom and dustpan. He used them to sweep up all the crumbs from the floor. Finally, the room was fixed and looked very organized! The friends were happy with their work. They knew that it was important to fix things and keep things neat and tidy. The moral of the story is that it is important to stay organized and tidy.

One day, a boy named Tim went to play outside. It was icy and cold, but he wore his big coat. In his pocket, he had a small book and a pen. He wanted to write a story about his fun day in the snow. While Tim was playing, he met a big snowman. The snowman said, "Hello, Tim! Can you help me? I want to write a letter to my friend, but I don't know how." Tim was very surprised that the snowman could talk! Tim said, "Of course I can help you!" He took out his small book and pen from his pocket. They wrote the letter together. When they finished, the snowman thanked Tim and gave him a big icy hug. And that's how Tim made a new friend on a cold, snowy day.

Mama was feeling very hungry and wanted to get something to eat. She asked her 3 year old daughter, "Do you want to go to the store with me?" The daughter was excited and said, "Yes!" Mama explained to her daughter that she had to be very careful in the store. She said, "Remember to look for the labels on the food and only pick the food that say it is okay for you to eat." The daughter smiled and nodded in understanding. They went to the store and her daughter was very good. She looked carefully at all of the labels and chose the food she was allowed to eat. When they got home, the daughter went to get the food out of the bag to eat, but mama stopped her. She said, "I'm sorry but those are not the right foods." The daughter was surprised and asked, "Why not?" Mama explained that she had made a mistake and picked the wrong food. She was so hungry that she had chosen the wrong labels. The daughter was sad and disappointed. She had been so careful to look at the labels, but mama still made a mistake. They had no food to eat and mama just apologized.

One day, a little girl named Lily found a pretty wrap in her room. She put it on and went outside to play. Lily was a thoughtful girl who liked to share her toys with her friends. She saw her friend, Tom, looking sad. Lily asked Tom what was wrong. Tom said he was sad because he lost his ball. Lily wanted to help Tom feel better, so they looked for the ball together. They looked near the trees, behind the bushes, and under the slide. Suddenly, they found the ball in a hole. But when they tried to get the ball out, it was stuck! Lily had an idea. She took off her wrap and used it to pull the ball out of the hole. Tom was so happy and said, "Thank you, Lily!" But then, Lily's wrap got dirty. Tom felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Lily." Lily smiled and said, "I forgive you, Tom. We are friends, and friends help each other." They played together for the rest of the day, and Lily's wrap became a symbol of their friendship.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to swing and slide and run. One day, they see a big bunch of grapes on a table. The grapes are purple and shiny. They look yummy. "Can we have some grapes?" Tom asks Mia. "I don't know. Maybe they belong to someone else," Mia says. "But I'm hungry. And they look so good," Tom says. He reaches for a grape. Mia stops him. "Wait, Tom. We should ask first. Or we can share our snacks. I have a banana and you have a cracker. That's fair," Mia says. Tom thinks for a moment. He likes bananas and crackers. But he likes grapes more. "OK, Mia. I promise I won't take the grapes. Let's eat our snacks," Tom says. He puts his hand behind his back. He crosses his fingers.
