Once upon a time, there was a big red car. It had four round wheels. One day, one wheel went crazy. It did not want to go straight anymore. The car could not drive well. A nice man saw the car with the crazy wheel. He wanted to help. He had a new wheel that was not crazy. The nice man said, "I can change the wheel for you." The car was happy. The nice man took off the crazy wheel and put on the new wheel. But then, something unexpected happened. The new wheel started to talk! It said, "Thank you for changing me. I am a magic wheel. I can make the car fly." The car was so surprised. Now, the car could fly in the sky with its magic wheel. The car and the magic wheel went on many fun adventures together. They became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a baby bear named Bobo. Bobo was very envious of his big brother's crib. His big brother's crib was big and had lots of fun toys. Bobo's crib was small and had only a few toys. One day, Bobo saw his big brother go outside to play. Bobo thought, "Now is my chance to try the big crib!" So, he climbed into his big brother's crib and played with the toys. He was so happy. But then, the weather outside became very cold, and it started to freeze. Bobo's big brother came back inside, and saw Bobo in his crib. He said, "Bobo, that's my crib! You should not be in there!" Bobo did not listen and kept playing. The big brother became very angry and pushed Bobo out of the crib. Bobo fell down and started to cry. The big brother did not help him up, and Bobo was left alone on the floor, sad and hurt.

One day, a little girl named Sue went for a walk in the fog. She saw a broken toy on the ground. Sue was sad for the toy and decided to take it home. Sue showed her mom the broken toy. "Mom, can we fix it?" she asked. Her mom said, "Let's try, but first we need some glue." Sue and her mom looked for glue, but they could not find any. They decided to go to the store. At the store, they found the glue and fixed the toy. Sue was very happy and played with her new toy all day.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a small stream. A little bird named Lily lived near the stream. Lily was very foolish. She did not know how to set her nest. She tried to set it on the ground, but it was not safe there. One day, a big wind came and blew Lily's nest away. She was sad and did not know what to do. Then, she saw a big fish in the stream. The fish saw Lily was sad and asked, "Why are you sad?" Lily told the fish about her nest. The big fish had an idea. He told Lily to set her nest on a tree near the stream. Lily thought it was a good idea. She set her nest on the tree and was very happy. But then, something unexpected happened. The big fish jumped out of the stream and tried to eat Lily's eggs! Lily was scared, but she was brave too. She pushed the big fish back into the stream. The big fish was sad because he could not eat the eggs. In the end, Lily learned not to trust everyone. She knew that she should be careful when setting her nest. She set her nest in a safer place and lived happily with her eggs.

One day, a big storm came to the town. The sky was dark and the wind was strong. A little boy named Tim saw the storm from his window. He wanted to go out and play in the rain, but his mom said, "No, Tim, it's not safe." Tim was sad and felt sour. He did not like being stuck inside. He asked his mom, "Can I just open the door and look?" His mom let him open the door, but told him to stay inside. As Tim looked outside, he saw a big tree near their house. The wind was making the tree move a lot. Tim thought it was fun to watch. He forgot about the storm and felt happy. But then, the big tree fell down. It hit Tim's house and made a big hole. Water came in and everything got wet. Tim's mom was sad and said, "We should have closed the door and stayed away from the storm." Now Tim knew that when there is a storm, it is better to stay safe inside and not let the storm come in.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the zoo with his mom. He was so happy, he started to skip. At the zoo, they saw many animals like big lions, tall giraffes, and funny monkeys. Then, they went to see the snakes. Tim was scared of snakes. He held his mom's hand tight. His mom told him not to be scared. She said the snakes could not hurt him. Tim felt better and started to skip again. They saw more animals and had a fun day at the zoo. Tim was not scared anymore. He could not wait to come back to the zoo again.

Once upon a time, in a bright, sunny house, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to play outside with her dog, Max. They would run, jump, and laugh together all day long. Lucy's mom would make dinner for the family every night, and Lucy always looked forward to it. One day, Lucy and Max were playing near the kitchen, and they saw a big bowl of yummy food. Lucy thought it was for them to eat right away. So, Lucy and Max ate all the food in the big bowl. They were so happy and full, but they did not know that they had just eaten dinner for the whole family. When Lucy's mom came into the kitchen, she saw the empty bowl and knew that Lucy and Max had spoiled dinner. She was very sad and told Lucy that they could not have any more food that night. Lucy felt bad and said sorry to her mom. That night, everyone went to bed hungry because there was no dinner. From that day on, Lucy learned to wait for her mom to tell her when it was time to eat.

Once upon a time, there lived two funny animals. A bunny and a gopher. They were very good friends. One day they decided to go for a walk in the woods. As they walked, the bunny noticed a twig on the ground. It was colorful and sparkly. She picked it up and wondered what it was. Suddenly, a few more twigs began to fall from the sky. The bunny was so excited that she began to jump around. She and the gopher watched as twigs fell everywhere in a circle around them. Then, all of a sudden, the twigs began to move. The bunny and the gopher gasped. They were so amazed! The twigs moved around in a funny way, spinning and changing colors. It was like a mini, colorful twig show! The bunny and the gopher watched the twig show until it ended. They both wondered what it was, but neither of them could find out. But that didn't matter. They enjoyed the show, and had lots of fun together!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy loved to collect crayons. She had many colors like red, blue, and yellow. Every day, she would sit in her comfortable chair and draw pretty pictures with her crayons. One day, Amy's friend, Tom, came over to play. "Amy, can I use your crayons?" Tom asked. "Yes, of course!" Amy said. They started drawing together, having lots of fun. They drew a big sun, a green tree, and a blue bird. Suddenly, as they were drawing, something unexpected happened. The crayons started to talk! "Hi, Amy and Tom!" said the red crayon. "We want to play too!" The children were so surprised, but they laughed and played with the talking crayons. They all had a great time, and it was the most fun day ever.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was 3 years old and very adventurous. One day, she found an old trumpet in the woods while she was playing. It looked very wet, but the little girl wanted to use it. "Mommy, I found a trumpet," she excitedly said. Her mommy gave her a big smile. "What are you going to use it for?" she asked. The little girl thought for a moment. "I'm going to use it to make music with, of course!" she said proudly. The little girl went back to the woods and started to play the trumpet. The sounds came out wet and warbly, but the little girl kept playing and making beautiful music. Soon, the whole forest was filled with her music. The little girl smiled and said, "Mommy, look at what I can do with my trumpet!" Her mommy smiled and said, "I'm so proud of you, sweetie. You're a very special and talented little girl."

One day, a cat named Bob went to search for some food. He was very hungry and wanted to find his favorite food, tuna. Bob had a serious look on his face as he looked around the kitchen. He saw a big can on the table. Bob jumped up and sniffed it. It smelled like tuna! He was very happy. But the can was closed, so he needed help to open it. Bob went to find his friend, Sam the dog. He asked, "Sam, can you help me open the tuna can?" Sam wagged his tail and said, "Yes, let's go!" They went back to the kitchen and worked together to open the can. Then, they shared the tasty tuna and had a great meal.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was a very persistent dog. He loved to play and run around all day. One day, Spot saw a big cat named Whiskers. Whiskers did not like to play with dogs. But Spot wanted to be friends with Whiskers. Spot said to Whiskers, "Let's play together!" Whiskers did not want to play with Spot. But Spot did not give up. He tried again and again to be friends with Whiskers. Whiskers finally said, "Okay, we can play together. But only for a little bit." As they played, they found a big door. The door had a sign that said "Veterinarian." Spot and Whiskers did not know what that meant, but they wanted to find out. They pushed the door open and went inside. Inside, they saw many animals. Some were sick, and some were just there for a check-up. Spot and Whiskers saw a big fish tank with a tiny fish inside. The fish looked sad, so Spot and Whiskers decided to part the water to help the fish. As they parted the water, the fish began to smile. It was a magic fish! The fish said, "Thank you, Spot and Whiskers! Because you helped me, I will grant you one wish." Spot and Whiskers wished to be best friends forever. The fish granted their wish, and they played happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and play with her friends. One day, her uncle came to visit. Lily liked her uncle because he was fun and funny. Her uncle said, "Let's dance, Lily!" They danced in the living room. It was easy and fun. They danced fast, they danced slow, and they even danced like animals. Lily's uncle danced like a monkey, and Lily laughed and laughed. After they danced, Lily and her uncle sat down to rest. Lily said, "I love to dance with you, uncle!" Her uncle smiled and said, "I love to dance with you too, Lily. We can dance together any time you want." And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a helpful little girl named Lily. She loved to play near the river with her friends. One day, while playing, they saw a bridge that they had never seen before. "Let's go and peek!" said Lily. Her friends were scared, but Lily was brave. They walked across the bridge, and on the other side, they found a big, sad dog. "Why are you sad?" asked Lily. The big dog said, "I can't find my way home. I need help." Lily and her friends wanted to help the sad dog. They thought hard and came up with a plan. Together, they walked around the town, asking people if they knew the big dog. Finally, they found the dog's owner, who was very happy to see him. The owner thanked Lily and her friends for being so helpful. The moral of the story is that being helpful and brave can make a big difference in someone's life.

Lily was playing with her dolls in her room. She liked to pretend they were having a tea party. She put a bow on her doll's hair and gave her a cup of juice. She said, "You look very pretty, Miss Daisy. Do you like your juice?" Suddenly, she heard a loud noise from downstairs. It was the telephone ringing. Lily was scared of the telephone. She did not like the sound it made. She thought it was a monster. She hugged her doll and hid under the bed. Her mom heard the telephone and ran to answer it. She said, "Hello, who is this?" It was Lily's grandma. She wanted to talk to Lily and see how she was doing. She said, "Can I speak to Lily, please?" Lily's mom went to her room and looked for her. She saw her hiding under the bed. She said, "Lily, what are you doing? Grandma is on the phone. She wants to say hi to you." Lily peeked out from under the bed. She saw her mom holding the telephone. She was still scared, but she wanted to talk to grandma. She said, "Hi, grandma. I'm sorry. I was playing with my doll. I'm scared of the telephone." Grandma heard Lily's voice and smiled. She said, "Don't be scared, Lily. The telephone is not a monster. It is a way to talk to people who are far away. I love you, Lily. You are very brave." Lily felt better. She said, "I love you too, grandma. Thank you for calling me. Can I show you my doll? She has a bow on her hair." Grandma said, "Yes, of course. I would love to see your doll. She sounds very pretty. Can you hold her up to the phone?" Lily did as grandma asked. She held her doll up to the phone and said, "This is Miss Daisy. She is my best friend. She likes juice and tea parties." Grandma said, "She is adorable, Lily. You are very good at taking care of her. I'm proud of you, Lily. You are a wonderful girl." Lily smiled. She was not scared of the telephone anymore. She said, "Thank you, grandma. You are the best grandma ever. Can I talk to you again soon?" Grandma said, "Yes, of course. You can call me anytime you want. I'm always happy to hear from you. Goodbye, Lily. I love you very much." Lily said, "Goodbye, grandma. I love you too. Have a nice day." Lily's mom hugged her and said, "You did great, Lily. You are very brave and polite. I'm glad you talked to grandma. She misses you a lot." Lily said, "I miss her too, mom. Can we visit her soon?" Lily's mom said, "Yes, we can. Maybe next weekend. How about that?" Lily said, "That would be awesome, mom. I can't wait to see grandma. And maybe she can see my doll too." Lily's mom said, "I'm sure she would love that, Lily. Now, do you want to continue your tea party?" Lily said, "Yes, please. Can you join us, mom?" Lily's mom said, "Sure, why not. Let me get another cup of juice." Lily said, "Yay, thank you, mom. You are the best mom ever." Lily and her mom went back to her room. They played with her doll and had a fun tea party. Lily was happy and not scared anymore. She learned that the telephone was not a monster, but a friend.

Once upon a time, there was a small red jeep. The jeep loved to go on adventures. One day, the jeep decided to collect pretty rocks. The jeep went up a high hill to find the most beautiful rocks. It found a big, shiny, blue rock. The jeep was very happy and put the rock in its trunk. The jeep went back down the hill to show its friends the pretty rock it collected. All the friends loved the rock and they played together. The little red jeep was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Timmy. Timmy lived in a small nest on a roof of a big house. One day, Timmy saw a big, red ball in the yard. He wanted to play with it, so he flew down to the ground. Timmy pushed the ball with his beak and it rolled. He was very glad. Then, he saw a little girl named Sue. Sue saw Timmy playing with the ball and smiled. She said, "Hi, Timmy! Do you want to play with me?" Timmy nodded and they played together. They had so much fun. As they played, Timmy became Sue's best friend. From that day on, Timmy and Sue always played together and they were very happy.

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there was a little lion named Leo. Leo loved to roar very loud. One day, Leo found a tool. It was a big stick. He thought it was a reliable tool to play with. Leo went to his friend, the monkey named Max. "Max, look at my new tool!" Leo said. Max looked at the stick and wanted to play too. They played with the stick all day long. But then, the stick broke. Leo and Max were sad. They could not play with the stick anymore. The day had a bad ending, but they still had each other to play with.

One day, a little cat named Kitty went into the kitchen. She saw a big, rough oven. Kitty was very curious and wanted to look inside. She jumped up and opened the oven door. Kitty blinked her eyes, surprised by what she saw. Inside the oven, there was a big party! All her animal friends were there. The oven was not hot at all. It was a magic oven! The animals were playing games and eating yummy food. Kitty blinked her eyes again, making sure she was not dreaming. Kitty joined the party and had lots of fun with her friends. They played games and ate cake until it was time to go home. When the party was over, the magic oven turned back into a normal, rough oven. Kitty blinked her eyes one last time, and she knew it was a special day she would never forget.

Lily and Ben were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and bridges and castles. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes. "Look, Lily, I made a big tower!" Ben said, showing his creation to his sister. "Wow, Ben, that's very good!" Lily said. "Can I help you make it bigger?" "Sure, Lily, you can. Here, take some blocks and put them on top." Ben said, handing her some blocks. They worked together, adding more and more blocks to the tower. They were having fun and did not notice that their mom was calling them for lunch. "Lily, Ben, lunch is ready! Come to the kitchen, please!" Mom said from the other room. Lily and Ben heard mom, but they did not want to stop playing. They wanted to finish their tower. "Just one more block, mom!" Ben said. "Me too, mom!" Lily said. They put the last blocks on the tower and paused to admire their work. It was very tall and colorful. They were proud of themselves. "Okay, mom, we're coming!" Ben said. They got up and started to walk to the kitchen. But they did not see that their dog, Spot, was lying on the floor behind them. Spot was sleeping and did not hear mom either. Lily and Ben tripped over Spot and fell down. Their tower fell down too. The blocks went everywhere. Spot woke up and barked. Mom came to see what happened. "Oh, no, what a mess!" Mom said. "Are you okay, Lily and Ben?" Lily and Ben were not hurt, but they were sad. They looked at their broken tower and the scattered blocks. They felt like they wasted their time. "We're sorry, mom. We didn't see Spot. We wanted to show you our tower." Lily said. "We worked hard on it, mom. It was very big." Ben said. Mom hugged them and said, "It's okay, sweeties. I'm sure your tower was very nice. But you have to listen to me when I call you for lunch. And you have to be careful not to step on Spot. He's part of the family too." Lily and Ben nodded and said, "We're sorry, mom. We love you and Spot." Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. Now, let's go to the kitchen and have some lunch. You must be hungry. And after lunch, we can clean up the blocks together." Lily and Ben agreed and followed mom to the kitchen. They felt better and hungry. They hoped that Spot would not be mad at them. They also hoped that they could play with their blocks again later. They still liked to build towers and bridges and castles.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys and books and a big lamp that gave them light. One day, their mom said they could decorate the lamp with stickers and ribbons. Anna and Ben were very happy and ran to their room. Anna wanted to put pink stickers and ribbons on the lamp, because pink was her favorite color. Ben wanted to put blue stickers and ribbons on the lamp, because blue was his favorite color. They both grabbed the stickers and ribbons and tried to put them on the lamp. But they did not share or take turns. They pulled and pushed and shouted at each other. "Stop it, Anna! I want blue on the lamp!" Ben said. "No, Ben! I want pink on the lamp!" Anna said. They fought so hard that they knocked over the lamp. The lamp fell on the floor and broke. The light went out and the room became dark. Anna and Ben stopped fighting and looked at the lamp. They felt sad and scared. "Mommy! Daddy! Help!" they cried. Their mom and dad came to their room and saw the broken lamp. They were not happy. They asked Anna and Ben what happened. Anna and Ben told them the truth. They said they were sorry and hugged each other. Their mom and dad said they were glad they said sorry, but they still had to clean up the mess and learn to share. They helped them pick up the pieces of the lamp and the stickers and ribbons. They said they would buy a new lamp for them, but they had to agree on how to decorate it. Anna and Ben said they would share and take turns. They said they would use both pink and blue on the lamp, and make it look incredible. They said they loved each other and their mom and dad. They said they learned their lesson. They smiled and hugged again.

One day, a little dog named Mark went for a walk. He loved to play in the dirt. Mark became very dirty. He liked being dirty. Mark was a happy dog. As Mark played, he heard a loud noise. It was thunder! Mark was scared. He ran back home as fast as he could. The thunder followed him. He did not like the thunder. When Mark got home, he found a big surprise. His owner had a bath ready for him. Mark did not want a bath. But then, the thunder made another loud noise. Mark jumped into the bath. He found out that he liked the bath. It made the thunder less scary. Now, Mark was a clean and happy dog.

Once upon a time, there was a painter named Tom. Tom liked to paint pretty pictures of trees, flowers, and animals. He was very good at it. But one day, Tom felt very tired. He had been painting for many days, and he needed a break. Tom decided to go for a walk in the park. He saw a little girl named Sue playing with her ball. Sue saw Tom and said, "Hi! You look tired. Do you want to play with me?" Tom smiled and said, "Yes, I would like that." They played together, and Tom started to feel better. Sue made him laugh when she made funny faces. After playing, Tom said, "Thank you, Sue. I had fun and I am not tired anymore." Sue smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tom. Let's play again soon." Tom agreed, and they both went home, happy and ready for a good night's sleep.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a gloomy house. The house had a big tree and a little dog. The dog was sad because he did not have any friends to play with. One day, a little girl named Amy came to the house. She saw the sad dog and wanted to meet him. Amy went to the owner of the house and asked if she could play with the dog. The owner said yes, but only for a little while. Amy and the dog played in the yard. They had so much fun, but then it was time for Amy to go home. The dog was sad again because he did not want his friend to leave. Amy promised to come back and play with the dog again. The next day, it was raining and Amy could not go outside to play with the dog. The dog was very sad and missed his friend. He waited and waited for the rain to stop, but it did not. Amy never came back to play with the dog. The dog stayed sad and lonely in the gloomy house. The owner tried to find a new friend for the dog, but no one wanted to play with him. The dog lived a sad life without a friend to play with.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a lady who loved the color purple. She had a big purple house, a small purple car, and even a tiny purple dog. Every day, she wore a purple dress and purple shoes. One sunny day, the lady went to the park. She saw a big purple ball on the grass. She was very happy and wanted to play with it. So, she ran to the ball and grabbed it with her hands. She threw the ball high in the sky and her tiny purple dog chased after it. As the lady played with the purple ball, a little girl came up to her. The girl was sad because she lost her ball. The lady knew the purple ball was the girl's. She gave the ball back to the girl and they played together. They laughed and had fun. From that day on, the lady and the girl became very good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a popular cat named Tom. Tom loved to play in the kitchen. One day, Tom saw a little mouse in the kitchen. The mouse was scared of Tom. Tom said, "Don't be scared, little mouse. I will protect you." The mouse was happy and thanked Tom. They became good friends and played together. Soon, all the other animals saw how Tom protected the mouse. They wanted to be friends with Tom too. Tom became even more popular and everyone loved him. And they all played happily in the kitchen together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to travel with her family. One day, they went to a big forest. In the forest, there were many tall trees. Lucy saw a big pine tree and was glad. Lucy said to her mom, "Look, mom! A big pine tree!" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, it is very big and pretty." They walked and played near the pine tree. Lucy found a pine cone and showed it to her dad. Her dad said, "That's a nice pine cone, Lucy!" After playing, Lucy and her family were tired. They sat under the big pine tree to rest. They were very glad to have traveled to the forest and found the big pine tree. They had a lot of fun and went home happy.

Jen and Ben are twins. They like to watch TV after school. But they do not like the same shows. Jen likes to watch cartoons. Ben likes to watch animals. One day, they have a big fight. Jen wants to watch her cartoons. Ben wants to watch his animals. They both grab the remote and pull. They yell at each other. "Let me watch my cartoons!" Jen says. "No, let me watch my animals!" Ben says. They do not share. They do not take turns. They are not fair. Mom hears them and comes to the living room. She sees them fighting. She is not happy. She takes the remote and turns off the TV. "Stop fighting, Jen and Ben!" Mom says. "You need to learn to share and take turns. That is fair." She tells them to sit on the couch and talk. She gives them a paper and a crayon. She tells them to make a schedule. "You can add the shows you want to watch on the paper. Then you can divide the time. One hour for Jen, one hour for Ben. That is fair." Mom says. Jen and Ben look at the paper. They think for a while. They write down the shows they want to watch. They draw a line in the middle. They show Mom. "Look, Mom, we made a schedule. We can share and take turns. That is fair." Jen and Ben say. Mom smiles. She is proud of them. She gives them a hug and a kiss. She turns on the TV. "Good job, Jen and Ben. You can watch your shows now. But remember to follow the schedule. That is fair." Mom says. Jen and Ben nod. They sit on the couch and watch their shows. They do not fight. They are happy. They are fair.

There were two friends Sally and Jack. They were walking through the park together. Sally saw a pick laying on the ground. She wanted to join it and took the pick back home with her. At home, her room was very charming. She put the pick in the corner and then looked for Jack. Jack was still in the park looking for more picks. She called for him and he came running back. Sally showed Jack the pick she had brought back home. They both smiled in delight and decided to play with the pick. Jack found a ball and Sally set up their game. They had so much fun, bouncing the ball back and forth and then hitting the pick from different angles. They played together for a long time. Eventually, Sally got tired, so she joined Jack on the floor and they fell asleep. All was peaceful and quiet and they both had a wonderful dream together.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. It was a cool night. Tim saw a big sack on the ground. He asked his mom, "What's in the sack?" His mom said, "I don't know, Tim. Let's open it and see." They opened the sack, and inside were many toys. Tim was very happy. Tim wanted to take all the toys home, but his mom said, "No, Tim, we must share the toys with the other kids in the park." Tim didn't want to share, but he listened to his mom. They gave the toys to the other kids, and everyone was happy. Tim learned that sharing is good, and it makes everyone happy.

Once there was an old man who was very compassionate. Every day, he would lie down and take a nap beside his pipe. He would rest his head on the pipe while dreaming of the sunny days. One day, a little three year old girl wandered over to the old man. She was curious about what he was doing lying down like that all the time! The old man looked kind and compassionate, so she was not afraid. The old man smiled, and told her that he was taking a nap. He explained to her that he liked to lie down and rest; it was his favorite thing to do. The little girl was fascinated and asked him why he chose to use the pipe as a pillow. The old man smiled and said that he liked the feel of the pipe against his head. He said it made him feel safe and comfortable. The little girl thanked the old man for being so compassionate, then she waved goodbye and ran off to go play. From then on, the old man continued to take naps beside his pipe every day and the little girl would come back to check on him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play with his red bricks. Tim would build tall towers, big houses, and long roads with his bricks. He had so much fun playing with them every day. One sunny day, Tim saw his friend Sue playing outside. Sue was playing with her own bricks. Tim felt a little embarrassed because he had never played with anyone else before. But he wanted to join Sue and play together. So, he picked up his red bricks and walked over to Sue. "Can I join you?" Tim asked shyly. Sue smiled and said, "Yes, let's play together!" They both started to build a big house with their bricks. They laughed and had so much fun. From that day on, Tim and Sue played with their bricks together and became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a violin. He loved to play it every day. One day, he went to the park with his mom and his violin. At the park, he saw a girl named Sue. Sue wanted to play with his violin. Tim said, "Do you want to play my violin?" Sue said, "Yes, please!" So, Tim passed the violin to Sue. Sue played it and made a very loud noise. It scared a bird in a tree. The bird flew away. Sue felt guilty for scaring the bird. She said, "I'm sorry, bird." Tim said, "It's okay. Let's play together and be friends." So, Tim and Sue played the violin and had lots of fun at the park. And the bird came back to listen to their music.

Once upon a time, there was a little humble car. The car had many gears. One day, the car went for a ride with its friend, the big truck. The car and the truck were having fun. The car said, "I like to go fast with my gears!" The truck said, "I like to go slow and carry heavy things." As they played, they saw a small bike. The bike was sad. The car and the truck stopped and asked, "Why are you sad, little bike?" The bike said, "I have only one gear, and I cannot go fast or carry heavy things like you." The car and the truck smiled and said, "We can help you. We can all play together." So, the humble car, the big truck, and the small bike played together all day. They learned that even with different gears, they could have fun and be friends.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely bird. The bird lived in a cage. The cage was in a big tree. The bird liked to sing and play. One day, the door of the cage opened. The lovely bird flew away. It saw many new things. It played with other birds. It was fun. But the lovely bird missed its cage. It wanted to return home. So, it flew back to the big tree. It found its cage and went inside. The lovely bird was happy to be home again. It sang a happy song.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max liked to wander around the big park. He would run, jump, and play with his ball. Max was a tough dog, and he was not scared of anything. One day, Max saw a big cat. The cat said, "You can't play here, this is my park!" Max did not like this threat. He wanted to play in the park with his ball. Max said, "I am tough, and I can play here too." Max and the cat talked and decided to share the park. They played together and had lots of fun. From that day on, Max and the cat were best friends. They learned that it is better to share and be nice to each other.

Tom and Mia are best friends. They like to play in the park every day. They have a loyal dog named Spot who follows them everywhere. Spot likes to run, jump and bark. One day, Tom and Mia find a big open space in the park. It has green grass and yellow flowers. They decide to have a picnic there. They spread a blanket on the ground and take out their sandwiches and juice. "Look, Spot, we have food for you too!" Mia says, holding a bone. Spot wags his tail and runs to Mia. He takes the bone and chews it happily. "Can I have some of your juice, Tom?" Mia asks, looking at Tom's cup. "Sure, Mia, you can have some. We are best friends, we share everything." Tom says, handing Mia his cup. "Thank you, Tom, you are very kind." Mia says, taking a sip. They eat and drink and talk and laugh. They are very happy. Spot is happy too. He loves Tom and Mia. He is a loyal dog. He stays with them and protects them. He is their best friend too.

Ben likes to work with his dad. His dad works at the post office. He puts letters in envelopes and stamps them. Ben helps him sometimes. He likes to see the different stamps and the different places the letters go. One day, Ben and his dad go to work together. But when they get there, they see a big problem. There is a big hole in the roof. The rain came in and made the letters wet. Some of the envelopes are torn and some of the stamps are gone. Ben and his dad are sad. They want to send the letters to the people who are waiting for them. Ben's dad says they have to work hard and fast. He says they have to find new envelopes and stamps and write the addresses again. He says they have to be dependable. That means they do what they say they will do. Ben wants to be dependable too. He says he will help his dad. Ben and his dad work together. They find new envelopes and stamps. They look at the wet letters and try to read the addresses. Sometimes they can read them and sometimes they can't. They ask the other people who work at the post office to help them. They work and work until they finish. Ben and his dad are happy. They send the letters to the people who are waiting for them. They are dependable. They did what they said they would do. The people who get the letters are happy too. They thank Ben and his dad for their hard work. Ben and his dad hug each other. They are proud of each other. They go home and tell mom what they did. Mom is proud of them too. She gives them a big hug and a big kiss. She says they are the best. Ben and his dad smile. They are happy. They like to work together.

Once upon a time there was a brilliant girl. She loved to study the universe! She would spend hours watching the stars, learning about the planets, and imagining what else might be out there. One day her dreams came true. The brilliant girl was invited to take a special trip to explore the universe. She eagerly packed her bags and was soon off on her incredible journey. For weeks she flew across the stars, visiting all sorts of planets and discovering amazing new things. Each day she wrote down her findings in her special book, learning more and more about the universe. Finally, when the brilliant girl arrived back home, she was ready to share her incredible adventure with her family. She opened her book and taught them all sorts of fun facts about the universe. The little girl was so happy that she had been able to study the universe and learn so much!

Once upon a time, there was a big van. The van was blue and shiny. It liked to go fast on the road. The van had a friend, a little girl named Lily. Lily was very obedient. She always listened to her mom and dad. One day, the van and Lily went to the park. They saw a lot of kids playing. Lily wanted to play too, but she was shy. The van told Lily, "Don't be scared. You can make new friends." So Lily went to play with the kids. They played with a ball and had a lot of fun. When it was time to go home, Lily was happy. She said to the van, "Thank you for helping me. I want to pray and say thank you to God." Lily and the van went home. Lily prayed with her mom and dad. She thanked God for her new friends and the fun day. The van was happy too. It knew that Lily was a good girl, and they would have more fun days together.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play with dolls and cars and books. One day, they decided to play marry. They put on their parents' clothes and rings and found a big carpet in the living room. "Let's pretend this is a church," Lily said. "You be the groom and I be the bride." "OK," Ben said. "But who will be the priest?" They looked around and saw Lily's cat, Fluffy, sleeping on the sofa. "Fluffy can be the priest," Lily said. "He is mild and nice and he likes us." They picked up Fluffy and put him on a chair. Then they walked on the carpet, holding hands. "Do you, Ben, take Lily to be your wife?" Fluffy meowed. "I do," Ben said. "Do you, Lily, take Ben to be your husband?" Fluffy meowed again. "I do," Lily said. They leaned in to kiss, but Fluffy did not like that. He hissed and scratched their faces. They screamed and let go of him. Fluffy jumped off the chair and ran away. Lily and Ben cried and ran to their parents. Their parents were angry and shocked. They scolded them for playing with their clothes and rings and for hurting Fluffy. They took them to the doctor to get bandages and medicine. Lily and Ben learned their lesson. They never played marry again. They were still friends, but they played with other things. They also stayed away from Fluffy, who was not so mild after all.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy cat named Tom. Tom had a friend, a little dog named Max. One day, Tom and Max found a letter on the ground. They were very curious about the letter. They decided to share the letter and read it together. As they read the letter, they saw that it was from a bird named Sam. The letter said that Sam had lost his way and needed help. Tom and Max wanted to help Sam, so they went on a big adventure to find him. After a long search, they found Sam. But, surprise! Sam was not a bird, he was a frog! Tom and Max were very happy to have a new friend, and they all shared a big laugh. From that day on, they all played together and shared many more adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to draw with his white chalk. One sunny day, he went outside to draw on the sidewalk. Tim saw a little plant growing near the sidewalk. He decided to draw a big, white sun next to the plant. "This will help you grow, little plant," said Tim. The plant seemed to smile at Tim. The next day, Tim went outside to check on the little plant. It had grown bigger! Tim was so happy. He drew more white suns around the plant. "Keep growing, little plant!" Tim said. And the plant grew and grew, thanks to Tim's white chalk suns.

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary cow named Molly. Molly lived on a farm with other cows. Every day, she would eat grass and give milk to the farmer. One sunny day, Molly saw a little girl named Lily. Lily was looking for milk to drink with her snack. Molly said, "I can give you milk!" Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Molly!" Lily drank the milk and it was very good. She said, "This is the best milk I have ever had!" Molly was happy to help. From that day on, Molly and Lily were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a generous boy named Tim. Tim loved to play in the sand at the park. One sunny day, Tim went to the park with his toy trucks to play in the sand. While Tim was playing, a new boy named Sam came to the park. Sam wanted to play in the sand too. But Sam did not want to share the sand with Tim. Sam said, "No, this is my sand!" Tim felt sad. Tim thought for a moment and decided to accept Sam's words. He said, "Okay, we can both play in the sand." Sam smiled and they started to play together. They had lots of fun and became good friends. And from that day on, they always shared the sand at the park.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom and dad. One day, they see a big hill with many steps. They want to climb the hill and see what is on top. Mom and dad say they can go, but they have to be careful and hold hands. Anna and Ben are glad. They start to climb the steps. They count one, two, three, four, five, and so on. They see birds and flowers and bugs on the way. They have fun. But when they get to the top, they are very tired. They sit on the grass and look at the sky. They see clouds and planes and a big sun. They feel warm and happy. They lie on the grass and close their eyes. They rest for a while. Mom and dad come to the top too. They see Anna and Ben lying on the grass. They smile and sit next to them. They hug them and say they are proud of them. They say they can stay for a bit, but then they have to go back down. Anna and Ben nod. They are sleepy, but they are also hungry. They wonder what is for lunch. They hope it is something yummy. They love their mom and dad. They love the park. They love the hill. They love each other.

Timmy was a very envious little boy. Every time he saw his older brother playing in the hallway with his new toys, he wished he had something as fun and exciting. One day, his mom told them both to go play in the backyard. Timmy started playing in the sandbox and soon enough he had built the biggest castle he had ever seen. He was so proud he ran back inside to show his mother. When Timmy got back to the hallway, he saw his brother had the same castle. He was so envious! He couldn't believe how his brother had the same castle. He said to his brother, “How did you make the same castle as me?” His brother replied, “I have been working hard to make it. It didn't happen overnight.” Timmy realized that with persistence and hard work comes great reward. He knew if he wanted something, he had to be willing to put in the effort to get it.

One day, a little girl named Lucy wanted to help her mother. Her mother was doing a difficult job. She was trying to fix a big hole in a sock. Lucy asked, "Mother, can I help you?" Her mother smiled and said, "Yes, Lucy. You can help me by finding a small sock for the little hole." Lucy looked around and found a small sock. She brought it to her mother. Her mother was happy and said, "Thank you, Lucy. You are a big help!" Together, they fixed the sock. Lucy felt proud that she could help her mother with the difficult job. From that day on, Lucy always tried to help her mother with anything she could. And her mother was always happy to have her help.

Ben likes to study ants. He has a book with pictures of ants and he learns their names and what they do. He likes to watch them in the garden, how they carry food and dig tunnels. He thinks ants are smart and busy. One day, he sees a big ant hill near the fence. He wants to study it closer, so he brings his book and a magnifying glass. He kneels down and looks at the ants. He sees red ants and black ants and some ants with wings. He says, "Wow, so many ants!" But then, he hears a loud bark. It is Rex, the neighbor's dog. Rex is big and scary and he does not like Ben. He runs towards the ant hill, barking and growling. He wants to dig up the ants and chase Ben away. Ben is afraid. He does not want Rex to hurt the ants or him. He shouts, "No, Rex, bad dog! Go away!" He picks up his book and his magnifying glass and runs to the house. He hopes the ants are safe. He tells his mom what happened. She hugs him and says, "I'm sorry, Ben. Rex is a mean dog. He should not bother you or the ants. You are brave and kind. You love to study ants and learn new things. Maybe we can find another ant hill for you to study. A more mysterious one, where Rex can't find it."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved the color purple. One day, she found an empty box in her room. She was very excited and wanted to fill it with her favorite things. Lily went to her friend, Tim. She said, "Tim, I have an empty box. I want to fill it with purple things. Can you help me find purple things that match?" Tim smiled and said, "Yes, Lily! Let's go find purple things!" They looked all around and found many purple things. They found a purple ball, a purple doll, and a purple hat. They put all the purple things in the empty box. Lily and Tim were very happy. They had a lot of fun matching the purple things and filling the empty box.

Tom and Mia were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They liked to make them zoom and crash and beep. They had a lot of cars, but they only had one fuel station. The fuel station was a small plastic box with a hole and a pipe. They pretended that the cars needed fuel to run. "Can I use the fuel station now?" Mia asked Tom. She had a pink car that was very fast. "No, it's my turn. You have to wait." Tom said. He had a blue car that was very strong. "But you already used it twice. It's not fair." Mia said. She felt angry and sad. "I don't care. It's mine. Go away." Tom said. He pushed Mia's car away with his foot. Mia cried and ran to their mom. She told her what Tom did. Mom was not happy. She went to the garden and saw Tom playing with the fuel station. "Tom, what are you doing? Why are you being mean to Mia?" Mom asked. "I'm not mean. I just want to play with the fuel station. It's mine." Tom said. "No, it's not. It's ours. We share it. You have to include Mia in your game. She is your sister and your friend." Mom said. "But I don't want to. She always wants my things." Tom said. "That's not true. She has her own things too. And sometimes you want her things. That's normal. But you have to be kind and generous. How would you feel if she did the same to you?" Mom said. Tom thought for a little while. He remembered how he felt when Mia took his favorite teddy bear. He felt bad and lonely. "I would feel sad." Tom said. "Exactly. So, do you think you can say sorry to Mia and let her use the fuel station too?" Mom said. Tom nodded. He went to Mia and hugged her. "I'm sorry, Mia. I was wrong. You can use the fuel station too. Do you want to play with me?" Tom said. Mia smiled and wiped her tears. "Thank you, Tom. I'm sorry too. I want to play with you. Can we take turns?" Mia said. "Sure. Let's do that. And maybe we can make a race or a story with our cars. That would be fun." Tom said. They took their cars and the fuel station and played together. Mom watched them and smiled. She was proud of them. They learned to include each other and share. They had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a serious boy named Johnny. Whenever he had something he didn't like, he always complained. One day, he was too noisy complaining, so his mother brought out a special glass and told him he could only complain into it from now on. At first Johnny thought it was silly, but soon he realized how useful it was. Whenever he was angry, he could just talk into the glass and feel better. One day, Johnny was walking through the park when he saw a new friend. But his new friend was not very nice and kept picking on him. Every time the new friend did something bad, Johnny complained into the glass. The next day, when Johnny and his new friend were at the park, Johnny went to the same spot they were at the previous day. Suddenly, the new friend started to complain. Johnny realized he was complaining into the same glass his mother had given him! Johnny smiled at his friend and said, "It's okay if you have something to say. You can complain into this glass too." From that day onwards, Johnny and his new friend became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there a was a lazy man named Tom. Every day, Tom did not want to do anything; he just wanted to lie in the sun and relax. One day, his mother decided to encourage him to learn something. She suggested to Tom to learn history, so he could have a better understanding of the world. Tom was not interested to learn at all, so he said: "I don’t want to learn, I am lazy". But his mother understood and encouraged him: "You never know, you might like it and even become passionate about history". Tom’s mother was right in the end: despite his initial reluctance, Tom ended up enjoying learning about the past, and he became a history expert. His mother was proud of him for continuing to learn.

Once there was a fierce bear who wanted to celebrate. He looked around and saw some plastic cupcakes, so he decided that it was the perfect way to celebrate. He grabbed one of the cupcakes and waved it around and said “Let’s celebrate!” But then he heard someone laugh. He turned around and saw a small rabbit. The rabbit said “That’s a silly way to celebrate. You should find something else.” The bear looked around and saw some plastic streamers. He grabbed one of the streamers and started to swing it around as he said “Now this is how to celebrate!” The rabbit laughed and said “That’s much better! Now it looks like we’re really celebrating.” The fierce bear and the small rabbit celebrated with the plastic cupcakes and streamers all day long. They had lots of fun celebrating together.

Ben and Mia like to play in the old house. The old house is big and dark and has many rooms. They pretend they are brave explorers and look for treasure. But they are also scared of ghosts. They think ghosts live in the old house and make noises at night. One day, they find a big box in the attic. The box is dusty and cheap. It has holes and cracks. Ben and Mia open the box and see many things inside. They see clothes and books and toys and pictures. They are happy and start to count the things. "One, two, three, four, five..." Ben counts. "Six, seven, eight, nine, ten..." Mia counts. They hear a voice behind them. The voice is low and spooky. It says: "Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen..." Ben and Mia turn around and scream. They see a ghost. The ghost is white and has no legs. It floats in the air and smiles. It has a hat and a coat and a cane. It looks like one of the pictures in the box. "Hello, children," the ghost says. "Don't be afraid. I'm not a bad ghost. I'm a friendly ghost. I used to live in this house. This box is mine. These are my things. I like to count them too. Do you want to play with me?" Ben and Mia are very scared. They don't want to play with the ghost. They want to run away. They grab each other's hands and run down the stairs. They don't stop until they are outside. They never go back to the old house. They don't like ghosts. They like to count other things.

Once there was a woman who wanted to explain something very difficult. So she invited her three-year-old nephew to listen to her. The woman said, “I’m going to explain something very difficult. Are you ready?” The three-year-old nodded his head. The woman began, “Well, this is something that’s very hard to understand.” But the three-year-old was still confused. He said, “I don’t understand. Can you explain it again?” The woman sighed and said, “No, I will not explain it again. It is too difficult for you to understand.” The three-year-old looked really sad and he started to cry. He said, “I wanted to understand, but it’s too difficult.” The woman said nothing more and just walked away. The three-year-old was left alone, feeling confused and sad.

One day, a bossy cat named Tom went out to play. He saw a big object on the ground. It was round and red. Tom did not know what it was, so he decided to taste it. When Tom tasted the object, it was very sweet. He liked it a lot. He wanted to eat more of it. But then, something unexpected happened. The object started to roll away from him! Tom chased the object as it rolled faster and faster. He almost caught it, but then it jumped into a hole. Tom looked into the hole and saw a little mouse. The mouse was eating the object! Tom was not mad at the mouse. Instead, they became friends and shared the sweet object together.

One day, Tom got a big box of toy cars. He was very happy and proud. He wanted to sort them by color. He put the red cars in one pile, the blue cars in another pile, and the yellow cars in a third pile. Tom's friend, Sue, came over to play with him. "Look at my cars!" Tom said to Sue. "I sorted them by color!" "Wow!" Sue said. "Can I play too?" "Yes!" Tom said, and they started to play with the cars. They made roads and had races. Suddenly, a real car drove into their playroom! The car was red, blue, and yellow, just like Tom's toy cars. Tom and Sue were very surprised. The car stopped, and a clown came out. The clown had a big smile and said, "I heard you like cars! I wanted to show you my car!" Tom and Sue laughed and clapped. They had never seen a real car like this before. They played with the clown and his car all day. It was the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little crab named Billy. Billy lived in a pretty shell near the beach. He loved to play with his friends all day long. One day, Billy started to feel dizzy while playing. He did not know what to do. His friend, Sally the sea star, told him to believe in himself and take a rest. Billy listened to Sally and went back to his pretty shell to rest. He closed his eyes and took a deep breath. After a while, he started to feel better. The next day, Billy felt strong again and went out to play with his friends. He learned that when he felt dizzy, he needed to rest and believe in himself. The moral of the story is to listen to your friends and trust yourself when you need help.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sue. Sue loved to do exercise. She would run, jump, and play all day long. Sue was also very creative. She liked to draw and make things with her hands. One day, Sue went to play in the park. While she was there, she met a new friend named Max. Max liked to exercise too. They ran and jumped together, having lots of fun. Sue thought Max was a great friend. Then something unexpected happened. Max started to fly! Sue was very surprised. Max was not a boy, but a bird! Sue laughed and clapped her hands. She had a bird friend who loved exercise just like her. They played together every day and Sue became even more creative, making bird toys for Max.

Once upon a time, there was a big cat named Tom. Tom was very good at delivering things to his friends. One day, Tom's friend, a small dog named Tim, asked him for help. Tim needed a pan to cook his food. Tom went to his house and found an empty pan. He was very happy to help his friend. Tom carried the pan in his mouth and walked to Tim's house. It was a sunny day, and the birds were singing. When Tom delivered the pan to Tim, Tim was very happy. They both cooked some yummy food together. After they ate, they played outside and had lots of fun. Tom and Tim were very good friends who always helped each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little fairy named Fifi. Fifi had an important job. She had to kick a big red ball every day. The ball made the sun go up and down. One day, Fifi met a new friend. His name was Tommy. Tommy asked Fifi, "What do you do?" Fifi said, "I kick the big red ball. It is an important job." Tommy wanted to help Fifi. So, they played together. They kicked the big red ball up and down, and the sun went up and down too. Fifi and Tommy were very happy. They knew they were doing an important job together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dress up in her mom's clothes. One day, Lily wanted to look successful like her mom. She put on her mom's big hat, long shoes, and pretty dress. Lily felt very happy. But, when she went outside to play, the wind blew her big hat away. Lily was sad. She wanted to find her hat before noon. She looked under the tree, behind the bush, and on the swing. But, she could not find her hat. Just then, her friend Max came to help. Max and Lily looked everywhere. Finally, they found the hat on top of a small hill. Lily and Max climbed up the hill together. They got the hat back just in time for noon. Lily and Max felt successful and happy. They played together all day long.

"Run! Run! Run!" Little Amy shouted, running around the park with her friends. She was chasing the others with an enormous hammer in her hand. Her friends laughed, trying to escape from her. "You can't catch us!" they shouted and started to skip happily. Suddenly, Little Amy tripped over and fell down with a thud. Her hammer flew out of her hands. "Are you ok?" her friends asked, walking towards her. "Will you join us now and skip with us?" Little Amy smiled and replied, "Yes! I'm ready now. Let's skip together!" And so Little Amy and her friends jumped, shouted, ran and skipped in the park, having a wonderful time together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old, and she loved to chew! She had tiny little teeth and would chew on anything she found. One day, she found something that was hard and dull-looking. She thought it might be fun to chew on and so she did. But it was so hard, her teeth couldn’t make a dent! Suddenly, the little girl realized that it was a tooth! It was just like the ones in her mouth, only it was very very old. She ran to show her mom and dad the dull old tooth. Her mom and dad looked at it and told her that it was a dinosaur tooth! They said that dinosaurs had been alive a very long time ago, and now this tooth was all that was left. The little girl was so excited and she put the tooth carefully back in its special spot. Every day she would go and visit the tooth and she would smile, thinking about the time she had chewed it.

One day, a boy named Tom went to play at the park. It was sunny, so he wore his sunglasses. He saw his friend, Sue, and they decided to play catch with a ball. Tom threw the ball to Sue, but it went too high! The ball landed in a wet puddle. Sue got the ball and threw it back to Tom. They both laughed because the ball was wet and made their hands wet too. They played until the sun went down. Tom and Sue said goodbye and went home. Tom put his sunglasses away and thought about the fun day. He couldn't wait to play with Sue again.

Once upon a time, there was a little yellow bird named Sunny. Sunny loved to fly in the wind. One day, while flying, Sunny met a small blue bird named Sky. "Hi, Sky!" said Sunny. "Do you want to have a race?" "Yes!" said Sky, and they began to race through the sky. The wind blew, and they flew fast. As they raced, they saw a baby bird on the ground. It was scared and alone. Sunny and Sky stopped the race and flew down to help. They kept the baby bird safe and warm. Soon, the baby bird's mom came and thanked them. Sunny and Sky learned that helping others is more important than winning a race. They became best friends and flew together in the wind, happy to have each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He was very popular in his town. Everyone liked him because he was always happy and kind. Tim had a big bag of rice that he wanted to share with his friends. One sunny day, Tim met his friend, Sam. Sam was hungry and said, "I need some food, Tim." Tim smiled and said, "I have rice! Let's eat together." They sat under a tree and ate the rice. It was yummy and they felt full. Soon, more friends came to join them. They all needed food too. Tim shared his rice with everyone. They were all very happy and thankful. Tim's rice made him even more popular in the town. From that day on, they all loved sharing and helping each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy had a big, attractive bottle. The bottle was very pretty, with lots of colors. Lucy loved her bottle very much. One day, Lucy's bottle was lost. She looked everywhere for it. Lucy was very sad. She asked her mom and dad to help her find her bottle. They all looked together, but they could not find it. Then, Lucy had an idea. She thought about where she last saw her bottle. Lucy went to her room and found her bottle under her bed. She was so happy that she solved the problem. Lucy, her mom, and her dad all smiled and hugged. Lucy was very happy to have her attractive bottle back.

One day, a little girl and her daddy went to the park. The sun was shining and the birds were singing. The little girl was very happy to play with her daddy. They played a game where they had to guess what the other person was thinking. The little girl was confused because she did not know what her daddy was thinking. She tried to guess, but she could not get it right. Her daddy laughed and said, "It's okay, keep trying!" The little girl kept guessing, but she still could not guess what her daddy was thinking. Then, the sky got dark and it started to rain. The little girl and her daddy got wet and had to go home. They were both very sad because they could not finish their game. The little girl never got to guess what her daddy was thinking, and they went home with a bad ending to their day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was a fair girl with big, bright eyes. Lily loved to dream at night. In her dreams, she would go on big adventures and play with her friends. One day, Lily found a pretty veil. It was soft and light like a cloud. She put the veil on her head and it made her feel like a princess. Lily ran to her mom and said, "Mom, look at me! I am a princess now!" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, Lily, you are a beautiful princess! Let's have a tea party with your friends." So, Lily and her mom invited her friends to their house. They all wore pretty veils and had a fun tea party together. That night, Lily had a dream about her tea party. She dreamed that she and her friends were real princesses in a big castle. They danced and laughed all day long. It was the best dream ever. When Lily woke up, she told her mom about her dream. Her mom hugged her and said, "Dreams are special, Lily. They can take you to magical places." Lily smiled and knew she would always remember her princess dream.

One day, a zebra named Zara was feeling anxious. She did not know why. Zara had many friends, but today she felt alone. She walked slowly, looking for something to do. Zara saw a big tree with a hole in it. She thought, "I will look inside." She looked in the hole and saw a big, shiny stone. Zara was surprised. She did not know what it was. She took the stone out of the hole. Then, a little bird came by. The bird looked at Zara and said, "I know why you feel anxious. You are not alone. That stone is magic. It can make friends for you." Zara was happy. She said, "I will use the stone to make new friends." Zara used the magic stone, and many new friends came to play with her. She was not anxious anymore. She was happy and had fun with her new friends. But then, Zara found out that the bird was the magic stone. The bird was a magic friend too. Zara was even more happy to have a magic bird friend. They all played together and had a great time.

Once upon a time there was a young girl who wanted to go for a drive. She grabbed her ancient dish and went outside to her car. Coming nearer she noticed an old man. She asked him: "Can I drive your car?" The old man smiled and said: "I can't let you drive my car, but I'll show you something better. Follow me." The girl followed the old man to the back yard and saw an ancient car. "This car is over fifty years old", the old man said. The girl was surprised and said: "Can I drive it?" "Of course you can," he replied. The girl was so excited she couldn't believe her luck. She jumped in the car, started the engine and drove away with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a plan. He wanted to clean up all the junk in his room. Tim's mom was not happy with the mess. She felt miserable every time she saw the junk. Tim started to pick up his toys and put them away. But then, he found a big box. Tim did not know what was inside. He opened the box and found a magic wand. Tim was very surprised. Tim waved the magic wand at the junk. All of a sudden, the junk started to dance and sing. The junk cleaned itself up! Tim's mom came into the room and saw the clean room. She was so happy, she was no longer miserable. Tim's plan worked, but in a very unexpected way. And they all lived happily ever after.

Little Jack had a coat. It was a big, thick, blue coat. One day, Little Jack put the coat on and went out for a walk. Outside, it was very cold and windy. Little Jack started to shiver in the cold. He looked at all the buttons on his coat and found one that was missing. That button was very important! Without the button, Little Jack’s coat wouldn’t stay closed. Little Jack needed to find the button! He searched and searched, but it was very difficult. Finally, Little Jack found the missing button hiding on the ground. He was very happy! He quickly put it back onto his coat and it stayed closed tight. Now Little Jack could stop shivering in the cold and go back home to play.

Once upon a time, there was a green bird. The green bird wanted to be a pilot. He loved to fly high in the sky. He had many friends who liked to fly too. One day, the green bird and his friends were flying together. They were having a lot of fun. But then, the green bird flew too fast and bumped into his friend. His friend was sad and hurt. The green bird felt very bad. He said sorry to his friend. His friend was kind and forgave the green bird. They hugged and were happy again. The green bird learned to be more careful when flying with friends. And they all flew happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a happy little boy. He loved to go outside and play. One day, he looked up at the big sky and saw a cloud. It was white and it looked puffy, like a big pillow. The little boy thought it was the most unique thing he had ever seen. He wanted to hold it, so he jumped up and tried to grab it. But the cloud was too high up in the sky and he couldn't reach it. So, the little boy just watched it and wished he could touch it. But then something amazing happened! As the little boy watched, the cloud began to move closer, coming closer and closer! The little boy smiled and, before he knew it, he could reach up and hold the cloud in his hands! He held it tight and felt all of its softness and reminded himself that it was truly very unique. The little boy had a wonderful time holding the cloud and watching it drift away on the wind. He knew he would never forget that day!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy guitar. He loved to play with it every day. One day, Tim felt very tired. He put his guitar down and went to take a nap. While Tim was sleeping, his mother had a surprise for him. She put a big red bow on his guitar. When Tim woke up, he saw the bow and was very happy. He said, "Wow! What a nice surprise!" Tim took his guitar with the bow and played a song for his mother. His mother clapped her hands and said, "Good job, Tim!" Tim smiled and played his guitar all day long. He was not tired anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a big castle. In the castle, there was a grumpy king. The king did not like to play or laugh. One day, a little girl came to the castle. She wanted to be friends with the grumpy king. "Hello, Mr. King," said the little girl. "Do you want to play with me?" "No," said the grumpy king. "I do not like to play." The little girl did not give up. She found a big box of toys and started to play. She played and laughed so much that the grumpy king began to watch her. He saw how much fun she was having and wanted to gain some fun too. The king decided to join the little girl and play with the toys. As they played, the king started to laugh and have fun. The grumpy king was not grumpy anymore! The little girl and the king became best friends, and they played together in the castle every day. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a big, happy dog named Max. Max was very enthusiastic. He loved to play, jump, and run. One day, Max saw a big cake on the table. He was so happy! He wanted to eat the cake all by himself. Max jumped up to get the cake, but he was too small. He tried again and again, but he could not reach it. Max started to shiver because he was sad. He really wanted that cake. He sat down and thought, "How can I get the cake?" Just then, a little bird named Lily flew by the window. Lily saw Max and knew he needed help. She flew inside and pushed the cake off the table. The cake fell on the floor, and Max was so happy! He jumped and licked Lily to say thank you. But then, something unexpected happened. The cake was not a real cake! It was a big, soft pillow that looked like a cake! Max and Lily laughed and laughed. They played with the pillow and had so much fun. They became best friends, and they never felt sad about the cake again.

Once upon a time there was a very brilliant cat. Everywhere she went, people admired her and told her how good-looking she was. But the cat was an unhappy one and she would often complain about how she never found a good place to sleep. One day, the cat saw a thief lurking around the corner. She was about to run away but then she remembered how brave she was. She meowed loudly and the thief ran away. The cat was so relieved she found a safe home in the corner of the garden. From that day she never again complained about where to sleep and she was always happy living in her new home. The end.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with their toys. Tom has a big truck. Mia has a soft cat. One day, they go to the park with their moms. "Look, Tom, there is a slide!" Mia says. She runs to the slide. Tom follows her. He wants to go on the slide too. "Me first!" Tom says. He pushes Mia. Mia falls down. She cries. "Tom, that is not nice!" Mia's mom says. She picks up Mia and rubs her knee. "Are you okay, Mia?" Mia nods. She is sad. She does not want to play with Tom. "Tom, you need to say sorry to Mia," Tom's mom says. She looks at Tom. Tom does not look at her. He does not say anything. "Tom, did you hear me?" Tom's mom says. She taps his ear. Tom shakes his head. He points to his ear. "I can't hear you, Mom. I am deaf," Tom says. He signs with his hands. Tom's mom hugs him. She is sorry. She forgot that Tom can't hear well. She signs with her hands too. "I am sorry, Tom. I love you. You need to be gentle with Mia. She is your friend," she signs. Tom nods. He feels bad. He wants to be a good friend. He signs to Mia. "I am sorry, Mia. I did not mean to hurt you. Can we play together?" he signs. Mia smiles. She is not mad. She signs to Tom. "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. Yes, we can play together. Do you want to share my cat?" she signs. Tom smiles too. He likes Mia's cat. He says thank you. He rubs the cat's fur. The cat purrs. Tom and Mia are happy. They play with the cat and the truck. They take turns on the slide. They listen to their moms. They follow the order. They are good friends.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. It is red and yellow and blue. It has a zigzag shape. Lily and Ben think it is attractive. They want to go on the slide. They rush to the slide. They wait for their turn. Lily goes first. She sits on the slide. She slides down fast. She feels happy. She says, "Whee!" Ben goes next. He sits on the slide. He slides down fast. He feels happy. He says, "Wow!" Lily and Ben go on the slide again and again. They have fun. They laugh and smile. They like the zigzag slide. They think it is the best slide in the park.

Once upon a time, in a quiet little town, winter came. Snow fell and covered the ground. Everyone was happy and played outside. One day, a boy named Tim met a snowman. The snowman could talk! "Hello, Tim!" said the snowman. Tim was surprised but happy to have a new friend. Tim and the snowman played all day. But then, the sun came out. The snowman started to melt. "Oh no!" said Tim. "I don't want you to go away!" The snowman smiled. "Don't worry, Tim. I surrender to the sun. But I will be back next winter, and we can play again." Tim was sad but knew he would see his friend again. He waved goodbye to the snowman and went home. He couldn't wait for the next winter to come.

Sam and Mia were excited to play with their new water balloons. They filled them up with the hose and tied them with strings. They ran to the backyard and threw them at each other, laughing and splashing. But then, Sam noticed that one of his balloons had a leak. He saw a tiny hole where the water was dripping out. He tried to throw it at Mia, but it was too light and fell on the ground. "Hey, what's wrong with your balloon?" Mia asked. "It has a leak. It's no good," Sam said, feeling sad. Mia looked at the balloon and had an idea. She picked it up and ran to the flower bed. She put the balloon near a sunflower and squeezed it gently. The water came out of the hole and watered the flower. "Look, Sam, I changed your balloon into a sprinkler. Now it can help the flower grow," Mia said, smiling. Sam ran to Mia and saw what she did. He smiled too and hugged her. "That's so cool, Mia. You're very smart. Thank you for changing my balloon," Sam said. They played with the other balloons and watered more flowers. They had a lot of fun and made the garden happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big park. In the park, there was a long slide. The slide was black. Many kids liked to play on the slide. One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. He saw the black slide and wanted to play. But the slide seemed too high for him. Tim was scared. His friend, Sam, was there too. Sam said, "Don't be scared, I will help you." Tim and Sam went up the slide together. They held hands and went down the slide. It was fun! They went down the slide many times. Tim was not scared anymore. The moral of the story is that friends can help us when we are scared. With friends, we can be brave and have fun.

Tom and Sue are husband and wife. They love each other very much. They live in a small house with a big garden. They like to grow flowers and vegetables in the garden. One day, Tom finds a mysterious box in the garden. He does not know where it came from. He thinks it might have something nice inside. He wants to open it and see. But he also thinks it might belong to someone else. He does not want to be rude or greedy. He decides to ask Sue what to do. He brings the box to the house and shows it to Sue. Sue is curious about the box too. She thinks it might have something pretty or tasty inside. But she also thinks it might be a gift or a surprise for someone else. She does not want to spoil it or take it. She suggests to Tom that they should wait and see if anyone comes to look for the box. She says they should be honest and kind. Tom agrees with Sue. He thinks she is very smart and good. He puts the box back in the garden and waits with Sue. The next day, a man comes to the garden. He is looking for the box. He says he is a magician and he lost the box when he was doing a trick. He says the box has a magic wand inside. He thanks Tom and Sue for keeping the box safe. He gives them a reward. He shows them how to use the magic wand to make flowers and vegetables grow faster and bigger. He also teaches them some fun tricks to make their friends laugh. Tom and Sue are very happy. They are glad they did not open the box. They learned a lesson. They learned that being honest and kind is better than being rude or greedy. They also learned that being curious and asking questions is good, but respecting other people's things is also important. They hug each other and thank the magician. They enjoy their garden and their magic wand. They love each other very much.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Mia was playing outside on a sunny day. She saw a bright yellow butterfly, and started running and chasing after it. She was racing to catch up with the butterfly, faster and faster. Mia immediately shouted with joy, "Mama! Look, I'm racing!" Her mother smiled and replied, "That looks like so much fun, Mia. Keep running!". Mia just kept running, until the sun got higher and higher and it became noon. "Oh no! It's getting so heavy," Mia said. Suddenly her mother stepped in and said, "Mia, it's time to go inside. Noon is too hot for you to be outside right now." Mia sighed and sadly replied, "Ok, mama. I guess I have to stop racing for now." She put her arms around her mama and the two of them walked inside, hand-in-hand.

One day, a big powerful van was driving down the road. The van was very fast and loud. A little boy named Tim was playing with his ball near the road. He saw the van coming and felt scared. The van stopped near Tim. The driver opened the window and said, "Hi, little boy! I urge you to move away from the road. It is not safe to play here." Tim listened to the driver and moved away. But then, his ball rolled back towards the road. Tim wanted to get his ball, but he remembered what the driver said. He was in a conflict. Tim's mom saw him and came to help. She said, "Tim, I know you want your ball, but remember what the driver said. It's not safe." Tim's mom picked up the ball and they went back to their yard to play. In the end, Tim learned to listen to the advice of others and stay safe. He played happily with his ball in the yard, far away from the powerful van and the dangerous road.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with blocks and dolls. They have many toys in their room. They are happy. One day, a new boy comes to their school. His name is Tom. He is very intelligent. He knows many big words and facts. He likes to read books and do puzzles. He does not like to play with blocks and dolls. Tom sees Anna and Ben playing in their room. He wants to join them. He knocks on the door and says, "Hello, can I play with you?" Anna and Ben look at him. They do not know him. They do not like his big words and facts. They say, "No, you cannot play with us. Go away." Tom is sad. He does not understand why they do not like him. He thinks they are mean. He says, "But I want to play with you. I can teach you many things. I can help you with your blocks and dolls. Please let me play with you." Anna and Ben get angry. They do not want his help. They do not want to learn his things. They want to play by themselves. They say, "No, you cannot play with us. You disturb us. You are not our friend. Go away." Tom is very sad. He feels lonely. He does not have any friends. He goes away. He cries. Anna and Ben see him crying. They feel sorry for him. They think maybe they were too mean. They think maybe he is not so bad. They think maybe they can be his friends. They go to him and say, "We are sorry. We did not mean to hurt you. We were rude. You can play with us. We can share our toys. We can learn from you. You can be our friend." Tom smiles. He is happy. He says, "Thank you. You are very kind. I am sorry too. I did not mean to disturb you. I was curious. You can play with me. I can share my books and puzzles. I can learn from you. You can be my friend." Anna and Ben smile. They are happy. They hug him. They say, "You are welcome. You are very smart. We are curious too. We can play with you. We can have fun. We can be your friend." They go to their room. They play with blocks and dolls and books and puzzles. They talk and laugh and learn. They are friends. They are happy.

One day, a boy named Tim and a girl named Sue went to play by the river. They liked to look for rocks. They found a big, smooth rock. It was the best rock they had ever seen.
